Extensive training in the use of handguns, such as laspistols, bolt pistols, autopistols, stub revolvers, and similar firearms.
When worn, a backpack or sling increases your maximum Encumbrance by 4.
All allies of the Commissar that can see them gain +1 SL to Discipline (Fear) Tests.

If an NPC of the Commissar within Short Range fails a Discipline Test or makes a roll on the Perils of the Warp Table, the Commissar may execute them as a Reaction. As long as the Commissar lives, all allies that can see them automatically pass all Discipline Tests until the end of the Encounter, and the party’s Superiority is reduced by −1.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.NrJuy93Put0XCYq9#melee-(ws)]{Melee}

Extensive training in the use of swords, axes, maces, and other melee weapons that can be used with a single hand.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.NrJuy93Put0XCYq9#medicae-(int)]{Medicae}

Advanced training in treating disease and injuries in Humans. Used for first aid, stabilising the heavily injured, and stopping bleeding. Despite the name, it will work on Abhumans such as Ratlings, Ogryn, and Kin of the Leagues of Votann.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.NrJuy93Put0XCYq9#presence-(wil)]{Presence}

Trained to inspire others to put in their best efforts to achieve a desired goal. This can range anywhere from motivating a few clerks to finish a long survey in record time, to giving a group of desperate soldiers the courage to charge a fortified enemy bunker.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.NrJuy93Put0XCYq9#presence-(wil)]{Presence}

Applying pressure through threats, subtle or blatant, that physical chastisement and other dire fates await those that fail to do as they are told or confess all they know. Intimidation is often opposed by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.rZwUyULrgjBjGlbN]{Discipline (Composure)}. If one party is of a larger @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.zQYkbNcsJmGintdL#size]{Size} than the other, the larger creature gains Advantage on this Test.

notes.player:
Cognomens: Heat Suit, Thermal Suit, Radwear

Across the Imperium, uncountable attempts at planetary colonisation have ended in failure, or the designation of planets as death worlds — planets categorically unsafe for Human habitation. Safety, however, is no object compared to strategic importance or abundance of resources, so death worlds are routinely colonised and exploited, with the typical cost in Human lives proving their moniker. Extreme Weather Clothing is one means to reduce the effects of a typical death world’s casualty rate on production output. These articles of clothing vary as much as the planets they are designed for, all providing limited protection for environments that Humans were never suited to survive.

Extreme Weather Clothing is often defined by local resources, or lack thereof, and resourcefulness which that demands. The tanned hides of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.wHl3ZP7wM7OQvSLC]{Jotungarth’s} sea creatures have been manufactured into cold-weather clothing since they were used to patch the clothing of the first colonists, making adequate defences against freezing sea-mists. On @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}, sets of patched heat-reflection suits have been handed down over generations of workers who manage the geothermal intakes for the volcanic world’s industries.

Extreme Weather Clothing grants the wearer +1 SL on Fortitude (Endurance) Tests made to resist the extreme weather that the clothing is designed to protect against.

text.content: In The Eye of Voll the party is thrust into the caustic wastelands of Voll, planetary region Gamma-74, in search of a powerful rogue psyker, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, who must be stopped at all costs! The cult has recently come into possession of a valuable artefact, one of interest to many factions, that could twist the region’s power balance in the cult’s favour. The Eye of Voll can serve as a stand-alone experience played over 2-3 sessions or as part of a larger campaign. Be sure to familiarise yourself with the various @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP]{Dramatis Personae}, as their interactions and confrontations with the party are key to how this adventure evolves.

Once @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} is defeated and the Eye of Voll acquired by the party or one of the hunting groups, the characters have time for any final dealings to settle their debts with any allies. If they double-crossed their allies at the end, it might mean fighting their way out of @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}.

The death or capture of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} has profound influence on Planetary Region Gamma-74. In the coming weeks riots break out in acid refineries and processing plants. Depending on who is left alive, @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#venykars-sanctifiers]{Venykar’s Sanctifiers} go on a purge, burning the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#the-shrine-of-the-scarred]{Shrine} in the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#c.-the-western-remediation-pools]{Western Remediation Pools} and any other followers of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} they find. @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#heldraxs-stalkers]{Heldrax’s Stalkers} disappear into the darkness. @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost} is the site of a massacre as Imperial forces, aided by @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#echo-team]{Echo Team}, tamp down on lawlessness. Replacement workers from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} are brought in, and the cycle begins again.

Some NPCs the characters encountered could become valuable Contacts or Hirelings in their future adventures, such as @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.n6q9PZhLT9AdBPLp]{Ramm Kragon}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Morgan Trace}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Zenyi Restax}, or any of the hunting groups they allied with.

Experience Points

All characters should earn 30 XP for participating in the adventure. If any characters achieved personal goals or fulfilled a goal for their Patron, their reward should be increased accordingly. In addition, the following experience can be awarded:

  • 10 XP for discovering @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}’s betrayal of the Imperium and bringing him to justice.

  • 10 XP for each ally group gained during the mission, whether they survived or not.

  • 10 XP for each opposing hunting group they personally defeated.

  • 20 XP for killing or capturing @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}.

  • 20 XP for obtaining the Eye of Voll for their Patron.

Influence

Award or reduce the character's Personal Influence according to their behaviour towards the factions they have encountered — primarily the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} of Aserion Outpost or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists} of Gamma-74, but any factions tangential to the opposing Hunting Parties Patrons, the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} (@UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#venykars-sanctifiers]{Venykar’s Sanctifiers}), The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Iaysus Rogue Trader Dynasty} (@UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#heldraxs-stalkers]{Heldrax’s Stalkers}) or the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} (@UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#echo-team]{Echo Team}).

These increases can bleed over to their Patron’s Influences if they represented their Patron honourably or made such a gross error in judgment as to affect their Patron’s standings. Aim to award (or detract) at least one point to each character and their Patron.

Failure

There could be a chance that any of the opposed hunting groups make it to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} and the Eye before the characters or sufficiently repel the party’s advance and claim victory instead. In this case, the characters must lick their wounds and return to the hive with nothing to show for their efforts. This gives you an excellent opportunity to reintroduce this hunting group to a future adventure — becoming a thorn in their side once more or allowing them to thwart their new foe.

If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} is left alive, even if he is forced to go into hiding for some time, his cult has the potential to resurface and grow on Voll. The characters might see Sihn’s cult begin to build power in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokart} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal}.

If the Eye of Voll is not retrieved, the cult eventually bargains it to underhanded members of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} by way of one of Voll’s noble houses. In return, they receive enough protection to allow them a greater chance to expand into one of Voll’s hives.

What’s Next?

The end of this adventure has a few loose ends that could be spun into further adventures for your party. Consider the following:

  • A young, unknown rogue psyker is among the replacement workers brought to Gamma-74. She hears whispers that she can heal the sick and dreams of an unblinking eye, just like Sihn did so long ago. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} may have been dealt with, but the forces behind his powers seek a new puppet to act as their tool.

  • Escorting @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Morgan Trace} back to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} can be expanded into a full-fledged adventure. The noble turned pirate has made many enemies, especially from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#nethecare]{House Nethecaré}, and her marauders are not happy about her abandoning them to face Imperial retribution alone.

  • Wherever the Eye goes, someone wants to get their hands on it. Until someone decides what they want to do with it, and until that project goes into production, all manner of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists} and other factions may try to get their hands on it.

Eventually, the party returns to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost (A)}. They may have learned that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin} is part of the Sihn’s court, and if so, they should confront him. Or they might head into the tunnels beneath the outpost looking for the @UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ#the-enclave-of-sihn]{Enclave of Sihn}.

Confronting Dorin

If the characters involved @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Resta}x in their plans, she warns Dorin of their return, and his office is empty when they arrive. One of the adepts states that Dorin left in a hurry and didn’t say when he would return but that the sub-prefect looked agitated by something. 

If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} is not warned of their return, he is working in his office none the wiser. The party should know now he is a traitor and has been running them around the region to keep them away from the truth. How they wish to deal with Dorin is up to them. The sub-prefect is not a fighter, and while he genuinely believes in Sihn, he will not die for that belief. He tells the characters anything they want to know to secure his safety, but never more than he needs to.

The following information can be learned from Dorin directly or extracted from his cogitators:

  • @UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ#the-enclave-of-sihn]{Sihn’s enclave} is beneath Aserion Outpost. Dorin knows of a tunnel system that leads straight to the heart of it (though he does not offer clues to the entrance’s defences unless pressed).

  • He spills his rhetoric about the overbearing rule of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#nethecare]{House Nethecaré} and the highborn of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} and how he believes that someone like Sihn is needed to destabilise their rule — which may sound like valid justifications to him but, without a doubt, brand him as a heretic. 

  • The Eye of Voll has been moved into @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}’s enclave to protect it and ensure no one can easily steal it. Members of the enclave will put their lives on the line to protect the Eye.

  • Digging deep into his cogitator logs reveals data and logs that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} previously scrubbed to protect Sihn and the court — highly incriminating evidence of his activities that could be used against him later. 

If left alive and able to evade capture, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} does his utmost to flee to Sihn and find safety in the Court and warn the Rogue Psyker that the characters are coming.

In any circumstance, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Zenyi Restax} refuses to die for @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin}; she is far too pragmatic for that and aims to leave the party as soon as possible. Depending on how they treat her, Restax may be counted as a new contact for the characters; useful if they wish to return to the region at a future date.

Into the Tunnels

Finding the Enclave leads the party through the tunnels and underground of @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}. Note to the characters that they have one last chance to prepare before they go below the surface. They should grab anything they need now and contact any allies they wish to accompany them before communications drop off. Any preparations they make, or allies they draw upon should count towards their Superiority in the encounters ahead.

Finding an entrance to the tunnels without @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin}’s directions requires making a Hard (−20) Navigation (Surface or Tracking) Test; failure allows another one of the hunting parties to get a step ahead and wastes the character’s time. Any area within the tunnels can have any of the Dark, Difficult Terrain, Minor Hazard, Obscured, or Poorly Lit Environmental Traits, which you should keep in mind if they enter combat or encounter a challenge. The following encounters happen in the tunnels; the characters can skip to the last encounter if they receive Dorin’s directions:

  1. The characters first encounter an underground camp of outcast @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dregs}. Ask the whole party to make a Hard (−20) Presence (Intimidation) Test. If any character succeeds, the Dregs won’t approach them and allow them to pass. Otherwise, a few of them approach the party, slowing them down, begging for food and solars, and potentially pickpocketing whoever is bringing up the rear.

  2. The characters come upon a length of tunnels filled with toxic gasses leaking from a refinery above (Minor Hazard). Characters must make a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Poison) Test to avoid becoming Poisoned for the next 1d10 Hours. Alternatively, they can use any appropriate equipment to avoid making this Test.

  3. The characters come upon an area strewn with detritus and burrowed holes. The characters can make a Hard (−20) Stealth (Move Silently) Test to move through this area unhindered. Failing the Test, the party is attacked by a pair of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5} , who individually attack the character leading the party and whoever takes up the rear.

  4. The characters find the sonic barriers the cult set up to keep the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }out of their enclave. They can find a way to turn the obstacles off or tough through the area with a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Endurance) Test. Failing this Test causes a character to take 1 Damage, ignoring armour, and become Deafened for the next 1d10 Hours. Alternatively, they can use any appropriate equipment to avoid making this Test.

  5. They find the enclave’s entrance, which is outfitted with an automated @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.vEhnJA0i6WqddsNh]{Heavy Stubber} that the court uses to guard the door. It can only track targets within short range but shoots anything that moves detected by its auspex array. Dealing 15 Damage to it is enough to shut it down unless the characters devise a more creative solution to bypass it. There is a concealed control panel outside its short range that can be accessed to shut it down with the correct password or a Hard (−20) Tech (Security) Test.

Any loud confrontations in the tunnels have a chance to alert the enclave that trouble is on the way, causing them to be ready for any group that arrives.

Allies and Enemies

The characters aren’t limited to the other hunting parties when gathering allies. They could draw upon the loyal forces stationed within @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}, leverage their position with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Morgan Trace} to gain the help of her marauders, or even call in aid from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. Let them use their Influence creatively to gather the necessary forces. The more allies they gain, the more you can draw on enemy forces to pit against them; their opposing hunting parties, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}’s devoted among the wastelanders or rebels from the Processing Plant Gamma-74c15 strike. Aim to create a balance, but always favour the character’s side to ensure they reach the end.

If the characters have not gathered any allies going into the final confrontation, the attack on the court of Sihn should be difficult. At least one other hunting group should be present to fight against their goals.

You should also remember to keep the adventure’s focus on the characters; this is their story. The other hunting parties and forces are there to support or hinder them and add more twists to the final confrontation, not take control of the situation away from them.

The Enclave of Sihn

The Enclave rooms were once underground vaults part of @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}’s industrial outflow system. It consists of three major rooms, interconnected with corridors and smaller cloisters. Sihn’s closest friends and allies live within — the most important members of his cult mingle with mutants whose bodies have been wracked by his corrupting touch. The cult has done its best to block off any other entrances. The @UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ#the-antechamber]{Antechamber} is the true bottleneck of the enclave; once characters have entered, they can find ways into the other rooms besides taking the main hallways, such as hidden passages and navigating through the cloisters at the side — ask the characters to make Difficult (−10) Awareness (Sight), Logic (Investigation), or any other appropriate Tests to uncover these routes.

Besides piles of supply crates that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} has been feeding the cult, every room contains once-ornate furniture, faded throw pillows, and cracked glassware, all signs of an attempt to sophisticate the enclave. They also provide ample Light or Medium Cover in a fight. Filtration systems provide a constant hum and strange heady incense burns in every chamber. No matter how deep the enclave is, it is still subject to a light coating of grime and stench drawn from the surface. Any larger surface is painted with murals, most depicting a radiant @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} in one stance or another, lording over citizens of the wastes kneeling in supplication and pleading for aid.

The Antechamber

The entrance to the nave looks more like a communal living area than a place of reverence. The cult created an inner barricade using the furniture and crates they had on hand. It provides Medium Cover, but sections of it can be destroyed by dealing 10 Damage to it. If the cult senses they are losing, they’ll break off and retreat into the Nave.

Initially, the whole court is gathered here, ready to lay down their lives to protect @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} and their fellow cultists. Playing for peace might be an option to supplicate some of the regular cultists. They might lay down their arms in the face of overwhelming odds, favourable bargaining, or reasoning, but Sihn and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultists} know their true fate — facing execution for heresy — and fights anyone to the bitter end.

The Nave

This is the cult’s main chamber of worship. It is littered with twisted effigies of the God-Emperor and other works of art, including aspects of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}’s iconography. Makeshift pews provide ample Light Cover across the centre of the room. Most of the cultists are gathered at the opposite end of the room, next to an altar that provides Heavy Cover but not enough room for them all to hide behind. Three improvident chandeliers hang from the ceiling; minor damage to their hangings would cause them to fall to the pews below. Characters hit by these chandeliers take 5 Damage and are knocked Prone, and also cause the room to become Poorly Lit (both the characters and the opposing NPCs can take advantage of this feature).

Like the Antechamber, the cult retreats into the Sanctuary if they feel like they’re losing — @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.CQH3R36NIhE0JyQ9]{Corbid} attempts to lead them.

The Sanctuary

Once a place of quiet contemplation, the court’s Sanctuary now hosts the Eye of Voll, pride of place in the centre of the room. The use of any explosives in this encounter, especially if any Tests Fumble, could risk damaging the Eye; ensure that an NPC calls this out shortly after entering the room. The court took their time moving the Eye into this room — it would be impossible to snatch and grab.

During the fight, characters can make a Difficult (−10) Awareness (Sight) Test to spot some desperate cultists at the rear of the chamber removing panels and fixings from the wall — they are attempting to uncover an old exit point that leads back into the tunnels, but it takes them several rounds to do so. 

The Final Confrontation

See the @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#the-court-of-sihn]{Court of Sihn} composition; note that his handful of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultists} should be spread out between the main rooms. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} begins in the Antechamber with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.CQH3R36NIhE0JyQ9]{Adriana Corbid}, initially believing he can stay the hand of the party or other hunting groups about to attack the enclave. During the fight, he aims to retreat from room to room until he’s backed into a corner in the @UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ#the-sanctuary]{Sanctuary}.

The Court’s behaviour during the fight is as follows:

  • At all times, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} keeps his distance from the fight, with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.CQH3R36NIhE0JyQ9]{Corbid} supporting him. He’ll attempt to heal any of his forces who retreat to him, especially Adriana if she is hurt.

  • His @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultists} rush the intruders while his @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ppicZvgr0bEuhWeh]{Cultists} take cover and try to engage at range.

  • If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} dies, the group immediately becomes @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.3j1kargHBeCTssE7#resolve]{Desperate}.

  • If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} uses any Psychic Powers that would cause any significant collateral damage, or he causes any Warp Phenomena or Perils of the Warp, this can shake the enclave’s foundations, causing objects to fall over and debris to fall from the ceiling, turning appropriate Zones into Minor or Major Hazards.

With the lay of the land and the gathering of NPCs, both allies and enemies, you should have everything you need. As always, let your characters lead the way, throw plentiful obstacles in their direction, and see how they best deal with it. They will devise creative solutions that are not accounted for, so do your best to adapt and bring the adventure to a satisfying conclusion.

Many characters are present in Voll’s Gamma-74 region, and many are on the hunt for @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} and the Eye of Voll. Some are potential hunting allies to the characters, while others would lay down their lives to protect Sihn and his interests or otherwise remain neutral until encountered.

The Court of Sihn

The Court is the name given by Markis Sihn to the group that surrounds him. While some claim that he is a boon to the area, helping those that live in these blighted lands survive to see another muted sunrise, others proclaim him a heretic, a withc damned by the Warp. The rank-and-file members of Sihn’s Court are @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ppicZvgr0bEuhWeh]{Cultists} with a few @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultists} among them that Sihn keeps hidden away in his enclave. Some of them bear Sihn’s Mark, which functions as a Mark of Tzeentch.

  • Mark of Tzeentch: +10 Intelligence and Willpower. These increases improve Initiative and Wounds by +1.

Markis Sihn

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

The Daemon Behind The Curtain

A foul Warp entity, a daemon of Tzeentch, noticed Sihn and his capabilities when he was young. The daemon infiltrated his dreams, instilling visions of grandeur, and later, it did the same to his partner and lover, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.CQH3R36NIhE0JyQ9]{Adriana Corbid}. The Hunter Teams

The three teams of hunters presented here — Heldrax’s Stalkers, Echo Team and Venykar’s Sanctifiers — are each assigned specific patrons. However, you can swap these Patrons out for others the characters might have encountered on their previous adventures if their goals or oppositions align better.

These hunting teams can become allies or enemies throughout the adventure, depending on the treatment they receive from the characters. You do not need to use all three teams if you wish to shorten or simplify the adventure. Each team has a leader, a second in command, and a generic squad member to make up the rank and file. The total number of team members (including their Leader and Elite second in command) should be close to the number of player characters, plus one or two more Troops. You can raise or lower their squad size to better balance against the party, including adding reinforcements between encounters.

The players now choose where to investigate. The characters travel across the Voll wasteland, moving from location to location and potentially finding clues that can lead them to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}. They can begin their investigations at @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#b.-processing-plant-gamma-74c15]{Processing Plant Gamma-74c15} (B), the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#c.-the-western-remediation-pools]{Western Remediation Pools} (C), or @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#d.-survey-crawler-b38649]{Survey Crawler B38649} (D). Through investigating these sites, the characters can learn about the existence of @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask} (E)  and the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#f.-the-float]{Float} (F). In those former locations, the characters can discover their most valuable clues: the location of Sihn’s enclave and the fact that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin} is a member of the Sihn’s court. Their explorations lead them back to the adventure’s finale (@UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ]{Part 3: Hidden Beneath}) at @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost} (A).

Planetary Region Gamma-74

This planetary region of Voll is composed of several hundred material mines and processing plants. Apart from specks of life, the entire area is an acidic wasteland hostile to most life forms. As they travel, the characters spot acid-washed imperial machinery, small clusters of wastelander habs bolted onto industrial facilities, and much cast-off waste and foul sludge created by the region’s manufactorums and extraction processes.

Characters should ensure they are well-protected from the elements. Remember to introduce harsh weather conditions as they traverse the region to evoke the planet’s atmosphere — horizontal winds, heavy rainfall, and lightning-threatening skies. They might even spot a wild herd of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }swimming or digging just below the terrain’s surface.

The Other Hunters

While investigating the wastes, add some encounters between the party and the other three hunter groups. This is an opportunity to add extra complications to the hunt, rescue the characters from certain peril, or allow the characters to make more allies or enemies.

If a fight goes poorly at the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#c.-the-western-remediation-pools]{Western Remediation Pools} (C) or breaks out at @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask} (E) or @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#f.-the-float]{The Float} (F), having an allied hunting group ready to aid the party might prove useful to their survival and keeping the adventure moving. If however, the party is rude, overbearing, or downright hostile towards any of the other hunting parties, that hunting party might find an ally with another group. 

Assuming the characters met one hunting party before departing the hive and another at @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}, they should meet the final group at @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask} (E). The adventure is structured this way, but you should feel free to rearrange the groups to different locations.

Remember, everyone is after the same prize, and the characters should know this — it is often each group’s methodology and beliefs that can ally or stand at odds. Additionally, if the party is stuck, introducing another hunting group that has or can uncover key information can get the adventure back on track. The encounter then becomes a question of how the characters get this information from the hunting group — they could spy on or follow the other hunting party to the next clue, or find a way to barter or extract this information from them.

A. Aserion Outpost

Central to the wastelands of Sub Sector Gamma-74 stands Aserion Outpost, the thriving heart of the Imperium’s industry within the region. It comprises several hundred hab buildings, massive vehicle bays, launch pads, and various administration buildings to support the region’s operations, all encompassed by bastion walls and watchtowers. Cargo haulers arrive from the wasteland at all hours of the day on a web of shifting dirt and acidlogged roads that reach outward from the outpost. Upon arrival, their contents are catalogued and repackaged, and cargo flyers arrive from Voll’s hives to transport them to other manufactorums for further processing, grading, testing, and final refinements before being shipped off-world.

The acid-washed outpost is home to several thousand @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial Citizens} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers} and is rapidly running out of room for more. It is common for these workers to wear goggles and rebreathers or scarves to keep the worst of waste’s atmosphere and industrial runoff at bay. Inside the habs, things are not much better, but the people of the outpost are used to it and hardly notice.

Coming Full Circle

The adventure eventually brings the characters back to Aserion Outpost to confront @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} and his cult, hiding deep in the industrial tunnels below the outpost. Do your best to limit their investigation in the outpost; all the NPCs, rumours, and clues they’ve found so far should be pointing their fingers elsewhere. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin} has a vested interest in getting the characters out of the way; he intervenes if they linger too long, pushing them towards @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#b.-processing-plant-gamma-74c15]{Processing Plant Gamma-74c15} (B), citing that the situation is rapidly deteriorating.

The Tunnels Below

The tunnels beneath the outpost are a veritable labyrinth, and getting lost is a genuine concern if you don't know how to get around. These tunnels predate the outpost to when it was first prospected as a crystal mine. Supports and massive refinery mechanisms now keep everything from collapsing in on itself. The tunnels are rarely discussed among the topside citizens, as it is generally accepted that they are too dangerous to be used for anything. 

The Aserion Outpost underground is also infested with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, Voll’s native tardigrade-like vermin. These primarily consist of the easily farmable @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.7F9x6CZCJCp0IV6b]{Acynadi Beta-3}’s found all across the wastes and the occasional canid-sized @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5}. The Court doesn’t bother with them,  knowing that rumours of the more dangerous Delta-5’s living in the tunnels should keep others away. The cultists have set up ultrasonic barriers to keep the acynadi away from their enclave, which seems to have worked so far.

Besides the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, a few others dwell in the tunnels: outcast @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dregs} from the outpost who live off the discarded trash, acynadi meat, and detritus from the outpost above. These few tunnel dwellers are easily intimidated or coerced and can be convinced to lead the party around. 

Hidden deep beneath the outpost is the @UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ#the-enclave-of-sihn]{Enclave of Sihn}. Members of his court have infiltrated the outpost command for some time now and are doing everything they can to hide @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} and their activities. But with burgeoning numbers and desperate citizens coming to Aserion Outpost to seek their leader’s aid, the cult’s activities are becoming harder to hide. Additional information about these tunnels can be found in @UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ]{Part 3: Hidden Beneath}, when the characters return after exploring beyond the Outpost’s walls.

B. Processing Plant Gamma-74c15

Processing plants on Voll take the raw harvested chemical precursors obtained by extraction rigs and process them into various medicae reagents. They extract these through physical straining and chemical processes, refining the acidic soil and waters into dust and toxic sludge. These dusts are often ejected from large stacks that spray the particulates high into the atmosphere, and the sludge is dumped through a network of leaking pipelines into one of the world’s many remediation pools. 

Currently, Processing Plant Gamma-74c15 is operating far below acceptable efficiency. Some workers have explicitly gone on strike, and rumours swirl that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} is somehow involved. A cadre of conspiratorial @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers} and their leader, another labourer named Lhax Barro, have barricaded themselves in the manufactorum’s gas storage depot. Threatening to overload the tanks, filled with highly volatile gas, they seek to press their agenda — better working conditions, additional prayer breaks, and more rations for everyone in the manufactorum.

Official Missive Aserion-234EDX

Workers of Processing Plant Gamma-74c15,

We have heard your demands and processed them. By official decree of the office of the subprefect of Planetary Region Gamma-74, your demands amount to treason, endangering the planetary tithe and besmirching the name of the God-Emperor.

In reparation for your insubordination, your nutritional supplements will be reduced across the manufactorum until efficiency is restored to an acceptable level.

You will immediately abandon your strike action and return to your assigned shifts or face execution.

Sub-prefect Rastigan Dorin, of Planetary Region Gamma-74. 

In truth, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} has nothing to do with the work stoppage and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} intends to use the characters to do his dirty work for him. He wants them to end the strike and bear the brunt of the workers’ ire, perhaps even injuring them so badly they’ll stop searching for Sihn. Dorin has provided the party with the following official missive from his regional sub-prefect's office. It is sealed and should be handed directly to whoever is responsible for the strike (though a simple wax seal may not deter some characters’ curiosities, if they read it beforehand, they might have a better idea about what they’re walking into).

However, a third element is in play at the Processing Plant. Not to be outdone in their duty, the plant’s @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.wzB86nJHHIRHMQTO]{Overseers}, led by Overseer Ingria Llon, have a bloody plan to defuse the situation and get everything back on track. They know if they go in guns blazing, they’ll likely set off the tanks and cause an explosion that could damage the manufactorum. So, they are slowly and safely draining the gas tanks without the labourers knowing via a nearby fuelling junction. Once the tanks are sufficiently empty, Ingria's overseers will assault the striker’s position, aiming to take no prisoners. They believe a lethal show of force will spur the rest of the workforce back to peak efficiency. The only kink in her plan is that draining the tanks will take another day or so.

From here, it’s up to the characters to defuse the situation best while also gathering information about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}'s whereabouts.

How Did We Get Here?

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin} gave the characters the location of the manufactorum. He wants the plant’s production back on track and thinks the characters are the perfectly blunt instruments to do it for him. Alternatively, they might have heard about the work stoppage from rumours in the hive or around Aserion Outpost.

Arriving at the Plant

The characters are greeted by Overseer Llon when they arrive at Processing Plant Gamma-74c15, accompanied by a pair of fellow overseers. She was forewarned of their arrival by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin} and doesn’t seem too happy to see the characters meddling in the manufactorum’s affairs. However, she recognises their authority and secretly hopes they’ll provide ample distraction until her own plan comes to fruition.

She escorts them into the Manufactorum, into one of the control rooms, and gives them the lay of the land — Lhax Barro, the other strikers, their position in the gas storage depot, and the ins and outs of her plan (of which she is exceedingly proud of concocting).

If they have been amicable with Overseer Llon so far, she provides them with an additional asset. A day ago, they captured one of the strikers who attempted to sneak away and retrieve more food. Jaqe Idian, another labourer known to be Lhax Barro’s cousin. She has been thoroughly interrogated and is locked up in a nearby brig, though Llox hasn’t been able to get anything useful out of her. How the characters use her is up to them.

If the characters speak to Jaqe Idian, they notice that she has suffered dramatically from the interrogation, but has just enough energy to talk to them. She fears execution for joining the strike, but she truly knows very little about the strikers’ plans other than what has been obvious so far — they will attempt to blow up the gas tanks as a last resort. She believed in her cousin, perhaps too much, and foolishly accompanied him.

If the party asks Jaqe about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, she relays that he once helped Lhax get over an illness that Sihn was sure he suffered from due to his work in the processing plant. This spurred her cousin to seek better conditions, resulting in the strike. She also mentions that Lhax knows precisely where the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#the-shrine-of-the-scarred]{Shrine of the Scarred} is in the Western Remediation Pools (C), because he visits it often.

If they ask Overseer Llon about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, she tells them the following information: As far as she knows, no one named Markis Sihn has ever visited or worked in this manufactorum, so she doesn’t know why the labourers are getting all worked up. She also relays that some workers are spreading rumours that Markis Sihn was involved in the attack on Survey Crawler B38649 (D). She knows that the crawler had reported the discovery of a sizable rough gemstone within a massive @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }carcass found on its latest survey, and that someone stole it from the crew.

After Llon’s briefing and potentially meeting Jaqe Idian, the overseer leads them to the gas storage depot to deliver their missive to the strikers.

Confronting the Strikers

Before Overseer Llon allows the party into the gas storage depot, she asks them to relinquish any firearms or explosives they might have on them — she doesn’t trust anyone with a firearm in the gas storage depot, not even her fellow overseers (they will be returned when the characters leave the depot). Unless the characters can convince Llon otherwise, she refuses to give them any additional overseers to aid them in the encounter, she also stays behind. 

The gas storage depot is a dense cluster of tanks and pipework off to the western edge of the manufactorum. Many of the pipes and fixings have garnered deep layers of rust due to the acidic atmosphere, and the concrete flooring is covered in puddles of potentially flammable effluent. A constant hissing noise envelops the depot, the sound of compression tanks working and small leaks sprouting elsewhere.

The area is Poorly Lit and strewn with Minor Hazards that would ignite if exposed to a spark or naked flame. Clusters of pipework provide Light Cover, and five massive gas tanks in the centre of the depot are Features that can erupt into Major Hazards if dealt 10 Damage at once with a firearm or weapon that could cause a spark. Take note: the real danger isn’t the initial explosion but the cascade of heightened pressure and flammable gas that could travel through the wider manufactorum, causing damage that would take years to repair. 

The labourers have built makeshift barricades around the base of the gas tanks to provide them with Medium Cover and obscure what they’re doing. As the characters approach, Lhax Barro emerges to meet them, arms raised to show everyone he is unarmed. He is initially pleased that the authorities have taken him seriously enough to send an envoy, but his demeanour may sour quickly depending on the party’s next actions.

If the characters hand Lhax the missive from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin}, he breaks the seal and unfurls the message. He reads it aloud so that everyone can hear what it says. He becomes visibly distraught with every paragraph, and by the end, he is livid, and his fellow strikers become riled up by the disrespect they’ve received.

The characters have three attempts to make a Difficult (−10) Extended Test requiring 6 total SL to resolve the situation before the strikers take drastic action. Any failed Test they make increases the Difficulty of the next Test by one step. Consider the following options and situations:

  • The characters could make a Rapport (Charm or Deception) Test to assure them that Dorin’s orders are their best option, or at least the only option to walk away with their lives intact.

  • They could make a Rapport (Haggle) Test to negotiate beyond Dorin’s orders, but anything they bargain would later be on their heads to provide.

  • They could even attempt a Presence (Intimidation) Test, wielding their authority to break the labourers’ collective will and get them back to work.

  • If Jaqe Idian is present, increase or decrease the Difficulty of any social Tests they make with the strikers by one step, depending on how the characters have treated her. Easier if they treated her well or brought her back to Lhax, or more difficult if, for example, they attempted to use her as a human shield.

  • If an overseer is present, increase the Difficulty of any social Tests they make with the strikers by one step.

If they have not succeeded after three Tests, Lhax believes that the overseers will execute them no matter the outcome, and immediately flees towards the gas tank cluster. He shouts to his fellow strikers to ignite the tanks and to run for their lives.

Strike Outcomes

Potentially, the best outcome involves the strikers accepting @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin}’s orders and peacefully returning to work. The characters could have made extra assurances to obtain this outcome — they may have invoked their Influence or their Patron’s authority to meet some of the striker’s demands. Any promises they make, be sure to wrap them up at the end of the adventure, and show the characters the consequences of their actions.

At worst, the strikers have exhausted their patience and take drastic action. Some attempt to ignite the gas tanks and cause damage to the manufactorum, while others attack the party in order to gain swift revenge. Any survivors will aim to escape the manufactorum, but fleeing the depot, most of them will surely be caught by the overseers and executed. (Characters may encounter a few survivors at the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#c.-the-western-remediation-pools]{Western Remediation Pools (C)} or @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask (E)} later in the adventure.)

Depending on their faction or their Patron’s orders, the characters may wish to side with the manufactorum overseers. They could go along with Overseer Llon’s plan, though waiting another day would certainly allow the other hunter teams to get ahead of the party. A Tech-Priest in the party may be able to use their Tech (Engineering) skill to speed up the process of draining the tanks, find another chemical to make the gas inert, or expel the gas into the surrounding Remediation Pools. Any of these actions requires a Hard (−20) Tech (Engineering) Test, but threatens repercussions, even a loss in Influence, for wasting so many Imperial resources. Additionally, failure causes the strikers to notice their efforts, making them more challenging to negotiate with (raising the Difficulty of Tests against them by two steps) and warning them of the upcoming assault.

If they ask Lhax or the other strikers about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} — either through interrogation or amicable conversation — their eyes light up in reverence, and they relay the following information:

  • They know that Sihn travels all over the region — he comes and goes, wandering the wasteland to help those in need.

  • Many of the strikers owe Markis Sihn their lives. They believe he alone cares about the workers of region Gamma-74, and if they held out long enough, he would come to take over the processing plant and liberate them.

  • Lhax mentions the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#the-shrine-of-the-scarred]{Shrine of the Scarred} at the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#c.-the-western-remediation-pools]{Western Remediation Pools (C)} and can provide directions, claiming they saw Sihn preaching and healing people there some time ago. Depending on the encounter’s outcome, he might escort them there himself.

Remember, your players are smart and may come up with their own solutions — be sure to play into their plans, if they are reasonable. What’s important is that they gather the necessary clues to continue their hunt for Sihn and generate some fallout around their actions that should come back to haunt them later. Also, if they are significantly injured or otherwise waylaid by fallout surrounding events at the Processing Plant, other hunting parties could get ahead of them.

Where to Go From Here?

From here, the characters should have learned about the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#the-shrine-of-the-scarred]{Shrine of the Scarre}d at the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#c.-the-western-remediation-pools]{Western Remediation Pools (C)} via the Manufactorum Labourers, or @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#d.-survey-crawler-b38649]{Survey Crawler B38649’s (D)} attack site via Overseer Ingria Llon.

C. The Western Remediation Pools

The remediation pools of the region contain the toxic sludge that is a byproduct of the acidic refinement processes. On good days, thin bands of sunlight cut through the dark clouds, drying out the sludge. Workers walk on stilts through the muck, stirring up pockets of mud to the top for drying with large rakes, meanwhile gathering any crystal fragments that slipped through manufactorum processing. Many say that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} established his beginnings here, trading for crystals he could then funnel back through @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}. It was here that Sihn first used his powers to aid the region’s workers, healing their acid burns and the hacking sickness that pervades the wastes.

As a result, the workers of the Western Remediation Pools built a shrine to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}, and they expressed their praise and gratitude for his aid. Seen as an unsanctioned saint, this was the beginning of Sihn’s cult of personality. The shrine has grown over the years since Sihn came to power, still standing on a rocky outcrop in the middle of a sludge flat. It is of little concern to most, a point of refuge to those among the pools and of significant meaning to Sihn’s followers.

How Did We Get Here?

The players were likely given the location of the pools by workers at @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#b.-processing-plant-gamma-74c15]{Processing Plant Gamma-74c15 (B)} or were told of the Shrine by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}. Dorin knows the Shrine has little to do with the Sihn’s actual operations and hopes that sending the characters here is at worst harmless at best might see them eaten by the wildlife.

The Pools

The remediation pools are large lakes of shallow sludge. Uneven shifting pools of chemicals and black tar-like substances, covered in a thin top layer of oily runoff that reflects a sickly chromatic sheen. The whole place reeks of chemical by-products, leaving a smoky, ashen taste in the air. Most workers use @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.16DWBUHaqigUg0ZT]{rebreathers} or wraps of scented clothes to protect their olfactory senses. Regardless of what they do, this stench is pervasive; just being near the pools is enough to infest a person’s clothes with the fetor and is nigh impossible to remove. Among the pools stand discarded poles and stilts, erected as markers or to hang a glowglobe from or show the direction of the wind.

Among the pools, stilt walkers wander about, taking careful steps upon their rigs. Jutting from their backs are long poles and extra sets of stilts they keep on hand in case one set breaks or they need to mark a position in the pools. They know they are not the only inhabitants of the pools. Some are hunting the small farmable @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, but they know that more raptorial strains (@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5}) that track and react to heavy sloshing in the pools, can jump out at them. 

When the characters first arrive at the pool’s outskirts, a stilt walker hails and approaches them at a careful trudge. She offers the warnings above and asks them not to drive their @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8} across the setting pools and to stick to the surrounding (though rickety) single-file walkways. Even a vehicle such as a Cargo-8, used to off-road traversal, is likely to get stuck in the mud and attract the attention of hostile @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}.

The characters can ignore these warnings and drive right through, but they would immediately lose the respect and hospitality of the workers. Consider having the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8} get stranded in the mud or encounter some @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5} when they’re stranded or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Restax} stops to check her directions. Without directions, it takes the party several hours to locate the isle.

Their goal should be to interview the stilt walkers to learn more about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} and the local shrine. Most workers they interview can tell that the characters are outsiders and say they know nothing about Sihn, despite many making regular offerings of crystalline shards or rough gems they find to the shrine. Some have terrible rasping coughs, bursting out in hacking fits even beneath sealed rebreathers. While others are comparatively healthy, these are the workers whom Sihn has healed with his powers.

The characters can more easily obtain information from the sickest workers. They can make a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Deception or Inquiry) Test to extract the necessary information, or they could consider bribery or more forceful methods. Approaching any healed workers increases the Difficulty of these Tests to Very Hard (−30). 

The Shrine of the Scarred

If they receive directions from the locals, they can find the shrine within two hours of arriving at the Western Remediation Pools. Without directions, that time is doubled, and another hunting party may be able to get ahead of them.

The shrine dedicated to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} is a large repurposed hab unit that sits centrally on the island. It is surrounded on every side by smaller shrines and markers dedicated to the local lost and dead — fashioned out of discarded machinery and scrap parts, all in some mockery of a traditional Imperial shrine.

A wall of half-buried cargo containers and machinery surrounds the island's perimeter, which some locals use for storage or makeshift lean-tos. Only a single sloping beach leads from the sludge up to the shrine entrance. A simple gate made from lashed-together stilts bars the way, but it provides no real security and could be easily forced open.

A few @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.5fAQrj0KDjAXkHRY]{Devout} tend to the site. They are not official members of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} (but recognise Influence the characters might bear in the ecclesiarchy’s name). They are former stilt-walkers who have had the rare privilege of surviving working the remediation pools but now too old to mount their stilts. Some have mounted their old stilts on their backs or use them as makeshift crutches. 

They’ve affixed dangling pieces of broken crystal and metal across their unofficial vestments, which tinkle and chime in the wind, much like those hanging from the shrines spread out around them. Characters can make a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test to notice that among their various scars and Imperial cult tattoos, each also sports the Mark of Sihn, the splayed hand with a central eye in the palm. These devout praise the God-Emperor and Sihn equally, preaching about their experiences with him — that they would have never lived long enough to serve the shrine if it were not for Sihn’s healing powers.

Inside the Shrine

The shrine’s doors are repurposed hauler hatches that both open to reveal a surprisingly clean interior. Across every surface, scraps have been welded into gaps to prevent the unit from leaking. Sickly grey candles made from recycled castings shed minimal light and far more smoke, adding to the acrid smell drawn in from the environment outside. A mishmash of statues stand among the throngs of candles; their grotesque faces look more misshapen and hideous than reverent.

The head priest of the shrine, Loris Gant (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.9kYI2Oshwn0wqWUo]{Ministorum Priest} stat-block to represent him), is in the middle of his daily canticles. His words are slightly modified Imperial prayers, scattering in mention of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} as a holy messenger of the God-Emperor himself. He looks much like the shrine priests outside, except his eyes are missing, and the acid-burned sockets are tattooed with Sihn’s palm-like insignia. He knows the shrine intimately and moves among the burning candles as if he can see them, lighting ones that have gone out or replacing ones that burned away. 

Loris tells the group anything they want to know about Sihn and is eager to proffer his beliefs. Here is what he knows (or rather, believes): 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} is a blessing afforded by the God-Emperor, and Loris does not understand any of the more nefarious rumours being spread about Sihn’s powers — that some of them have disappeared (new rumour) or that Sihn might be a xenos in disguise (old rumour).

  • He never knows when @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} will visit. Sihn used to pray at the shrine every day, but he is so busy using his gifts that he rarely visits these days. It would be no use for the characters to wait for Sihn to arrive (he won’t).

  • If the party arrived in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Restax}’s @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8}, Loris mentions that the last time @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} visited, he arrived in a truck much like the one they came in. He could tell by the minute sounds made by the engine; in fact, he thought they might have been Sihn paying a visit. (This is a hint that Restax has transported Sihn in the past, which would be the truth).

Loris has heard of the trouble at the processing plant and the attack on the survey crawler, but believes these things are unrelated to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}, despite what rumours say (if the characters have yet to visit either of these locations, then Loris mentions them). If the characters haven’t yet been pointed towards @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask (E)}, Loris mentions that many people in the wastes visit the Flask often, especially those who cannot set foot in @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}. Several of the local stilt-walkers visit there now and then, and the patron, Kragon, seems to know a bit about everything that’s going on in the region.

Heresy!

After hearing Loris’s prayers and learning more about Sihn, some characters may consider the Shrine of the Scarred inhabitants to be heretics and worthy of being purged in the name of the God-Emperor. Evidence the party gathers later about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} would prove this true. Don’t hold back from letting the players deal with the shrine however they wish, or dealing with it in a manner their Patron would deem fit. But if anything happens to Loris or the other devout, Markis Sihn is likely to learn about it before the characters return to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}, and learn about the characters before they confront him directly.

Where to Go From Here?

From here, the characters have learned about either the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#d.-survey-crawler-b38649]{Survey Crawler B38649’s (D)} attack site or are pointed towards @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#b.-processing-plant-gamma-74c15]{Processing Plant Gamma-74c15 (B)}. If they have been to both places already, Loris points them towards @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask (E)} instead.

D. Survey Crawler B38649

Survey Crawler B38649 is a massive array of mobile machinery that once plodded across Voll’s wastelands. It’s the sort of machine that would look at home among the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleet}, a massive multi-legged walking platform, outfitted with digging implements, scanning equipment and cargo space. Its job is to prospect key locations, sift dunes to the side, and bore test holes into the ground, all looking for suitable ground to extract mineral-rich or distinctly acidic soil. Once a plot of land is deemed viable for full extraction operations, permanent machinery is brought in, and the crawler moves on. 

A week ago, Crawler B38649 was attacked. During its prospecting operations, it extracted a single large uncut gem from the ground, thought to have come from the carcass of a massive and long-dead @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}. Word was sent to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}, marking the land’s unviability but noting the gemstone’s discovery. The crawler retrieved the gemstone and moved on towards its following test site but was attacked en route by marauders, and the stone in its cargo was stolen. 

How Did We Get Here?

The players may have heard of the attack site from rumours at the hive, from a reluctant @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}, from the workers at @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#b.-processing-plant-gamma-74c15]{Processing Plant Gamma-74c15 (B)}, or from the shrine Priest Loris at the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#the-shrine-of-the-scarred]{Shrine of Markis Sihn}.

Crawler Exterior

Currently, most of the crawler’s legs are broken; the remaining legs are being dug out and extracted by groups of scavengers. The body sits at an odd angle due to its remains sinking into the acidlogged landscape. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin} is covering up the loss of this crawler — while he knew of the attack, he expected the marauders to take the Eye of Voll and leave the crawler more or less intact to continue its work, not bring its whole operation to a halt. 

Atop the wreckage, scavengers pick over the crawler’s bones (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dregs} stat-block to represent them). Several makeshift tents and a couple of old haulers and walkers are parked in the shadow of the crawler, gradually piling up with the best pieces the scavengers can rip from the bones.

The gang of scavengers is not hostile, but they are territorial. They will not give up their salvage willingly. Their Resolve is 1 if encountered outside their camp (moving to and from or within the crawler) but 3 if encountered in their adjacent camp. Most of the extraction equipment and valuable parts of the crawler have already been salvaged. 

If a character talks to any scavengers and mentions @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, the scavenger in question appears reverent of him and sing his praises. The scavengers tell the party what they know happened with little coercion; a small trade or gift of solars would work — they know that marauders attacked the crawler and killed the crew, and left the wreckage to sink into the wastes (which they expect may happen over the next few weeks). Some scavengers saw them make off with a large piece of cargo — it took a long time for them to move it out of cargo storage and onto their largest hauler. They do not know where the marauders went or where they might be based, but they headed toward @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask (E)}.

Crawler Interior

The scavengers have picked over the crawler's insides. Most supplies and anything not bolted down is already gone. Still, some pieces of Imperial industrial gear can be found among the wreckage (Common Availability items at best, with the Shoddy item flaw). There are three stocky decks, and only a few internal walls and deck treads between them. Most of the space is taken up by stretches and twists of dense pipework and machinery, and apart from the bridge and a few compartments, every space is Poorly Lit and claustrophobic.

A lone scavenger is hacking away at the cogitator and control units on the crawler’s command deck. He’ll weakly brandish a knife in the character’s direction, saying he has a fair claim on the command deck’s contents. How the characters deal with this scavenger is up to them, but the man is a pushover when outnumbered. Any Tech-Priests among the party may feel like they should protect the integrity of the cogitators from this man, or any adepts may wish to reinforce the truth that the crawler as a whole is still the property of the Imperium.

Regardless, some of the cogitators are still active. Characters can make a Challenging (+0) Tech (Security) Test to glean the following information from its databanks (consider awarding one piece of information for each SL achieved on the test, so long as the characters have enough clues to proceed with their investigation):

  • Communication logs from the crawler captain back to sub-prefect @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} detail how the massive gemstone was discovered, pulled up from the wastes, and wrapped around the carcass of a long-dead @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }(this information may be helpful to anyone researching aspects of the acynadi).

  • Early investigation of the Eye of Voll and its general size, shape, properties, and other general notes via the crew’s Tech-Priest (a heavy hauler would be needed to transport it, not many of them in the area).

  • Logs state that the marauders came from the northeast (direction of @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask (E)}).

  • Vox logs show that the crawler signalled for aid to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost} several times, noticing the marauders circling the crawler for at least a day before the attack. They received no orders other than to continue on their planned prospecting route.

Where to Go From Here?

The players should have learned of the Flask from the scavengers and the marauder’s existence. The proprietor of @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask (E)} might know where the marauders went.

E. Kragon’s Flask

Kragon’s Flask is an unaccredited supply depot situated in a dried-up ravine to the northeast quadrant of Gamma-74. It is constructed from discarded pre-fabricated hab units, many elevated and lashed across the ravine to lift them out of the muck and optimise the vertical space. The natural shade and shelter of the ravine provide some respite from the world’s harsh weather, making it a popular spot for wastelanders in the region.

The proprietor, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.n6q9PZhLT9AdBPLp]{Ramm Kragon}, is a notorious Infractionist. He is a plodding, bulbous man who struggles to carry the weight of his augmetic arm, always tilting to his right and gritting his teeth against the haunting pain.

He enforces one rule above all others in his establishment — if you want to fight, take it outside. He’s taken great lengths to ensure the space is safe for those doing business, even between rival @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleet} crews who often visit to do so, especially those who want to do business away from Imperial entanglements. That said, Kragon also does some brisk business by spying on specific clientele and sharing pertinent information with his @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Dalal} contacts, who afford him protection to continue his business. 

The Flask and its barter hall have a reputation as a place where information is bought and sold, so others may be looking for @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, the Eye of Voll, or the marauders who took it — the characters could easily run into another hunting group here. Other denizens of the Flask are @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial Citizens}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dregs}, and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers}.

How Did We Get Here?

The characters may have heard of the Flask from Loris the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#the-shrine-of-the-scarred]{Shrine} Keeper or the scavengers at the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#d.-survey-crawler-b38649]{Survey Crawler B38649 (D}). From this, they should know that Kragon seems to be in the know about happenings in the region.

The Ravine

Surrounding the main hab units and storage, the ravine is choked with detritus, broken machinery and parked vehicles; @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8's}, other haulers and walkers are parked from end to end. The ravine even has room to host a few @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleet} walkers, all lashed up to the central hab units like a dock. Various crews and mechanics are about, repairing or preparing their vehicles to head back into the wastes.

Through the gaps in between, stilt walkers plod through the crowds carefully as young pickpockets practice outright snatch and grabs. Vendors hawk everything from slabs of grilled @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }meat to vehicle parts, dirty weapons, ammunition, or much-needed supplies to survive the wasteland.

The Barter Hall

An Ogryn named Cronk (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.AU5nhd0cV0sffDku]{Ogryn Ganger} stat-block to represent him) guards the door to the barter hall, along with a weaselly-looking doorman called Still (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Smuggler} stat-block to represent him). The latter does all the talking and determines who gets to go into the hall and who is turned away. Still makes it clear to newcomers that no violence is allowed in Kragon’s Flask, and breaking that rule means risking the wrath of Kragon and the other patrons.

Inside is a tumultuous riot of noise, pungent aromas, and wall-to-wall Humanity. The characters can see a mix of stilt walkers from the remediation pools, manufactorum workers with their telltale chemical burns, jumpsuit-wearing hauler drivers, and general wastelanders, criminals, and hive city outcasts. Most want the same thing: to find what they need and numb their existence with some of Kragon’s harshest swills or find some amusement in the form of gossip, gambling, or other vices — all fed by the bar on the opposite side of the barter hall.

Kragon prefers to spend his time among the crowds or hidden in his office, where he can monitor his patrons with an array of crude listening devices and auspex arrays.

Kragon’s Office

Characters can prove themselves to Still or anyone behind the bar by having 2 or more Infractionist Influence or by making a Challenging (+0) Presence or Rapport (Charm) Test. Succeeding, Still leads them to Kragon’s office. This is where Kragon feels the most comfortable, and compared to the rest of the Flask, the space is relatively clean and tidy.

Kragon’s desk is covered with an array of cobbled-together cogitators and data displays, constantly feeding him information. Either side of him is his personal @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.px7pplClKR01chqM]{Servitor} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.Y6oJff3F4qo2Xhlx]{Servo-skull} (the Servo-skull wields a concealed @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.tDe1U5EtxPowhYKn]{Web Pisto}l, and the Servitor is equipped with a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.DSKAdYMPRHvadLZz]{Shock Maul}). Both observe the characters with a steeled gaze; the Servitor, in particular, appears ready to strike at a moment’s notice.

He is happy to cooperate with the characters, knowing that they and other hunting parties are looking for @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{SIhn}, the Eye, and, by extension, the marauders. But something must be in it for him. He asks for 2,000 solars for the information they need. The characters can make a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Haggle) Test to lower this value by 100 solars per SL.

However, if the characters have dallied or wasted significant time at other locations, Kragon raises his base price by 500 solars. He’s already sold this information to one of the other hunting parties (either Venykar’s Sanctifiers, Echo Team, or Heldrax’s Stalkers), and it would be wrong of him to undersell his previous customer.

Here’s what Kragon knows:

  • He explains that the marauders have no static base but operate out of an armoured stilt-walker — the same sort that the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }farming @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleet} uses — and a smaller fleet of walkers to mark and strike at their targets. 

  • Because of this, @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#f.-the-float]{The Float (F)} moves about. But a long time ago, through dealings he made with the crew, he was able to plant a tracking device on it—he knows where it is right now and can give them the exact coordinates.

  • If asked about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, Kragon truthfully says he does not know how to find him. But he thinks the leader of the marauders does.

  • He knows the marauders attacked @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#d.-survey-crawler-b38649]{Survey Crawler B38649 (D)} and acquired the Eye. But soon thereafter, word spread that Sihn possessed the Eye and was willing to sell it to the highest bidder.

If the player characters cannot access Kragon for whatever reason, each character can investigate the Flask or the vehicle pool below. They can make a Hard  (−20) Awareness (Sound), Logic (Investigation), or Rapport (Inquiry) Test to reveal that @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#f.-the-float]{The Float (F)} is camped nearby, but they’ll need to move quickly to intercept it before they move on at sunrise.

Hunters on the Prowl

Once the players have left Kragon’s office, they are followed by @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP]{Heldrax’s Stalkers}, the final hunting group. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.H0LFfoPZTNE4TWjM]{Heldrax} wants to know what the characters know, and follows them as long as they can. He approaches them once they return to their @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8}. Characters can make a Hard (−20) Awareness (Sight) Test to catch Heldrax before he gets himself and his crew into position. If the characters fail, Heldrax and his crew have their weapons drawn ready to threaten the party and waylay them for information. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.Ke8aMBc9sS3H8SpH]{Trissa Vant} covers the whole scene from a sniper position hidden off to the side.  

Either way, Heldrax claims he knows why the characters have come to Gamma-74 (he’s been following them for some time) and believes that both parties can work together. All the Stalkers want is the Eye for their Patron. Getting rid of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} is not one of their objectives, but they would do so if it let them get the Eye. It’s up to the characters how they wish to respond to this ambush, and Heldrax’s offer — make an ally or another enemy.
