This is the last hunter group the party meets. Unless Heldrax is sufficiently discouraged at this point, he’ll aim to stalk the party, or at least assign some of his hunters to keep tabs on them until the end of the adventure.

Where to Go From Here?

The characters should have learned where the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#f.-the-float]{Float (F)} is located, about the marauders within and potentially their connection to Markis Sihn.

F. The Float

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Morgan Trace} leads a band of local marauders that move between planetary region Gamma-74 and other neighbouring regions between @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Dalal}. They aim to raid outfits of little consequence: depots, convoys, crawlers, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleet} walkers, and lone outposts. They are a known nuisance, but Trace is family to one of the local noble houses, so as long as she does no lasting harm and keeps funnelling information and money to her family, she is allowed to play pirate. The fact that she uses her ill gotten bounty to grease noble palms and remains outwardly devout also helps her keep her head attached to her shoulders. But her lifestyle and crew are now in jeopardy — the damage to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#d.-survey-crawler-b38649]{Survey Crawler B38649} was far more than she had planned, and Trace is worried that retribution is heading her way.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Trace} and her Marauders (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Ganger} stat-block to represent them) are based on an armoured stilt-walker called The Float. It’s better maintained than most stilt-walkers operated by Voll’s stilt-gangs and wasteland families. But more importantly, it’s faster, allowing The Float to pursue other walkers and outrun others easily. The marauders also maintain a fleet of smaller walkers — @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.PBcyq520buCt7qmx]{Striders} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.rJSCTS54GK4zYXit]{Sentinels} modified to better operate in Voll’s atmosphere — who act as The Float’s main attack force and a few @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8}s they use to go between outposts and fence their plunder.

How Did We Get Here?

From @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#e.-kragons-flask]{Kragon’s Flask (E)} the Float is the final location in the investigation before confronting Sihn and his agents. They should learn of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}’s duplicity and assemble the final clues to find Markis Sihn and the Eye of Voll.

The Camp Below

To save on fuel and avoid the dangers of the wasteland’s terrain at night, The Float often stops and makes camp after dark. The Float’s crew of attack walkers, haulers, and riders camp beneath the stilt-walker’s hull to shield them from some of Voll’s weather. The camp itself is a riot of tents, campfires, and debauchery. A cable elevator is swung over the side of The Float and operated by a crewmember should anyone need to go aboard. 

The marauders are not initially concerned that visitors have come to them — people often visit to seek an audience with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Morgan Trace} or trade with the crew — but anyone approaching is inspected in the camp before going aboard The Float. Attacking them is a foolhardy venture, as everyone in the camp is armed. 

Other Hunters

If the characters have had significant delays or lost their way along the adventure so far, it’s plausible that another hunting party has made it to The Float before them. Like the party, they have options for approaching The Float. They might go in all guns blazing and fail or succeed in making it to Morgan Trace — gunning down the crew or getting gunned down themselves. They may more sensibly parlay their way into her graces.

It is also likely the party’s last chance to forge an allegiance with one of the hunting parties or take them out of the picture before the adventure’s final chapter. Consider which hunting party you’d like to line up against them here, or which one you might wish to throw against the marauders, if any.

Going Above

The characters have a few options to convince the marauders to let them meet @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Morgan Trace}. They can make a Challenging (+0) Presence (Intimidation) or Rapport (Charm, Deception or Haggle) Test to convince them to let them aboard. The marauders are also easily bribed (which can overcome a failed Test in this instance). The guards at the cable elevator must ensure that no significantly powerful weapons are taken aboard but won’t strip the party of all their arms. The characters could also attempt to sneak aboard, though they’d have to find a way to climb up, and do so without being spotted.

Arriving at the top deck of The Float, the characters are met by a pair of guards who appear more like noble house guards than the marauders below (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcer} stat-block to represent them). These guards lead them to Trace. The outside of the float is not impressive, but the interior is well-appointed and shows more comforts than someone might expect in an upper hive hab.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Trace} meets the characters in what appears to be a large sitting room outfitted with lavish seating. The two guards stay with her throughout the meeting. She offers the characters refreshments and is happy to talk business with them. But Trace dismisses her guards once @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, the Eye, or the Survey Crawler is brought up. They seem surprised, but after a sharp word or look from Trace, they comply. 

Trace offers to tell the characters what she knows, but only on the condition that they escort her back to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} when they have finished with Sihn. She will not say why until they agree, at which point she tells her version of the story. Here is what Trace knows:

  • Trace is a childhood friend of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.CQH3R36NIhE0JyQ9]{Adriana Corbid}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}’s partner and lover. Corbid even calls herself the Left Hand of Sihn. Trace has misgivings about the nature of Sihn’s powers and worries that Adriana Corbid may soon be lost to them as well. She has not told anyone, even her family, what she knows about Sihn to protect Corbid. But that time seems to have passed now. She implores them to get Corbid away from Markis Sihn.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Trace} goes on to say that she was contacted by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}. He tried to disguise himself, but the old fool was obvious. She'd known for a while that he was Sihn's Right Hand. Dorin knew where the crawler was and offered it as plunder to her marauders, but on the condition that the large gemstone they now call the Eye of Voll would be delivered to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}, which they did.

  • The marauder’s attack on the crawler went wrong. She expected the crew to surrender as they often do, but they did not and fought to the last man. Before they died, the last survivor of the crew claimed there was a conspiracy aboard the crawler to claim the Eye of Voll for themselves. The fight between the crawler crew and Trace’s Marauders brought irreparable damage to the crawler they were told to avoid.

Now @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.12z2XfTtvXfn6kwY]{Trace} realises her time out in the wastes is up, and it’s time to return to her family, even with her tail between her legs — she has to get to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Dalal} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, where they can retrieve her. She doesn’t trust anyone in the region, and if she leaves the limited protection of her marauders, all her will rivals come after her. She needs someone like the players and their Patron to help get her out.

Of course, this is secondary to the character’s main mission, and Trace wants to ensure that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.CQH3R36NIhE0JyQ9]{Corbid} comes with her. Desperate for their help, Trace aids the characters however she can. 

Where to Go From Here?

The players should have learned of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}'s duplicity, and they likely want to confront him. Talking about doing so in front of their driver, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Zenyi Restax}, could mean Dorin is tipped off before they arrive. This clue leads directly into @UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ]{Part 3} of the adventure.

The party’s sub-orbital flight to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost} leaves in a few hours, so they only have a brief amount of time to gather what they think they might need for the mission ahead. If they are in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, their point of departure is within the mid-levels of the Void Buttress, level LH43.

Level LH43 and its neighbouring areas of the Void Buttress serve a fleet of light haulers and transports that fly between the hive and Voll’s industrial outposts, transporting goods and workers. If the characters arrive early, they can look around, dig up any information they might want, or prepare for their adventure into the wastelands. The walkways and terminals between departure platforms are often packed with merchants, selling any Equipment they might seek to aid them in their travels — though the party should note that the area is patrolled and inspected by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet} @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.pXsZLEawZr8Tf8Ym]{armsmen}, so acquiring any non-Subtle weaponry is likely out of the question.

In this area, characters can gather information about planetary region Gamma-74 by making an Easy (+20) Logic (Investigation) or Rapport (Inquiry) Test. Each character who succeeds learns a rumour from the following Table. You may need to tailor the information to any specific topics the player character asked about.

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.MPIbOaHVIrt42md2 noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumour}

Meeting Other Hunters

While the characters wait to depart, call for a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test. If any succeed, they notice their group is being watched by several figures clad in black @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} robes. They are heavily armed, each carrying a bulky flamer. They are Venykar’s @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.iKvdzTSaNlUB2E4l]{Sanctifiers}, and they seek to know more about their competition and find others who are hunting Sihn.

If the characters do not approach the Sanctifiers, they continue to follow the party and interview any locals they might have talked to, grilling them about what the characters asked them about and what they told in return.

Eventually, a shrouded and heavily tattooed Ogryn with a heavy flamer slung over one shoulder intercepts them. He only says, ‘Caul wishes to speak with you.’ and gestures towards a nearby cargo bay. 

If the players agree to meet @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.J2XpzgNHnNgxTXDV]{Caul}, they find him in a shuttle bay near their own with the rest of his group, otherwise, he and the rest of the Sanctifiers are waiting in the character’s shuttle bay before they depart. 

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.J2XpzgNHnNgxTXDV]{Caul} blatantly asks what their interest in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} is. He does not mince words; he states that Markis Sihn is an abomination and a heretic and will be purged. Caul is most concerned about knowing if the party is going to get in his way or not.

How this meeting goes is up to the characters’ reactions to Venykar’s Sanctifiers. If they are friendly then @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.J2XpzgNHnNgxTXDV]{Caul} shares what information he has (two of the rumours previously listed). If they are terse then Caul reciprocates and will be on the lookout for the player characters in the future. This is an opportunity to make a new ally or enemy.

If the party gets into a fight with the Sanctifiers, patrolling @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.pXsZLEawZr8Tf8Ym]{Armsmen} quickly respond and break up any fight, arresting any characters until their departure or delaying it further.

Other Hunters

This encounter as detailed assumes that Venykar’s Sanctifiers are a good fit as a possible ally. Consider swapping these hunters for another group (from the @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP]{Dramatis Personae} section). If a party member or their Patron has significant Influence with a Faction, picking a hunter group that aligns with that faction might be a better fit.

Similarly, the other two hunter encounters later in the adventure (@UUID[.hAh0wCOI99ZbTcQ6#others-looking-for-transport]{Others Looking for Transport}, and @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#hunters-on-the-prowl]{Hunters On the Prowl} should be modified as needed. Each encounter with Hunters should be more strained than the last. The group the party has the least Influence with should be saved for last.

Eventually, it is time for the players’ flight to region Gamma-74 — their @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter's} departure is imminent and announced over @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.4CglrWXiksan6Wk0]{laud hailer}. Regardless of how they get along, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.J2XpzgNHnNgxTXDV]{Caul} excuses himself and the rest of the Sanctifiers. They have more to do in the hive before they head to Gamma-74, and he cryptically promises to see them again soon. If friendly, he also gives the players his vox comm codes and frequency so that they can contact him later.

Arriving in Region Gamma-74

The flight to Region Gamma-74 and @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost} G74 is long and tedious. Through a vid-screen the characters can see outside — primarily dark clouds interspersed with flashes of lightning, a cause for heavy turbulence throughout the flight. When the weather breaks, they can see some of the terrain below — vast acidlogged wastes and outcroppings of acid-stained rocks. Eventually, the engines whine as the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter} drops below the clouds, and @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost} comes into view.

The outpost is home to a few thousand citizens and is bustling with activity when the characters arrive. Describe the scene to them: as they are ushered off the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter}, the crew begins to refuel, as new passengers embark to return to the hive. Cargo haulers come and go with supplies and tanks of acidic materials. Another flyer arrives soon after theirs and quickly detaches a few cargo pods.

The Subpar Sub-prefect

An @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} adept meets the characters near the landing pad, informing them he has been ordered to lead them to sub-prefect @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}. Their way through the outpost takes them through a maze of habs and support buildings until they reach a large Adeptus Administratum building at the heart of the complex. Once inside they are led through a large warehouse full of adepts taking inventories and filling in various reams of paperwork. They are led to a small office with a large ornate desk where sub-prefect Rastigan Dorin sits.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} looks tired and bedraggled. He greets them in a monotonous official tone and welcomes them to Voll’s planetary region Gamma-74. Dorin says he knows why they are here and who they work for, and is happy to help however he can. Dorin has already requisitioned for them a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8} ground hauler to travel across the wastelands and a driver to act as their guide. 

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} presents them with enough information to get the party going. He offers them the first lead without challenge, but each character can make a Difficult (−10) Presence or Rapport Test to gain another. The leads provided in order are:

  1. A workers’ strike is brewing at Processing Plant Gamma-74c15. The overseers have already captured a few labourers, but others have holed up in a volatile area of the manufactorum and refuse to speak to anyone except official negotiators. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} hands them a sealed missive and asks them to be his envoy and deliver it to the strikers, adding that ‘this should give the workers enough of what they want and get them back to work’. (In truth, Dorin knows that this work stoppage is only tangentially linked to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}, and he wants this foolishness to stop. He does not wish Sihn dragged into the dispute and needs the processing plant back to full efficiency, so no more scrutiny is drawn to the region. However, he currently lacks the manpower to defuse the situation, which is where the characters come in.)

  2. If pressed for more information on @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} tells them there is a shrine in the @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#c.-the-western-remediation-pools]{Western Remediation Pools}, which he heard Sihn used to frequent. The caretakers of the shrine could be of use in finding him. He does not tell them about the monsters rumoured to lurk in the pools, or that the shrine priests have no real connection to the Court of Sihn. 

  3. The last lead that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} might give them is the attack site of @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#d.-survey-crawler-b38649]{Crawler B38649}. If the party is particularly interested in the Eye, Dorin relays his thoughts that the crawler attack is where @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} acquired it. The only reason Dorin is giving up the attack site is that he knows Markis Sihn was not directly involved (the attack was by the marauders) and that scavengers have been picking over the crawler's carcass since the attack. He assumes this is a dead-end.

A Truck and a Guide

The characters are then let loose inside the outpost and given directions to find the garage where their @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8} transport, and its driver, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Zenyi Restax}, are waiting for them. The characters can attempt to find more information from the workers in and around the outpost. If they take the time to interview any locals, the characters obtain another rumour from the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.MPIbOaHVIrt42md2]{Rumours of Region Gamma-74} Table. They can make a Difficult (−10) Logic (Investigation) or Rapport (Inquiry) Test to acquire another. Note that citizens in the outpost are wary of talking to outsiders or ‘hive-dwellers’, which the characters may appear to be.

As the characters pass through the outpost, they notice a couple of workers cleaning graffiti off an alleyway wall. They can make an Easy (+20) Awareness (Sight) Test to interpret the scrawlings and fill in the blanks — the graffiti displays a hand with a large eye in the palm and rays emanating from it. When asking locals about this symbol, they prefer to give away as little information as possible, stating that it is just the mark of a local cult. In truth, this image is @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}’s symbol. 

The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.IfL7M9sq7tgeRlYx]{Cargo-8's} garage has several bays with other vehicles nearby in various states of repair. If the characters ask for @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.2b1OPABz1PyQO5eq]{Zenyi Restax}, they are pointed to a large, dilapidated cargo hauler on a lift. A woman in coveralls is working under it. This is Zenyi Restax, and she greets the party with grunts and nods, giving terse answers to any questions. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Dorin} told her the party was coming, and Restax says she will be finished with maintenance in a few minutes, asking them to wait.

Others Looking for Transport

While waiting for Restax to finish, a group of well-equipped soldiers stride into the garage. They lack a clear indication of any Imperial military affiliation, though they carry themselves like well-trained veterans. These are members of @UUID[.DnLjUQWLSFVsevlP#echo-team]{Echo Team} looking for a driver to take them into Voll’s wastelands, led by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.c8ecBxgeS9Rrtxpm]{Captain Pollis} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.r7RGS2rmtlm1xF4m]{Lieutenant Cole}.

If the characters aren’t intentionally keeping a low profile, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.r7RGS2rmtlm1xF4m]{Cole} notices the party and approaches them, and asks them questions about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}, but he’s careful to keep any intel of their own close to his chest. All characters approached should make a Difficult (−10) Discipline (Composure) or Rapport (Deception) Test, any failures reveal the party’s intention to the Lieutenant. Otherwise, Cole treats them with some respect if the party or characters have positive Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}. 

If the characters consider teaming up with them to defeat @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}, or simply share information, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.r7RGS2rmtlm1xF4m]{Cole} introduces @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.c8ecBxgeS9Rrtxpm]{Captain Pollis} to the party. She isn’t against teaming up, but is wary of working with anyone who seeks the Eye for material gain. Pollis is pragmatic; she has orders to kill Sihn and take the Eye, which she plans to do no matter what. If the party and Echo Team part amicably, Cole shares their Vox codes and frequencies to communicate with them later. If everyone parts on bad terms, tell the party they should avoid acting hostile towards Echo Team. Aserion Outpost guards (use the Astra-Militarum @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.060QdCc5DdlQwdhI]{Trooper} stat-block to represent them) are likely to interfere in any conflict. Unless the party has high levels of Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}, the guards are more likely to side with Echo Team.

Soon, another driver in the garage agrees to take Echo Team’s solars and transport them into the wastes. They load up and depart before the characters go towards their first destination. If the characters failed their Test against Cole’s inquiry earlier or parted on bad terms with Echo Team, the next time they come face to face, Echo Team treats them no better than competition and interference.

The adventure begins on Voll's surface, within one of the world’s hive cities. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} is the easiest to reach from voidship transfer, where many other adventures in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K]{Voll Adventures} begin. After they are situated, their Patron contacts the party via their usual means: perhaps face-to-face, via communications, or through an intermediary. Read aloud the following, modifying the text to suit your Patron’s goals:

Out in the wastelands, a cult of personality has sprung up around a man named @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn}. He appears to have some form of diabolical healing sorcery, and the following he has amassed is deeply concerning. Recently, the cult has acquired a monstrously large and pristine gemstone, an unusual acquisition dragged from Voll’s depths. They have dubbed it the Eye of Voll.

The appearance of large gemstones is not unusual on Voll. Some are found inside harvested acynadi but are worth little more than a broken tooth. However, this particular rough gemstone is large enough and clear enough to manufacture a defence weapon or even voidship weaponry. It is extremely valuable in the right hands. The wealth it could provide to the cult would be disastrous, and it is a powerful bargaining chip.

I have arranged for a shuttle to take you to Aserion Outpost, an Imperial bastion in planetary region Gamma-74, to serve as your base of operations. I’ve arranged for you to meet with an Administratum sub-prefect named @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}. Dorin knows you are coming and will brief you on the region and provide you with transportation and a guide.

The Patron also provides the party with 2,500 solars for bribes and expenses and reiterates the two objectives: eliminate the rogue psyker and acquire the Eye of Voll. Which objective takes greater precedence depends on their Patron’s motivations. This may be their last chance to ask any more questions before they head out into Voll’s wastes, and communications become difficult to maintain. If a character wishes to ask for more solars, they should make a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Haggle) Test. Each success level convinces the Patron to give them 250 more solars.

Patrons

Understanding the players’ Patron’s involvement in the hunt for Markis Sihn and Eye is crucial to kicking off the adventure. Each faction has different reasons for wanting to capture or kill Sihn or acquire the Eye. Below are suggested motivations for each Faction:

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}: The Adeptus Administratum's scribes misplace or fail to record inventories all the time, and a certain amount is to be expected. However, a crystal the size and calibre of the Eye of Voll should never have slipped through the Adeptus Administratum’s purview, and this error must be remedied. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}: Suspected as a powerful rogue psyker, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} must be captured for the black ships or otherwise eliminated. The Adeptus Astra Telepathica cares little about the Eye other than its apparent value to others; it is Sihn that they care about.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}: The Eye has great technical and weaponised potential, and could contribute significantly to Voll’s armaments or the Imperial tithe. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} is of little concern to the Adeptus Mechanicus, but the Eye must be acquired at any cost.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}: @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} is a cult leader who does not preach the word of the God-Emperor and must be destroyed. Their attempts at helping the populace through witchcraft are heresy, and their cabal must be purged. The Eye should be returned to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} for processing.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}: It is most likely that the Astra Militarum is being called upon to solve this problem on behalf of another faction or at a joint request from many. Secure the Eye and eliminate the rogue elements by any means necessary. Voll’s stability cannot afford any sizable rebellious elements operating on the world. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}: Fleet command knows that the Eye can be used to repair or produce powerful voidship weaponry, so it must be acquired. The elimination of a rogue psyker and his cabal in the process would show the prowess and capabilities of the Imperial Fleet.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}: Whether a criminal mastermind or a guild master, any Infractionist would instantly recognise the value of the Eye of Voll. Outside of claiming a small bounty, the fate of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} is of little concern to an Infractionist and might even make a good ally to some, but the crystal is the true prize.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}: Heretics and their ilk can not be allowed to flourish. Elimination of the rogue psyker and the destruction of his cabal before it festers into a full-blown heretical uprising is paramount. Retrieve the crystal and prevent it from falling into the wrong hands. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasty}: Voll, a planet ruled by the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#castyx]{Castyx} Rogue Trader Dynasty, labours beneath a tithe inflated by expectation. If it is all it is said to be, the Eye alone could pay a considerable portion towards this onerous burden. The profit potential is difficult to understate.

Depending on a Patron’s Motivation, the following may also be suitable:

  • Conflict: Any cult that imposes on the Imperium deserves to be quashed. Demonstrate the might and glory of the Imperium to the citizens of Voll.

  • Information: Traitors operate within Voll’s hierarchy of power. Find out who @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} was paying off to avoid attention and bring them to justice, along with the rogue cult.

  • Materiel: The Eye of Voll’s value to the Imperium is worth more than the lives of the cult’s dregs and the workers they’ve indoctrinated. Acquire this rare gemstone at any cost; don’t let anyone get in your way.

  • Reputation: Putting down an infamous rogue psyker and their anti-imperial cult and acquiring the Eye of Voll for the Imperium would be a boon to any Patron’s reputation.

  • Unity: The infighting and politicking over the Eye of Voll’s custody is sowing discord between the local factions of the Adeptus Terra; see this matter resolved hastily and deliver the Eye to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} for processing, as proper procedure requires.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} claims to be a messenger from the God-Emperor who has built a small domain amidst the centuries-old industrial infrastructure spread around the world’s hive cities. Voll produces vast quantities of medicae treatments, but little is used to benefit the citizenry who made it. Sihn wielded this fact and leveraged his unnatural powers to build a loyal following. He alone can heal the lung damage and acidic burns that result from working within the corrosive fumes and caustic liquids of the chem plants and acid refineries of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.59y8WFXTbwKRwiRI]{Voll}.

Those who have known the touch of Sihn are healed but also altered. Some recall lives that are not their own, while others find their appearance changed to the point where old friends no longer recognise them.

That @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} must be eliminated is a given, and if the powers that rule Voll were faithful and loyal, they should indeed have laid waste to the psyker and his cult years before. But in addition to his sway over the lower citizenry, Sihn has a knack for finding valuables among the effluent run-off and piles of rejected minerals and uses these resources in a web of bribery and intimidation to ensure the authorities pay no heed to his existence. 

Whispered rumours suggest that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} has uncovered a gemstone of unsurpassed size and clarity. This naturally-formed structure could be used in the construction of large-scale energy weapons, as part of voidship and planetary defence systems. Seemingly formed within the carcass of an abnormally sized @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, this gemstone, which Sihn has dramatically dubbed the Eye of Voll, is guarded carefully by the psyker and his court, for he knows it could promise wealth and ruin in equal measure. 

@UUID[.hAh0wCOI99ZbTcQ6]{Part 1: The Hunt Begins} — The characters are introduced to the adventure, some of its major characters and travel to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}.

@UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn]{Part 2: Into the Wastes} — The characters explore Voll’s wastelands searching for clues, braving the elements and testing their mettle in dangerous situations.

@UUID[.Dcvskxz1dZGpWgIQ]{Part 3: Hidden Beneath}—The characters return to @UUID[.eiMwmm7AQZLlFOkn#a.-aserion-outpost]{Aserion Outpost}, confront @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} and his fellow masterminds, and attempt to recover the Eye of Voll.

@UUID[.B8aJZIVIkn5ZVDlc]{Aftermath} — What happens to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Markis Sihn} and the Eye of Voll rests mainly on the character’s actions and how they dealt with the other hunters.

Numerous factions gather to make their bid for the Eye, perhaps among them the character’s Patron. The party must navigate betrayal, corruption, and the Warp-derived powers of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn} himself to survive. Arriving in the wastelands, the party must explore and try to uncover the hidden hideout of the rogue psyker. Whether they use guile and subterfuge or force and bolter shells, they will run into other groups with similar goals to their own. Will they make them allies or enemies, and how will the party deal with Voll’s wastelanders?

All roads lead to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kzYsrPppcXUNYTVe]{Sihn}’s lair, where he and the Eye are sequestered. The final confrontation puts the characters between the rogue psyker, other hunters, and the denizens of the waste who have fallen under Sihn’s sway.

Despite the relative safety of Voll’s hive cities, many Humans choose to, or are forced to, live on the fringes of the hive’s sprawl, or farther out into the caustic wastes and the Unsea between. There are countless Imperial or Infractionist outposts beyond the hive spire’s sight, and the Vigilite’s remit to patrol. These planetary regions are effectively lawless, where the best way to survive is to band together in gangs or cults, or adhere to the authority of the world’s guilds, who operate there. Altogether, these groups know they can get away with unauthorised acts, far from the Imperium’s brand of civilisation. 

Voll barely tilts on its planetary axis, so its seasons produce an almost imperceptible change. The weather may get slightly colder at the world’s poles and warmer around the equator. Terrain across the planet’s surface is essentially uniform, mainly consisting of acidic silt flats, caustic swamps, and an ocean known as the Unsea, punctuated by scant pockets of rocky outcroppings and truly solid ground.

The rarest sight on Voll’s surface is the few ancient ruins that jut out across the landscape, constantly being washed up above ground or brought back below by the shifting acid tides. Technoarcheologists from the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} believe they are the ruined foundations of an inferior pre-Imperium Human society, one summarily repelled by Voll’s acidic environment. Other theorists believe they are proof of a former xenos presence on Voll, perhaps a progenitor strain of the world’s only fauna, the @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}. The truth remains a mystery, whether it is one of these theories or hidden among others. 

The adventures @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.0sTvCVRuh5Wpawt9]{The Eye of Voll} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.QbQ7dTzbEVJyBLXJ]{Interminable Devotion} both take place beyond @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}’s perimeter, where characters have to fight against the environment as much as their antagonists.

Noxious Atmosphere

Voll’s hazardous atmosphere can significantly affect a character’s senses. Smell and taste are most affected; simply breathing without air filtration or protection can quickly overwhelm. Exposed eyes may easily sting or threaten blindness. Prolonged exposure to any acidic substance could also affect a character’s sense of touch. Consider increasing the Difficulty of Awareness (Sight, Smell, Taste, or Touch) Tests to reflect this when the characters are in exposed areas. Take particular care when describing what a character smells or tastes, as after a few days exposed to the surface atmosphere, these senses are easily dulled to the point of uselessness.

As per the Exposure rules, every four hours, a character is exposed to Voll’s bare atmosphere or weather without protection. They must make a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Endurance) Test or suffer the effects of a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.UaRHLqZ99zmg7AeE#exposure]{Noxious} environment.

Don’t worry too much if you forget about triggering this effect — Voll has a volatile weather system that causes the toxic atmosphere to ebb and flow. Instead of timing these Tests exactly, consider asking the characters to make these Tests once they return from the outside world, or between major scenes, to see if they were affected by it.

Wastelanders

In certain planetary regions, the Imperium runs large-scale industrial works. Remote outposts and manufactorums fed by neighbouring harvesting fields, synthesising chemicals for the hives while spewing out lakes of runoff waste. Workers cling to their manufactorums for survival, forced to live among the machinery or adjacent encampments. It is often better to take on an extra shift to keep a roof over your head than be ejected into the wastes.

Scavengers and field workers brave the harsh environment every day. They work the acidic pools and external pipeworks to ensure chemicals continue flowing, clearing away detritus while hunting @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }to feed their fellows. Many work atop stilts or one-person walkers to keep them above the Unsea level, and wear rebreathers to save their lungs. But that is rarely enough to protect their senses in the long term. Most citizens quickly lose their sense of smell and taste, and tend to go blind early in life — some sport crude augmetic eyes, while others simply learn to do without.

Infractionist elements hide between and beyond, easily forgotten or deemed unworthy of eradication by Voll’s leadership, more focused on maintaining their hive and tithe. This felonry leeches off the undefended populace and unaware authorities, stealing from imperial stockpiles, running rogue manufactorums, or pirating the @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleet}. Furthermore, the wastes are a prime breeding ground for proliferating cults. False seers can draw on an already impoverished populace, people seeking any shred of hope they can find, without much Imperial oversight to hold them back.

Voll Wastes NPCs

Among the imperial citizenry, characters are most likely to encounter @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dregs}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers}, and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers} out in the wastes, with pockets of Adeptus Terra representatives relegated mostly to protected Imperial outposts.

The Stilt-Fleet

Stilt-fleet families are borne of blood relations with old Voll lineages or gangs cobbled together from hive-city rejects and runaways. Each is defined by the stilt walkers they live on and pilot; multi-legged hab-units plundered or repurposed from Voll’s farms or industrial zones. Families patrol the wastes as nomadic gatherers, scavenging broken machinery, searching for wild patches of algae, but most importantly, hunting @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }for their meat.

The hive city highborn see the Stilt-fleet as a single laborious entity to keep placated from afar, but competition between families is fierce and often lethal. Unofficial territories are carved out across the wastes, the closer to a known @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }spawning ground or the world’s hives, the better. No family wants their stilt walker to break down so far from civilisation.

Stilt walkers need constant maintenance and rework to keep running. They are walking wrecks in the making, riddled with such jury rigging and ad hoc fixes that most could be written off as tech heresy. But the walker’s legs take the brunt of the wear and tear. After months of plodding through the caustic wastes, feet and shin sections often need total replacement; spares are frequently carried and fought over.

Some Stilt-fleet families deal directly with lower-hive and hive sprawl locals, often where their supply is most needed. But others are directly allied with the Mercator Carnem. They provide a steady trade for families' catches and some modicum of protection. But the guild isn’t beyond pressing families into open warfare to protect their hunting grounds, and is not beyond sending mercenaries to tilt the odds in their favour.

Characters lost in the wastes could encounter a Stilt-fleet walker for rescue. Most keep an open vox channel for emergency purposes. In some planetary regions, they are more likely to respond than any Imperial presence (especially if the characters lack Influence with the proper factions). But Stilt-fleet families are tightly knit bands; they are suspicious of any strangers they take aboard and consider them an instant burden. Characters should expect to pay their way, in solars or labour, in order to be delivered back to civilisation in one piece.

The Acynadi

When the Imperium first landed on Voll during the Macharian Crusade, besides the inhospitality of the world’s atmosphere, the acynadi stood as their only opposition. Back then, many more lethal variations were present: beasts as tall as a Warhound Titan could swallow a tank or walker whole. Few records remain of these truly titanic strains, and many believe that if any still exist, they have been pushed far back beneath the surface after facing the Imperium’s might.

It is a known oddity that @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-vishavar]{Hive Vishavar} still deal with these larger strains regularly, but in general, the farther anyone is from Voll’s hives, or a @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleet's} regular hunting grounds, the more likely you are to encounter new and equally strange strains of acynadi.

The acynadi are perhaps Voll’s greatest mystery. The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, and to a lesser extent, Voll’s guilds, have been studying them since the Imperium’s arrival. They are little-understood creatures, and far-flung theories about their means and origins are more prevalent than any truth.

All strains appear to share the same base genetics, regardless of size or shape. Imperial and Adeptus Mechanicus records have not found any similar species on any other world. No one has discovered how the acynadi breed, eliminating the possibility of acynadi husbandry, which is why they are still hunted to this day. Some believe they are spontaneously generated by some unknown process of Voll’s atmosphere, or as parasites to a much larger organism living far beneath the surface.

The acynadi have no standardised diet, and some don’t appear to eat at all. Those who do, consume roughly any biological matter without reservation, though Voll has little of it to go around outside wild patches of algae. Despite the differences between strains, the acynadi often appear to move in packs, intermingling between strains. While they seem to squeak and screech at times, no established method of communication between acynadi has been recognised, and no psychic presence has been detected between them.

The many Magos Biologis assigned to the task are overwhelmed with studying and assigning classifications to the new strains constantly appearing, so much so that they have substantially lowered the bounty they once set for retrieving intact specimens. It’s barely worth a hunter’s effort or the solars they receive in return to do so.  

But as long as the world keeps spitting them out, citizens and guilds continue to hunt the acynadi. They are a key proponent of Voll’s economy and tithe to provide the citizenry with a local supply of nutrition and bolster the world’s contributions. 

The acynadi feature in many of the book’s adventures. Stat-blocks and additional information can be found for three different varieties in Appendix I — @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.7F9x6CZCJCp0IV6b]{Acynadi Beta-3}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5}, and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.8dS1s1UvVXyt6dyv]{Acynadi Gamma-7}.

It should go without saying, but the contents of this book are for GMs’ eyes only. The five treacherous adventures contained within this tome are full of dramatic twists and turns, which are best kept hidden behind the GM screen until the players discover them.

No matter the adventure you choose, your players are guaranteed a thrilling experience, as their characters plunge into the depths of @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} and the wastes beyond its mouldering walls. They’ll see every corner of Voll, exploring and investigating their way through the Hive Spires, down twisted manufactorums and overpopulated hab-sprawls, and far into the dangerous acidic wastes.

Ensure you read your chosen adventure through from start to finish before play. Take notes along the way and determine the resources you need, like maps and handouts. Many of these adventures have nonlinear or exploratory sections that require some understanding and familiarity, knowing where your players can go next without getting them stuck or lost. Each adventure contains a host of unique NPCs, each with different capabilities, allegiances, and motives, and much of this information is separated into each chapter’s Dramatis Personae section for ease of reference.

Make sure you are familiar with the core rules of Imperium Maledictum, but if it is your first time being a gamemaster, or your first time running grim and treacherous adventures in the 41st Millennium, consider checking out @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.f5PuitUGgp6jQz5K]{The Gamemaster}. It lays out what it means to be a GM and the responsibility it bears, and it contains plentiful advice on preparing for and running exciting, meaningful, and safe sessions.

The remainder of this introductory chapter contains additional GM advice and information about the people of Voll, its hive cities, wilderness, and the various factions at play — everything you need to familiarise yourself with this setting.

‘In rare moments when the caustic clouds part and the light of Voll’s star is unhindered, looking down from the Hive Spires, the whole world shines like a pearl. Underneath its rugged and scaly shell, you can still find beauty on this largely barren world. Its true value to the Imperium lies just as hidden.

— Adept Faraos, Castyx Dynasty Appointed Historian

The Voll system orbits in the outer swathes of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}, a small system colonised by the Imperium towards the end of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#the-macharian-conquests]{Macharian Crusade}. Back then, Rogue Trader Halion @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{Castyx} saw its potential as a refuelling point near the system’s capital, until they surveyed the system’s worlds. Voll was scouted as the system’s only habitable world — the rest are no more than dead, resource-light globes — even though it is incredibly inhospitable to Human life. The fact that it boasts several hive cities and is home to over one hundred billion souls is nothing short of a miracle and a testament to the God-Emperor’s faith and Humanity’s fortitude.

Some of the world’s importance lies in its proximity to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}, capital of the Macharian Sector, and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia}, resting place of Saint Macharius and the sector’s most prominent shrine world. Voll sits relatively equidistant to them both, clustered in the middle reaches of the sector. These vastly more hospitable worlds rely upon Voll’s vast chemical production to supply critical medicines and other luxuries.

Heretics and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists} see Voll as a ripe stage to set their plans in motion. A perfectly placed foothold near Persepolis and Macharia, with none too many eyes keeping watch. Plenty of long-forgotten boltholes are pockmarked across the surface for rogue elements to hide and fester, protected by the world’s noxious landscape.

Yet, in all the centuries that the Imperium has laid claim to Voll, the planet still hides many secrets. Some are fiercely protected, and almost wholly misunderstood, by Planetary Governor @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{Jasper Castyx}, as they were by the forebearers of his Rogue Trader Dynasty. No one knows what all lurks beneath the caustic wastes, and the Imperium has no time to wonder when the Macharian Sector demands so much of this seemingly hazard-strewn sphere.

Beyond the System

Voll has some notoriety across the entire Macharian Sector, with far more in the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.y6qA7KARTXADwzeV]{Cytheris Subsector}. 

Primarily, it is known for its chemical supply. Either harvested as raw material and shipped off-world, or processed by one of the world’s manufactorums into base chemicals or consumables. They produce various medicae applications, from cleaning solutions to rejuvenat reagents. Some solutions comprise parts of combat stimulants or other Officio Medicae-sanctioned drugs vital to the Imperium’s forces.

The world’s @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }are an ongoing mystery, even to the Magos Biologis of Voll’s @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} enclave. Forge Fane Incalcos-6, the Tech-Priest’s headquarters in @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, contains the most complete account of the strange species. Some of their Biologis share findings with the greater Cult of Mars for additional theories or research, creating an inevitable web of rumours.

Among the Imperial citizenry, the @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }are known chiefly as a source of relatively abundant nutrition. The beasts are hunted or harvested, then cured, packed through labyrinthine supply chains, and finally shipped all across the sector. Sufficiently nutritious yet uniformly bland, one can is enough to fill an @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} trooper’s belly to fight another day.

Some among the Imperium’s military branches may have heard of the Ghasts of Voll, a tough penal legion conscripted from the sentenced infractionists of @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-sanksorak]{Hive Sanksorak}. Each trooper wears an @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.p5bbKpPoAek6oSIQ]{explosive collar} that can be detonated if improperly removed or triggered by a superior officer for insubordination.

See the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.PVBIdihw9kMQmw2M]{Voll Rumours }Table for more snippets of information characters might hear on their way to Voll or from travellers who have been there.

Time on Voll

Due to the planet’s rotation, Voll operates on an elongated 36-hour daily cycle, 50-percent longer than a standard Terran day. This matters little for hive labourers and workers who rarely get a glimpse at the rising or setting sun, who find more importance in sticking to their rotating shifts of work, prayer and recuperation.

But beyond each hive’s perimeter, where workers and @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }hunters are subject to the world’s elements, people’s survival is dependent on the tide. Voll doesn’t use a traditional diurnal cycle; instead, the day is broken into three twelve-hour segments that sync up with the acynadi’s movement patterns as the planet’s acidic tide rises and falls.

  • During Flowing (High-tide), the wasteland comes to life, and the @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }are more active.

  • During Tranquil (Mid-tide), the wasteland is mostly quiescent, as are the @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }out in the wastes.

  • During Unquiet (Low-tide), the wasteland descends into darkness, and the most dangerous and largest @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }come to the surface.

These shifts and cycles are not in sync across the planet’s hives — it may be Unquiet in @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-vishavar]{Hive Vishavar} while it’s Tranquil in @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} — it depends on where the hive is located.

There is no specific order in which Voll Adventures’ content should be approached. Simply read through the adventure summaries and pick the ones you like best. Remember that any content within — characters, locations, plot elements, and content your players may skip over — can serve as inspiration or be repurposed into your other adventures.

Each adventure has its own Dramatis Personae section, detailing the major characters present and their stat-blocks. Additional stat-blocks referenced in an adventure may be found in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.Gz7MByBhQgNHU9jX]{Appendix I} or the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ]{Bestiary} of Imperium Maledictum.

As you run multiple adventures from this book, be sure to seed aspects of the others into the background as you go. This will deepen your worldbuilding, enhance your players’ experience, reward them for interacting with NPCs, and indicate to you what adventure they might want to tackle next. See the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.pvLxM5N4RAtjZJLB]{Voll Adventure Rumours} Table for some examples.

Consider reusing NPCs the characters have encountered across multiple adventures, enemies and allies alike, especially where there is opportunity for suitable crossover. By the end of each adventure, your characters have the chance to garner new Contacts from across the Imperium’s various factions. Players will always appreciate seeing a familiar face and feel clever for invoking a Contact with which they were awarded previously. Of course, parties always have favourite or reviled NPCs they would love to see again.

Finally, be sure to give your players and their characters some downtime between missions to let them recover, pursue personal goals, and do anything else their Patron needs them to do (see @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.eUFS6mIQy2oiz6IX]{Between Missions}.
