Getting Situated

Each adventure is written from the starting point where the party is already situated on Voll, within @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, having either originated from the world or been delivered to it via voidship by their Patron’s vast means.

If you have yet to describe their arrival, they will most likely have travelled into the system via Imperial Voidship (such as a vessel in the Merchant Fleet) and delivered to @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth’s} Void Buttress via @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter}. Hive Rokarth is the most connected settlement on all of Voll, so from there, they can easily find travel links to wherever their adventure might begin.

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.pvLxM5N4RAtjZJLB noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumours}

Using data from conquest surveys, the Astro Cartographica designated Voll as a hive world. Its environment wasn’t hostile enough to be classified as a death world, nor did its low prevalence of metal deposits make it amenable for use as a forge world. Its closest secondary classification was as a mining world, simply for the amount of materials that the Imperium could extract from the surface. But beyond that, there was just enough usable land to set the foundations for several hive cities, to provide the Imperium with more of what it persistently needs: materiel for the tithe, cheap soldiers, and a breeding ground for emergent psykers.

@UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} began construction six centuries ago, followed by @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal}, @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-vishavar]{Vishavar}, @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-sanksorak]{Sanksorak}, and @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-amlyr]{Hive Amlyr}. Each hive offers major transport and landing hubs, leading to other parts of Voll. At one time, all the hives and many major outposts were connected by a huge series of land transport networks — railways and highways — but most have fallen into disrepair due to the constant struggle against the world’s environment, while others have been claimed by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists} or the world’s ruthless guilds. Though Voll’s skies are rarely clear, air transport is the most reliable way to get between hives and outposts; characters of sufficient means can find transport to anywhere on the surface by visiting Rokarth’s Void Buttress.

The adventures @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.DSccO5miF7LSJCVS]{Illicit Fabrications}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.yAAIQKv8lK49HRLz]{Implacable}, and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.mOfAsI4kLKUGTLXd]{Paradigm Shift} all take place within @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, the world’s capital hive. But it may be important to keep in mind the ties characters and factions have to the planet’s other hives, and reminding your players that these other hive-cities exist will highlight the world’s enormity.

Hive City NPCs

@UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} and Voll’s other hive cities are diverse environments, bringing together all manner of characters and lifestyles from across the Imperium. You can populate the world with any of the Human NPCs listed in Imperium Maledictum (@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ]{Chapter XII: Bestiary}). See also, the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Macharian Vigilite}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.AU5nhd0cV0sffDku]{Ogryn Ganger}.

Hive Rokarth

Rokarth is Voll’s largest and capital hive, with over a thousand levels of Imperial metropolis and home to the highest concentration of population on the planet: over thirty billion Imperial citizens. It is Planetary Governor Jasper Castyx’s seat of power and dominion of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{Castyx} Rogue Trader Dynasty. Rokarth is also home to representatives of all branches of the Adeptus Terra, the world’s major guilds and noble families. Most have a headquarters in the upper hive or sequestered among the hive spires. Therefore, characters can source almost anything in Rokarth and find someone from virtually any faction to talk to, provided they have the correct Influence and endure the labyrinthine bureaucracy it takes to get there.

The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Macharian Vigilites} police Hive Rokarth and take orders directly from the Planetary Governor. Their unspoken duty is to maintain the cordon between the lower and upper hive — Precinct Majoris — and prevent revolts from forming among the citizenry below. The only significant deviation from their jurisdiction is the hive’s Void Buttress, which is under the total control of the Imperial Navy.

Rokarth’s primary outputs are the healing unguents, medicae implements, and chemicals for las packs, which Voll is widely known for. Manufactorums are wedged into the lower levels of the hive, entirely dedicated to their production. The manufactorum workers are forced to handle corrosive materials in their fabrication; all bear the telltale scars of acidic burns across their hands, forearms and other exposed flesh. Many lose the sense of touch in their fingers by middle age, the patterned ridges of their palms and fingers scoured away entirely, altogether removing their fingerprints, though this is true for much of Voll’s labouring class.

Hive Amlyr

Imperial authorities have long known that Amlyr is a hotbed for off-world smuggling and hosts a multitude of black markets. For centuries, the formerly ruling @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#kalveo]{House Kalveo} turned a blind eye to this rampant Infractionist activity; indeed, they encouraged it as active participants, acting under the belief that Amlyr would thrive best on such illicit business. Their judgment was, perhaps, influenced by the fact that many of them had become dependent upon the same substances they peddled.

No longer. The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#castyx]{Castyx} Dynasty has recently condemned House Kalveo for gross negligence and deposed them from their ruling position. Amlyr is now ruled by a Castyx Regent, assisted by a rotating council of bureaucrats and nobles from @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, each chosen at Planetary Governor Castyx’s whim. Their official remit is to scour the hive of Infractionist activity and steer Amlyr’s chem production back towards feeding the Imperial Tithe.

To survive, scions of House Kalveo have taken desperate measures. Not only have they continued their chem smuggling, some have become embroiled in the sub-sector’s Silent Trade. They now funnel xenos artefacts through Amlyr and @UUID[.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, attracting traders who wouldn’t dare to make such deals on nearby @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.0g60Fj0fRMDfzYGB]{Macharia} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.qLLaIGWiU6Lf6Rjy]{Persepolis}, due to their far greater security.

The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#mercator-carnem]{Mercator Carnem} has a profitable business supplying Amlyr with @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }meat harvested elsewhere on Voll, as most native strains of the beasts near Amlyr are utterly inedible. Yet, they are still hunted for other purposes as they contain potent reagents for synthesising stimms and narcotics, highly sought by the Mercator Lenimen and Infractionists alike. One group of Infractionist alchemists, known as the Durhior, use these compounds to bestow chemical augmentations that can supposedly aid people in surviving the rigours of Voll’s environment.

Hive Dalal

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#nethecare]{House Nethecaré} rules over Hive Dalal. Their authority was granted by House Castyx some centuries ago, due in part to the strong bonds between their house and the great work of Ravia Nethecaré. She was a Biologis savant and expert in biochemistry and hydroponics, who set the course for the house’s value to the Imperium and its virtues. She trained schools of scions in her methods and instilled the competitive nature between them that has persisted through the ages. Despite centuries of familial infighting and diplomatic marriages, House Nethecaré continues to produce Biologis experts that threaten to rival even the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}.

House Nethecaré were also installed as Hive Dala’s rulers to combat its primary issue — the hive’s architecture and its citizenry are engaged in a never-ending war with an incredibly resilient form of flora. Massive invasive root-like structures, dubbed ‘verminvine’, have burrowed through the entire hive, slowly pushing through the rockcrete from which Dalal was initially constructed. Thousands of labourers daily roam over the hive’s exterior, acid-pruning aggressive sprouts from every ageing crack. Many plunge to their deaths, as thorned outgrowths of verminvine sever climbing tethers with unusual frequency. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#nethecare]{House Nethecaré} is searching for fresh means to combat the vine’s rampant growth.

The house is uncomfortably aware of the hard time limit placed on Dalal’s stability; without a solution, the vines will outpace their efforts within a century, and the hive will fall. Their efforts to dig to the root of the vine’s creep are rebuffed by the plant’s incredible resilience and the region’s tectonic instability. As a result of this struggle, many of Voll’s other noble houses abandoned their holdings in the hive long ago or traded them to House Nethecaré for next to nothing. In truth, the Nethecaré are glad to see them gone.

Countless buildings have suffered bulbous-shaped ruptures, and new growths often disrupt traditional means of travel between hive levels, tearing apart whole floors, leaving massive open-air gaps between hive layers. Yet Dalal’s citizens regard this ongoing struggle with the verminvine as part of their daily lives. Most live near the manufactorums where they work and worship, and travel by winched platforms, climbing nets, and ladders, all easily repositioned to avoid new growths.

Due to their research, House Nethecaré are adept at growing algae and crops in Voll’s environment, mass-producing algae rations for their citizens and the Imperial Tithe — all grown and processed right in the heart of the hive. An unintended consequence of this feat has attracted a few rare strains of airborne @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }who circle the hive’s spires searching for algae to consume. Many end up as opportune hunts for the hive’s citizenry.

Hive Sanksorak

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#vylathi]{House Vylathi} are the masters of Hive Sanksorak, home to one of the most infamous penal legions in the entire Macharian Sector — the Ghasts of Voll. The Ghasts make up a significant portion of the hive’s tithe contributions, so much so that House Vylathi takes on prisoners from other hives in trade to bolster their numbers. Hive Sanksorak is surrounded by a massive body of strangely tainted, acidic water. The dreaded Pale Lakes are so named because their corrosive waters can burn exposed flesh through to the bone, and many osseous remains lay littered beneath their surfaces. The environment is so toxic, that the unprotected vocal cords of prisoners sent to work the Pale Lakes are soon reduced to horrid rasps by the caustic mist in the air. Infractionists that survive the Pale Lakes are known for being particularly hard to kill, their wills strengthened by the torturous environment, and it is they who form the core of the Ghasts.

The hive’s secondary output concerns animal protein. It is a primary supplier of non-@UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }meat on Voll, much to the Mercator Carnem’s chagrin. Little of their stock, save their famed large tardigrades, makes it below any hive’s spires. House Vylathi spends considerable solars on maintaining enclosed farming habs within Hive Sanksorak, to keep their varied and imported livestock safe from Voll’s atmosphere. The slaughter of each animal is a ritual made of blessing and bureaucracy. Thanks are given to the God-Emperor amid filling in reams of paperwork and contracts, each cut of meat carefully negotiated and predestined for delivery before any butchering begins, and no part of the animal is wasted.

Hive Vishavar

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.Dml6BI69jLrNOQU0#taj]{House Taj} is the ruling nobility of Hive Vishavar. Its scions are seen as heroes and noble warriors of the Imperium and are looked upon favourably by their populace and citizens across Voll. The house has one of the finest personal guards on the planet, more akin to an @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} regiment, with plentiful connections to the Astra Militarum, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}, and the Macharian Vigilites. Their proliferation over time has made the other noble houses of Voll uncomfortable, but House Taj’s forces are often the first to mobilise when the hives are threatened, leading the charge.

Much of Hive Vishavar consists of weapon, munitions, and vehicle manufactorums, supplying themselves and other garrisoned forces across Voll. Their artisans are responsible for providing the world’s Vigilites with their iconic gilded armour.

It is in the Hive’s favour that they have so much weaponry on hand. Vishavar remains under regular attack from strains of colossal @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}. Weeks or months can go by between attacks, but each spawned swarm threatens to destroy swathes of the hive city. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} Magos Biologis theorise that vibrations caused by the hive’s manufactorums attract the beasts, but none can afford to halt production to test this theory.

A rotating complement of Imperial Knights has protected the hive for centuries to combat this known menace. Currently, a deployment from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#macharian-knight-houses]{House Vandensarg}, from their nearby homeworld of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.IbZpibGY7OUzFmD3]{Maleer}, holds vigil. The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#macharian-knight-houses]{Vandensarg} relish in close combat engagements and outfit their knights accordingly. They are well-suited to fighting gigantic beasts, as their homeworld is rife with them. They collect trophies from each kill, such as massive claws and strange crystalline growths, from each one they vanquish.

Hive Vishavar suffered an infamous ‘spire fall’ several centuries ago — a total collapse of one of their hive’s central spires due to Voll’s tectonic shifts. The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} suffered some blame for not adequately preparing for this disaster in the hive’s construction, although many Tech-Priests cite unaccountable interference from the titanic @UUID[.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }as the primary fault. The collapsed spire destroyed a quarter of Vishavar at the time and killed countless millions. It has never been entirely repaired, leaving Vishavar with a massive western gash in its architecture that runs from spire to sprawl.

Having discovered a link between the explosion and an underground fighting pit, the party navigates the dangers and dealings within The Dreg before uncovering a vile plot and a mysterious benefactor lingering in an abandoned hideout.

The Dreg

The Dreg is a collection of the miserable and the desperate, all seeking some escape from the drudgery of their lives. An abandoned hovel amid the hab slums, made from collapsed tunnels and crumbled industrial floors. The dug out antechamber is lit by a discordant mix of scavenged, flickering lumens of various tones. A stairway descends to a heavy iron door where two massive brutes bulked by grafted muscle stand sentinel.

In the far corner of the antechamber, impossible to miss in his red scarf, sits Datan. He’s finishing up selling some of his black market rations to a customer. Should the characters approach him, Datan greets them with a greasy smile and begins to ask them what they’re in the market for. He has his rations on hand but otherwise claims to source ‘anything they need’ (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Smuggler} stat-block to represent him). 

If the party asks him about the rations, he confirms they’re his, a custom mixture made from militarum-grade rations and other nutrients sourced here in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. He claims it is much better stuff than what the dispensaries give out. He offers them at 10 solars for a pack of six — but is evasive if asked to whom he has recently sold them. Should the characters press him or otherwise mention their investigation of the manufactorum explosion, he says that he cannot confirm or deny any dealings he may or may not have had. Characters can make a Difficult (−10) Presence (Intimidation) or Rapport (Charm) Test, or simply offer him around 100 solars as a bribe, to loosen his tongue.

Other than his usual customers, Datan recently sold a large shipment to some gangers, the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#the-vylathi-knives]{Vylathi Knives}. The whole deal was brokered through a friend of his who also dealt with the Knives — the rations were something of a sweetener to the deal. Datan genuinely knows very little else about the deal. If the party asks about this friend, Datan points towards the stairs to the pit, guarded by a pair of rough-looking gangers:

‘You’ll find him down there in the pits. Kem, an old friend of mine, unless he’s done you some harm… In which case, I hardly know him. He sent the gangers my way. I didn’t get any names. The guy in charge looked pretty dangerous — smile like an acynadi and an attitude to match. They bought all my stock and left.’

Datan has little else of immediate use for the party but is a valuable Contact. If a character is particularly generous to him, purchasing some of his goods or paying 200 or more solars for his information, they may add him as an Infractionist @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#personal-influence]{Contact}.

The Pit Below

From beyond the doorway, leading down into the bowels of the Dreg, muffled cheering reaches up to be heard. Loud thumps and painful cracks further punctuate roars and screams. The architecture screams of decay, it might fall apart at any minute, but until then, the people here desperately need a place to go and forget their never-ending drudgery.

The muscled brutes guarding the stairs are Boritz and Urdo (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ciU9gLyQG3bdXpT1]{Grafted Ganger} stat-block to represent them). Anyone with at least 1 @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} Influence can easily talk their way in — punters and their solars are welcome after all — but anyone with a bearing of authority is asked about their business, requiring an Average (+20) Rapport (Charm or Deception) Test needed to get past them. If violence ensues, a short fistfight is considered a reasonable introduction in the Dreg, but anyone who pulls a weapon is set upon by three more @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ciU9gLyQG3bdXpT1]{Grafted Gangers}, who emerge from a side room and attempt to remove any offender from the premises with all due bloodshed.

The stairs down to the pit are plastered with graffiti, much of it carved into the rusting bulkhead walls and pipework along the narrow stairway. The space beneath is impressively large. Characters with Advances in the Engineering specialisation, or anyone who makes a Routine (+20) Tech (Engineering) Test, realise it was once a massive promethium storage tank.

Beyond the stairs in the vast open space, three tiers packed with a cheering crowd overlook a dome of razor wire where two bloodied figures circle one another, fists raised. At the far side, separated from the crowd on a raised dais, a large man sits on a chair flanked by four hulking guards.

The two continue to exchange blows as the characters enter. The crowd roars in approval at the bloody spectacle. Before long, one man catches the other with a right hook and sends his target sprawling to the floor, teeth scattering through the cage to be swiftly collected by eager punters willing to risk the razor wire for a souvenir. Panting and staggering to his feet, the victor raises a bloody fist. Shouts of ‘Kem! Kem! Kem!’ resound as smug gamblers pass by cursing losers to collect their winnings. ‘Make your bets now, dear patrons! The night’s main event is upon us!’ says the seated man, a vox unit amplifying his voice around the hall. ‘The butcher herself will take to the cage later tonight!’ 

Victorious but with more than a few bruises, Kem leaves the cage and limps towards a nearby passage. 

The characters are free to mix with the crowd for a while, most of whom are happy to discuss their wins and losses. The Pit strongly encourages gambling — though most citizens put rations and favours on the line, it's mostly the gangers who regularly bet solars. Meanwhile, characters easily hear speculation on the upcoming bout: the Butcher is the favourite by far, but Kem is popular with the crowd. Kem however, has been fighting in the pit for years longer than most, and many believe he has slowed enough to make the coming match an easy win for the Butcher.

Following Kem

Kem sits in a filthy ablution chamber, washing the blood from his skin with murky water from a rusted pipe. His deep, wheezing breaths accentuate the messy gashes crisscrossing his muscular flesh. A crimson rag lies on the floor beside him.

With the blood removed from his face and hair, the characters can see he is far older than he seems and weary beyond measure. Looking up at them, Kem spits a gob of red spit onto the floor and asks, ‘What do you want?’

If the party explains to Kem that Datan told them he might know something about the manufactorum explosion, he curses and growls. He threatens to ‘snap that little rat’s neck’ when he sees him before breaking into a coughing fit and spitting more blood on the floor. He eyes the characters carefully before speaking again. Read aloud or paraphrase the following information:

‘I’ve fought four tonight. Four strong, vicious men half my age, and I still owe Yarneg one last fight before I’m in the clear. He’s put me up against the Butcher, the pit champion. I know I can’t beat her. Maybe when I was young, but now? It's a death sentence. I don't want to die here. You want to know about the explosion? Help me out, and I'll tell you everything I know.’

Kem agrees to talk about what he knows only if the characters offer their aid. If so, Kem explains that Yarneg owns the Dreg, presiding over the fights with his guards at his side. He keeps the Butcher locked up like an animal and sends a lackey to feed her gruel laced with combat drugs before each fight. 

Kem takes two pills from a brown paper bag and swallows them. ‘These are some of the strongest pain suppressants this side of the hive, courtesy of your friend Datan. Switch the gruel and dump the rest of this bag in it; that should be enough to give me a chance. Unless one of you would rather fight her yourself?’

He also tells them where to find the Butcher’s cell. A lone @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dreg} guards her wretched prison. If the guard can be distracted or removed, the characters can dose the butcher’s meal without issue. If they draw attention to themselves, Yarneg’s guards, more @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ciU9gLyQG3bdXpT1]{Grafted Gangers}, arrive to remove them.

Otherwise, Kem could be intimidated into answering. A successful Hard (−20) Presence (Intimidation) Test is enough to convince him to answer. But without the character’s aid, his prediction proves accurate, and the Butcher tears him to shreds in the coming bout.

A character might offer to fight in Kem’s stead. They need to convince Yarneg — a bulbous, sweaty mess of a man interested only in solars and the raucous cheers of the crowd — that they can make it an exciting fight. Taking down one of Yarneg’s guards bare-handed is enough to do this. Kem is surprised and grateful — he didn’t think anyone would take him up on that option. Surviving a bout with the unmedicated Butcher is another matter. Whether the lucky character wins or not, Kem is true to his word. Use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ciU9gLyQG3bdXpT1]{Grafted Ganger} stat-block to represent the Butcher. If she’s taken combat drugs, she can use her Grafted Muscle Trait without suffering any Damage from its effect.

An Easy Win

An hour later, the bout with the Butcher begins. The massive brute, bulked with grafted muscle, is led out in chains as Yarneg laughs from his perch. The crowd’s cheering falters once the Butcher is unleashed. If her meal was dosed with pain suppressants, she stumbles through the fight, making it an easy match for Kem — or any character who stands in his stead — who puts the massive woman down in short order. Silence reigns throughout the chamber, and then the cheering begins. Though notably, Yarneg does not look pleased.

With the fight over, Kem thanks the characters and provides them with what he knows. Read aloud or paraphrase the following information:

‘A man called DeGuar, a manufactorum overseer, used to come here occasionally, but that night was special. More reckless than ever before, he won bet after bet, until he lost big. The Vylathi Knives fixed all the fights that night. I don't lose many bouts, and I'm not proud of it, but I took a dive. I did it without Yarneg's permission. He can't touch the Knives, but he’s taking it out on us anyway — that’s why I got put up against the Butcher tonight.’

Kem heard the gangers talking while collecting his payment. The Knives fixed the fights that night specifically to get Overseer DeGaur into their debt. Once he owed them a sufficiently ruinous amount of solars, they ‘helpfully’ offered him an alternative. DeGaur would grant them access to the manufactorum, and they would take his workers. DeGuar would keep some of the chems from that place and start a new life off the profits. The manufactorum was demolished to cover the gang’s tracks. 

By then, the gangers had noticed Kem paying attention, which is when he went to Datan, making it seem like he’d be interested only in hawking a friend’s wares rather than spying on the gang.

Kem gives the party directions to a ganger hideout — he visited it once while negotiating his own deal — and sends them on their way. If the characters think to ask, Kem can describe the gang’s weaponry, mostly @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.nyjv454gtdJ43klt]{autoguns}, and the defences around their hideout, granting the party 1 Superiority in their next confrontation with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#the-vylathi-knives]{Vylathi Knives}.

The Raid

As the party returns to the main pit, a croaking voice calls to them from a nearby drain. ‘Go… The Skitarii… they’re coming’. The characters only have a moment to react to this warning before the crowd’s chants turn to screams, backed by gunfire and plasma shots. A squad of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o]{Skitarii Vanguard} are raiding The Dreg, having also discovered the fighting pit’s connection to the mystery. Amply forewarned, the characters may run if they wish. They witness a pitched battle between the Skitarii and the gangers if they linger.

Smoke fills the air as the crowd of citizens and gangers duck for cover, returning fire at the Skitarii, who push quickly into the main chamber, the ragtag resistance providing little opposition. A character may attempt a Routine (+20) Stealth (Move Silently) Test to lead the party and skirt their way around the crossfire towards the exit.  

Let’s fight!

Most parties have enough sense to avoid getting into a firefight between Yarneg’s gangers and the Skitarii, but if they are so inclined, you may allow them to do so.

If they are fighting on the side of the Skitarii, then the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.vsiOALilPnEe3dKg]{Skitarii Vanguard Alpha} in charge of the squad — Landa-12, whom they may have encountered earlier in the hab slums — recognises their assistance. The Vanguard are ordered not to engage them unless they are fired upon. Landa-12 hears the party out before sending them on their way, advising them that further interference in the investigation would be ‘illogical and ill-advised.’

If they join in on the side of the Gangers and win, then Yarneg forgets any previous ill will and thanks the characters profusely. The Dreg must be abandoned, but Yarneg is optimistic about starting over elsewhere and invites the party to attend his new venture once it is opened. The party’s Patron can leverage this connection to gain 1 @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} Influence, and the characters may add Yarneg as a Contact.

From the dais above, Yarneg hurls @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.QaiU7Hod2xMnOTM7.Item.Oe9FDIz24FoyKhjl]{Frag Grenades} towards the invaders. The crowd rushes for the stairs, abandoning cover to be cut down by precise fire. Yet the press of bodies living and dying clogs the stairway, making it a Minor Hazard. One of the characters may attempt a Routine (+20) Athletics (Might) Test to barge a path through the crowd without taking Damage. 

In the ruined antechamber above, several gangers are kneeling, hands shackled, and overseen by two @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o]{Skitarii Vanguard}. As the fleeing crowd bursts onto the scene, they raise their rifles and acquire targets. Unless the characters can muster at least +3 Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} and succeed a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Charm) Test, these Skitarii immediately open fire on them, as their command protocols have been set to engage any potential targets emerging from the Pit.

Assuming the party survives events at the Dreg, they can follow Kem’s directions to the Vylathi Knives' hideout. The mysterious voice they heard in the Pit could point the way if they did not acquire this information. The party may also have begun to suspect that Vand is DeGuar and now has enough information to hand the former Overseer over to the authorities if they are so inclined.

The Hideout

A rundown warehouse complex sits decaying and lightless amidst the hab slums. Sealed windows stare out over a former processing yard strewn with puddles of promethium, rusted machinery and vast spools of wire.

Following Kem’s directions, the party reaches the Vylathi Knives' hideout, finding it abandoned and unguarded. Its first floor consists of an open area and a small back room. Piles of refuse and loose strands of cabling scatter the floor before a dark stairway that rises to the level above. The smell of body odour and effluent is heavy, and a strange green stain marks the floor. Characters can find clues listed in the Abandoned Hideout Clues Table, should they search the hideout — provide at least one to each character involved in the search, and allow them to puzzle over what each might mean, or get them to make Challenging (+0) Investigation (Logic) Tests if they are stumped.

Once the recording (‘Labelled Vox Recording’) has been played, have anyone who hears it make an Investigation (Logic) Test, the difficulty of which varies depending on how long they have spent with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Barsis Vand}. If successful, it becomes clear that DeGaur's voice on the recording is the same as that of Vand, albeit somewhat more inebriated. If Vand happens to accompany the characters while the vox recording is being played, his terrified reaction makes this connection all the clearer.

What is Rejuvenat?

During the long millennia spent eking out an existence in an innately hostile galaxy, Humanity developed several methods of extending one’s natural lifespan. These often involve chemical treatments, mechanical augmentations, or stranger, poorly understood methods. These varied procedures, often commonly referred to as rejuvenat treatments, bear little similarity to each other beyond their shared effects. Some techniques hail from the Dark Age of Technology, and their workings are arcane. Others rely on chemical infusions that take weeks to administer or necessitate the permanent fusion of machinery to living flesh. On Voll, as elsewhere, rejuvenat treatments are the preserve of those whom the Adeptus Terra judges worthy of receiving them. Typically, the highborn of a given world, though loyal and surpassingly useful servants of the Imperium, may, through service, be worthy.

All these nuances and vagaries are lost upon @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.kdhQ2SwO7Vm2rzUI]{Navrak} and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#the-vylathi-knives]{Vylathi Knives}, who know only that the precursor chemicals produced by the manufactorum they targeted are used in rejuvenat treatments. Though valuable, they lack the additional components, the expertise, the arcane infusion arrays, and even the patience to administer the life-extending protocol properly. Of course, this will not prevent them from trying.

The party is confronted with an unlikely ally and the horrific fate of the manufactorum workers and must decide if they are willing to descend even deeper into the mystery.

Lerna Harrog’s Story

The party may react violently to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog}. If so, she attempts to plead her case while dodging their attacks and hiding in the shadows. Her voice is halting, fearful and angry at once. She knows she is an abomination, and her memories are beginning to fade. She fears — correctly — that whatever Humanity she has left will soon be lost.

She tries to explain that she wasn’t always like this, that something was done to her, and that once she realised that the characters were investigating the ruins, they might help her. Read aloud or paraphrase the following information:

‘I was a worker in the manufactorum… all of us were once,’ she says, gesturing to the bodies. People with guns came and took us. Then there was another manufactorum, an… underfactorum, I heard someone call it, somewhere below. They wanted us to make something, but we couldn’t get it right. The man above would ask who wanted to be set free, and I volunteered. But that was a lie. I remember a vat and terrible pain, then darkness, and I woke up here.’

Whether the party is chasing her or they are parlaying with her, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog} leads them into a vast cistern in the Maintenance Spillways, which contains evidence related to her tragedy.

The Maintenance Spillways 

Intended to provide emergency capacity to the massive chemical pipelines that thread their way through the level, the cistern has become a charnel house. Dozens of twisted corpses lie strewn about the chamber, their rotting forms massed against barred sewer grates. The remains of misshapen creatures and hideous mutants are strewn across the pit, but here and there, a recognisable limb or face can be made out amidst the horror. These are the remains of those who volunteered to undergo treatment with the stolen rejuvenat, their bodies tossed aside once it was clear the effects were not what was desired.

Having tried to find the so-called ‘underfactorum’ many times, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog} has never been successful and states that the longer this goes on, the more workers die or worse. Should the party mention @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Navrak}, Harrog is hit by a wave of pain, clutching her head and trembling; several seconds pass before she settles again. Harrog confirms that she believes Navrak was the man above in charge. Should the characters ask about a Tech-Priest, she affirms that one was present among the Knives. 

If the party spares @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog}, she can lead them to the facility — she knows where it is, but has been too afraid to go there alone. If they attack Harrog, she still tries to point them in the right direction. If they slay her, the characters are on their own, but there are tracks to follow. A successful extended Challenging (+0) Navigation (Tracking) Test requiring 10 SL total, with one Test allowed each hour, can bring them to the facility, mainly by tracing the spillways back in the direction the bodies appear to have come from.

The Underfactorum 

The spillways carry very little Human filth — what liquid flows through them is primarily chemical waste and, little better, any excess acid rain that had made its way down from above. Still, the stench of promethium and sweat can be made out as the characters approach the facility. Far more apparent are the cacophonous rattle of machinery and dull susurrations of captive @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers}. Dozens of tightly packed workers, pale and exhausted, operate hastily organised machinery amid an ancient manufactorum brought back to some semblance of function.

A dozen armed @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers} guard a large central chamber, with twin metal staircases leading up to a metal gantry above. Bright green fluid collects into waiting tanks lining the walls.

Sensible characters might judge this arrangement as too many gangers to overcome in a frontal assault. If the party seems set on rushing in, remind them they could gain some Superiority by scouting the area or taking up advantageous positions before the fighting begins. If they are determined to simply open fire, you should oblige them with a suitably brutal fight — feel free to arm a few gangers with heavy weaponry, such as a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.vEhnJA0i6WqddsNh]{Heavy Stubber}. In combat, many gangers spend their turns taking the Aim Action to make sure they hit their targets and avoid collateral damage; they have been explicitly warned against damaging the machinery.

A Brewing Madness

Now, so close to the scene of her transformation, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Lerna Harrog}’s condition worsens. She clutches her head at a suitably dramatic point, her muffled screams threatening to give the characters away. It should be clear to them that Harrog’s time is running out.

Assuming the party did not rush in, they observe a shift change among the labourers. Workers file into makeshift cells within side chambers while the next group emerges to begin their shift. This process does not take long, but for this narrow window, there are no workers on the manufactorum floor — a moment the characters may take advantage of, if they act quickly or wait for the following shift change several hours hence.

Features of the Manufactorum

Various Zones, features, and rooms across the Underfactorum shape the following encounters:

  1. An iron grate at the centre of the manufactorum floor is partially concealed from sight; however, it appears to be locked tight and must be picked or cut through to be of use. This grate is a valuable escape route for later that leads to an exit point in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's}Lower Hive. 

  2. Behind another filthy grate lies the worker’s fetid abulation chamber. A single ganger guards it, but otherwise, it is a quiet place to hide or launch an attack from. The doorless entrance opens onto the manufactorum floor, and several discarded workers’ uniforms lie in a pile inside.

  3. A mouldering pipe leads to a small makeshift control room where cracked cogitator screens display pressure readouts. Two Manufactorum Workers attend these consoles while two Gangers sit at a small table playing cards, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.nyjv454gtdJ43klt]{Autoguns} leaning beside their chairs.

  4. Through a small drain just big enough to squeeze through is a cell where vast numbers of prisoners are held, most of them lying prone, shivering, and exhausted. If the party has not dealt with him yet or has escaped their grasp, in an isolated cell, sitting on the floor, is @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Barsis Vand}. The man is desperate enough to mount an escape attempt if the characters can slip him a weapon, likely drawing guards away from other areas.

  5. The gangers have a room set up as a makeshift barracks, containing seized contraband from the workers and a cache of spare weapons (@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.nyjv454gtdJ43klt]{Autoguns} and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.85opt2usT8oNSZyt]{Stub Pistols}).

With these options, it is up to the party to devise a plan to circumvent the gang's superior numbers. Here are some options they could pursue:

  • The workers are unarmed; finding a way to arm them would go a long way in stoking an uprising.

  • Breaking the imprisoned NPCs out of their cells would go a long way to stack the numbers in the party’s favour.

  • The characters may attempt to pass themselves off as workers. Go undercover to gain information on the gangers—their patrol patterns, general strength and numbers, and the layout of the Underfactorum.

  • Seizing the control room and overloading the pressure in the vats could work as a distraction to allow everyone to escape. But if they aren’t careful, everyone could be covered in the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.HPlvqxmfzkHy3gUG]{mutating rejuvenat chemicals}.

Completing any schemes also reward the party with 1 Superiority for the fight ahead. However, even the best-laid plans have complications. The following scene occurs just as they are about to enact their plan.

Who Wants A Chance At Freedom?

With laud hailer in hand, @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak} emerges onto the gantry above and speaks words that boom over the din.

‘My friends, once more, a chance for freedom beckons! Test our latest formula and survive, and you can gain freedom!’

A moment of hesitation passes, workers exchange looks, and several raise their hands. Life in the manufactorum is anything but pleasant, and any chance at escape, even one so risky and poorly understood, appeals to some. After all, none have returned after volunteering, so wherever they’re going must be better than here, or they’d come back.

Gangers round up a volunteer and march him towards the stairs. At this moment, if @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog} is still alive, the characters notice something moving through the shadows of the manufactorum. The mutant is making for the volunteer, moving swiftly, desperately even. The party has a short window of opportunity to intervene. If they choose not to, the following occurs:  

As the volunteer makes his way up the stairs, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog}’s horrific voice barks from the shadows. ‘No! No more lies!’ She has had enough and leaps from the darkened recesses of a towering manufactorum engine. She lands hard amidst the gangers, knocking several to the ground. She bites and claws at them frantically, but the gangers soon recover, throwing her to the ground and levelling their weapons at her. The characters are given another quick chance to intervene. If they do nothing, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog} breaks free but is wounded as the gangers fire upon her. She disappears into the tunnels, dripping blood. From then on, the gangers are alert and more watchful of intruders. Should the party attempt to look for Harrog later, they cannot find her.

The Rejuvenat Sepulchre 

Beyond the stairs and the gantry above lies a chamber lined with stolen machinery and vast industrial piping. Walkways run between large vats set into the floor, their mechanical hatches yawning open, revealing bright green fluid that reeks of chemical putrescence.

If the characters have infiltrated this area quietly, they witness the following. If not, events are far more hectic, with @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Navrak} trying to get his forces back under control and into defensive positions amidst the rejuvenat vats. 

Once the characters reach the rejuvenat vats, they find it occupied by @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak}, three of his most elite fighters (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo]{Smuggler} stat-block to represent them), and @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx}, the abducted Tech-Priest. The characters see the volunteer, a young man called Venck, next to the vats. If they do not intervene, Venck is lowered into the vat, his will holding until a look of horror crosses his face just as the acrid fluid reaches his neck. It is, of course, far too late for regrets now. The characters also notice several vats already have other volunteers sealed within, while others stand empty.

Captured!

If the gangers discover the party or somehow capture them earlier in the adventure, they are brought before the vats to be the next lucky ‘volunteers’. @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Navrak} takes the opportunity to explain his goals to characters who may not yet have figured out his role in all of this.

‘Quite the troublemakers, aren’t we? I appreciate your interest in my research, but unfortunately, discretion is our watchword here. Still, there’s always the chance that our latest batch of rejuvenat has come out right!’ 

@UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Navrak} then attempts to throw one of the characters into the vats. Depending on the situation, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog} may choose to appear, Tech-Priest @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx} may be able to assist, or the party may devise another means of escape. If not, one of the characters is tossed into a vat, leading to an array of possible outcomes (see the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.HPlvqxmfzkHy3gUG]{Crude Rejuvenat Effect} Table). To better demonstrate the dangers of the crude rejuvenat, consider presenting it to the party by putting a disposable NPC in first, and describe one of the worst results from the Table.

@UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Navrak} uses his vox to call for reinforcement if a fight breaks out. If the party hasn’t dealt with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers} in the rest of the complex, they gradually rush to their leader’s aid. At the beginning of each subsequent round, two to three more appear by the chamber door.

Take Cover!

There are numerous pipes, vats, and other bits of mechanical equipment to take cover behind in any laboratory Zone. However, many of these contain precursor chemicals of one sort or another, and an unfortunate spray of gunfire may cause these toxic chemicals to spray anyone nearby.

If anyone @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.xf46pBDy93sT0ZDl#take-cover]{Takes Cover} in these Zones and becomes the target of a ranged attack, roll a [[/r 1d10]]. On a result of 8–10, a pipe or vat nearby is hit and ruptures as a result of the attack. Anyone within Immediate Range must make a Challenging (+0) Reflexes (Dodge) Test or is hit by some chemical spray and must roll on the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.HPlvqxmfzkHy3gUG]{Crude Rejuvenat Effects} Table.

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.HPlvqxmfzkHy3gUG noCenter=true description=bottom]{Description}

At the beginning of the fourth round of combat, or at the beginning of any round in which the party is outnumbered two to one, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Lerna Harrog} appears if she has not done so already. Erupting from between the chemical vats. She sets upon @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Navrak} and his minions, taking the vengeance she has longed for. 

The party should use this distraction to either press their advantage or flee. Doubtless, their Patron is likely disappointed if they choose the latter option, as it results in the loss of both @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Navrak}, who flees, and Tech-Priest @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx}, whom Navrak takes with him in the hopes of setting up his operation elsewhere.

If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Harrog} died earlier in the adventure, then @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx} may be able to assist the players, finally throwing off the yoke of Navrak’s intimidation and striking back at the gangers. However, Arx’s Augmetics are optimised for maintenance, not warfare, and the gangers might make short work of their captive.

The adventure begins in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. The characters are summoned by their Patron and tasked with investigating the accident in Manufactorum Vitus-II, located in Rokarth’s Lower Hive. An explosion has levelled the structure, apparently vaporising its workforce and leaving Tech-Priest @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx} unaccounted for. This occurred several days ago. However, the party’s Patron recently became aware of a purported survivor.

Critical Information!

The players are not initially aware that this survivor is the manufactorum’s former overseer, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Calis DeGuar}. To avoid detainment, he is lying low and disguising himself as a labourer named @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Barsis Vand}. As Vand, he claims to possess knowledge that tells a different story of what happened and is lying low in a hab slum in the lower hive.

Depending on the specifics of their Patron’s motivations in investigating the Manufactorum, the characters may have preparations they wish to make or preliminary investigations they wish to undertake. Feel free to allow them to do so. However, they should eventually reach interviewing Vand and investigating the site of the manufactorum — their Patron should point them towards Vand if they spend too long pursuing other leads.

Patrons

There are many reasons why the characters’ Patron sends them to investigate the destroyed manufactorum. The following are suggestions for each Patron Faction:

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}: The destruction of Manufactorum Vitus-II has been recorded as an industrial accident, but rumours have reached your Patron’s ears that it is anything but. Amending the data is a momentous exercise in bureaucratic efforts. Before undertaking such a task, the Patron must know the truth and dispatches the party to investigate.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}: A powerful @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.4neMMGpoX4oC0yOt]{Astropath}, perhaps the Patron themselves, has received a horrific vision of hideous mutants flooding upwards from the sewers of the lower hive. In the vision, they originate from Manufactorum Vitus-II. The characters are dispatched to investigate, only to find the manufactorum a smoking ruin. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}: The Patron’s rival within the machine cult has been tasked with overseeing the investigation of a missing Enginseer following a manufactorum malfunction. Performing this task more efficiently and with fewer resources will communicate your Patron’s superiority over their rival.   

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}: The final shipments from Manufactorum Vitus-II were essential to the rejuvenat treatments of several high-ranking Ministorum officials. Though all are ready for their souls to join the God-Emperor, most are also outraged as a matter of principle and demand the punishment of all involved. The party’s Patron can gain significant influence from their aggrieved superiors if they can handle the matter.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}: It is discovered that the destruction of Manufactorum Vitus-II, previously thought to be an accident, was accomplished using purloined explosives stolen from a Departmento Munitorum shipment. Those responsible must be caught.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}: Spending untold years or decades in the void and subject to the rigours of voidship travel, it is often imperative that Imperial Fleet captains live beyond their natural means. For Patrons based in the Voll system, news of a reliable rejuvenat supply being tampered with would bring cause for alarm.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}: Lower Hive contacts report sightings of mutants and potential cult activity simultaneously as the manufactorum’s sudden destruction occurs — Inquisitors know that coincidences are often anything but.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}: The party’s Patron has received a tip that the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#the-vylathi-knives]{Vylathi Knives} are making a big play in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. Rumours say they are setting up an unsanctioned manufacturing facility on a larger scale than ever before attempted. The party is tasked with finding out if this is true and, if the Knives won't cut your Patron in for a share, ensure this operation meets with an accident of its own. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasties}: The party’s Patron recently made a deal with the overseers of Manufactorum Vitus-II to supply their family with various rejuvenat reagents. They would dearly like to know who is responsible for destroying the manufactorum, and ideally, recover the chemicals they’d been promised.

Depending on a Patron’s Motivation, the following may also be suitable:

  • Conflict: Conflict breeds strength, and discovering who is responsible for this mess before the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} can is just the sort of rivalry to demonstrate this sentiment.

  • Information: A potential attack on a rejuvenat manufactorum? The repercussions are too vast among the upper echelons of the hive for this to be a random attack.

  • Materiel: The chemical precursor agent produced at the manufactorum was of great value, as are the extended lives of those judged worthy to receive it. If the destruction was deliberate, these valuable chemicals may have been stolen before the destruction. Find and secure them.

  • Reputation: Several recent attacks on important manufactorums have conveyed that these vital pieces of Imperial infrastructure are vulnerable. Discovering the culprits will disabuse others of this notion and build the Patron’s reputation as a result.

  • Unity:  Exploding manufactorums hardly speak of a unified, secure hive. Moreover, the shortage of rejuvenating chemicals, though likely temporary, already has many of the hive’s upper crust at each other’s throats. A rapid, accurate investigation may go some way towards remedying this.

A Tech-Priest vanishes in the wake of a manufactorum explosion, leaving it to the party to unravel a conspiracy of revenge, corruption, and horrible experimentation. Illicit Fabrications can be used as a stand-alone experience played over 2–3 sessions or as part of a larger campaign.

A thick choking smog rolls through the chaotic morass of makeshift habs, flowing like gaseous sludge from the vast exhaust vents of massive manufactorums looming high above. Weary faces peer between the gaps in corrugated panels while filthy, shoeless figures dig for scraps in the waste. Despite the disorientation caused by smog and dust pooling in the sickly light of ancient, dimming lumens.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Vand’}s makeshift shack is a rusting collection of sheet metal nested among the walkways and corridors of a massive crumbling hab building. The man is paranoid and will not allow anyone to enter before identifying themselves, though characters can make a Routine (+20) Athletics (Might) Test to send the ramshackle door flying inwards. Assuming they do not enter by force, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Barsis Vand} offers the characters a swig of surprisingly good spirits from a dirty glass bottle. With introductions made and social obligations performed, he provides them with the following information:

‘An accident… You think an explosion that catastrophic would have happened with an Enginseer on site? It was sabotage! I was coming in for my shift, and I saw them heading into the manufactorum, armed to the teeth and carrying Militarum munitions crates. It was the Vylathi Knives, by their tattoos. I managed to keep my distance and stay out of sight, and then I saw the explosions. I’d bet it was the chems they were after… thieving, throne-cursed ganger scum.’

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Barsis Vand} (Calis DeGuar) is omitting his position as former Overseer and his dealings with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#the-vylathi-knives]{Vylathi Knives}, but his story is essentially true; he watched the whole thing unfold from a vid-screen in his former workstation. Characters can make a Hard (−20) Intuition (Human) Test to confirm his intentions, but only succeeding with 3 SL or more reveals that Vand is holding something back. Regardless, Vand suggests that the characters investigate the manufactorum for themselves if they have not already done so. If the characters ask Vand any other questions, he answers everything honestly so long as it doesn’t jeopardise his disguise.

Recovery Protocol 

The party had best interview @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Vand} with some haste, as they are not the only ones looking for him. As soon as the characters have gotten everything they can from Vand, or if they have begun to accuse him of duplicity openly, their attention is drawn to events beyond the ramshackle walls of the shack.

A clamour of raised voices and commotion from outside turns to screams, and the unmistakable roar-hiss of a plasma discharge erupts from beyond the shack’s thin walls. A gurgled cry cuts through the din as @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Vand} rushes to the wall. Peering between metal plates, his eyes go wide, and he speaks one word, ‘Mechanicus.’ 

The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} has begun its search for @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx}, the Tech-Priest who was supposedly killed in the explosion at Manufactorum Vitus-II. Strange energy emissions indicate to them that the Tech-Priest is still alive, though his location is difficult to determine. Shack by shack, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o]{Skitarii Vanguard} file workers outside, scattering belongings and lining them up in densely packed groups while a tall @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.vsiOALilPnEe3dKg]{Skitarii Vanguard Alpha} with an elaborate plasma pistol approaches. Close by, a worker’s corpse smoulders, a length of plasteel rebar presumably wielded as a weapon now fused to his blistered hand in an ashen death grip.

Depending on their preference and their Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, the characters are likely to choose one of two paths — flight or negotiation.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Vand} makes his preference clear by peeling back a panel at the rear of his shack, allowing their escape, stating he has somewhere he can hide out if the characters have been courteous toward him, or attempting to sneak away if they have not.

Alternatively, the party may attempt to leave the shack and deal directly with the Skitarii forces. In this area of the Lower Hive habs, they are led by Landa-12, a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.vsiOALilPnEe3dKg]{Skitarii Vanguard Alpha} whose body is far more machine than flesh. Landa-12’s command protocols have been set at their most severe and uncompromising, leaving the cybernetic warrior with little room for compassion or understanding, even towards others affiliated with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. Unless a character, or their Patron, has at least 3 Influence with the Adeptus Mechanicus, Landa-12 treats the party as potential suspects and questions them to determine if they are harbouring the vanished Tech-Priest.

These mostly amount to ‘Are you aware of the location of Tech-Priest Tyberis,’ followed by the coda, ‘Answer truthfully. I am empowered to execute anyone I suspect of lying, as even erroneous executions will encourage others to be more forthcoming.’

Events should not result in violence towards the characters unless the party chooses to escalate matters or if they refuse to consent to a search of their personal belongings. Somewhat ironically, even if they or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Vand} are otherwise behaving suspiciously, the Skitarii are ill-equipped to notice anything that falls outside their strictly encoded objectives.

However their encounter with the Skitarii resolves, the characters are left with a cold and stern warning from Landa-12. Until the fate of @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx} is determined, Manufactorum Vitus-II and the surrounding hab areas are under the complete jurisdiction of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. The vanguard will not be so lenient with them in future encounters, and their presence in the area is more pronounced.

Under the Radar

Should the characters choose to flee, or if they return to the Lower Hive habs later in this adventure, you may use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.yxEXWbQdSsRMtDcS]{Skitarii Occupation Encounters} Table to generate some events for them to encounter. While fleeing the Skitarii in this instance, one or two events are sufficient. These should be used to enhance the character of the decrepit habs and slums, but should not be deployed as combat encounters unless your party appears to enjoy carving their way through random gangers! Some encounters on the Table may prove helpful if you need to provide an ailing party with additional clues.

While the Skitarii patrols take a brutally efficient approach in dealing with any resistance, their protocols emphasise detainment and questioning over outright execution. These patrols comprise around two to four @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o]{Skitarii Vanguard}. If the characters are concerned about or soon to lose a fight with a group of Skitarii, their foes demand their surrender in clipped, augmented voices. If the characters become captured, refer to @UUID[.XeypfEF1bMJE0BmC#detainment-breach]{Detainment Breach}. If not, proceed to @UUID[.XeypfEF1bMJE0BmC#the-manufactorum-ruins]{The Manufactorum Ruins}.

Detainment Breach

Large, close-topped, cylindrical vats floored in rockcrete gravel bear fresh plasma-cut entryways bolted tightly with welded rebar cage doors. Blinking controls lock each door, beyond which two gun servitors patrol back and forth. A third unarmed servitor is slaved to a cogitator a short distance away, connected by long snaking cables to the walls, receiving and executing commands every few minutes.

If a Skitarii patrol captures the characters, they are dragged to their base of operations — the top floors of a colossal hab unit they’ve seized for their operation at the edge of the Lower Hive hab slums. Citizens in the lower levels have been ordered to stay indoors, and Servo-skulls patrol the corridors. Guarded Skorpius transports surround the building’s base, and Archeopters come and go, landing on the roof.

As their equipment is being seized, each character may attempt a Challenging (+0) Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) Test to hide one item from their inventory about their person, gaining Advantage if that item has the Subtle Trait or is otherwise small, or Disadvantage if attempting to conceal an item with the Heavy Trait. The rest of their equipment is inspected and diligently catalogued by the Tech-Priests — they thoroughly remove power cells from weapons inspect every corner of any container, all the while chanting benedictions to calm the machine spirits.

After the characters are locked up, the Skitarii Vanguard receive a vox transmission and leave abruptly, choosing to interrogate the party later. They leave behind a pair of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.KTlRprKRb8XzlnAD]{Gun Servitors} to watch over the prisoners.

Before any escape attempt can be made, the detainees in the next makeshift cell ask the characters who they are and what they were arrested for. These prisoners, Selto and Henn (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial Citizen} stat-block to represent them), are part of @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ]{Varik’s scavenger company} and were taken during the Mechanicum’s sweep of the blast site. They tell the party they’ve been trying to escape but haven’t figured out much except that the gun servitors are programmed to shoot on movement — they noticed one obliterate some local vermin earlier.

You should be generous in allowing the characters to arrange their own escape. The gun servitors shoot at anything that moves outside the cells unless it bears specific @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} markings. They could be tricked by throwing a small item towards a nearby cogitator, blasting it apart and opening the doors in the process, but they can not fire upon each other. If they are made to engage more than three targets, they begin a rearming sequence, which takes the sluggish servitors three turns to complete. The cells could be unlocked by making a Challenging (+0) Dexterity (Lockpicking) or Tech (Security) Test. If the characters escape while the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.KTlRprKRb8XzlnAD]{Gun Servitors} are active and armed, the Servitors pursue them.

If the characters are at a complete loss, Selto and Henn chip in with suggestions or organise an escape themselves, freeing the party in the process (though only to act as targets for the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.KTlRprKRb8XzlnAD]{Gun Servitors}). If they assist the other prisoners in escaping, Selto and Henn put in a good word for the party with @UUID[.XeypfEF1bMJE0BmC#interviewing-varik]{Varik} (granting 1 Temporary Influence). Varik can be found in the @UUID[.XeypfEF1bMJE0BmC#the-manufactorum-ruins]{ruins of Manufactorum Vitus-II}.

The Manufactorum Ruins

The mouldering carcass of Manufactorum Vitus-II lies burst open, its blackened walls standing at odd angles, steel supports splayed like ribs of melted masonry ready to collapse. Glass and dust crunch on hardened pools of liquid metal and heat-fractured plascrete as Human scavengers pick through the bones.

As the party leaves the hab sprawl and approaches the shattered manufactorum, they encounter their first oddity before even setting foot in the ruins. A collection of stained red and white papers is scattered against the edge of a storage container as if blown by a powerful gust before settling in disarray. A Routine (+20) Logic (Investigation) Test reveals these to be used in the preparation of tabac, with the red staining a result of being dipped into some kind of liquid, probably intentionally. 

Entering the ruins, the characters notice the dozens of scavengers picking through the remains, their small, portable lumens bobbing in the darkness. They seem to take little heed of the party until a gruff voice barks, “Away, our salvage!” from the nearby shadows. The characters are momentarily blinded as an exceptionally bright light is activated and pointed at their faces. Varik, the leader of the scavenger crew (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.kdhQ2SwO7Vm2rzUI]{Gang Leader} stat-block to represent him), attempts to question the characters about their intentions. 

Varik’s sole purpose is to protect his claim on the scrap. Should the party explain they are not scavengers and not with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, or if they pass a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Charm) Test, Varik lowers the light and allows them to proceed. He warns them not to interfere with his operation. If the characters assisted Varik’s captured crew in @UUID[.XeypfEF1bMJE0BmC#detainment-breach]{escaping}, this goes much more smoothly, and Varik offers to help the party by answering any questions they may have. By looking around or asking Varik, the characters notice several clues presented in the Ruined Manufactorum Clues Table.

Ruined Manufactorum Clues

Clue

Description

Interpretation

Red Ration Papers

Distinct white and red papers lie scattered around the entrance. The explosion did not burn them up.

On inspection, they appear to be wrappers for rations — nutrition blocks that have been unwrapped and re-wrapped. An additional Routine (+20) Lore (Rokarth) Test reveals these are not standard issue from any known dispensary. Asking around the hab slums should uncover where this contraband came from (@UUID[.0E1byP7m6ewbH53O#the-dreg]{The Dreg}).

Shattered Supports

Massive macro support columns, which once supported the manufactorum, lie shattered.

Whatever destroyed these structures was a powerful explosive of some kind.

Bloodstain

Some isolated blood stains mark the ground in one location.

This blood is fresh and is, in fact, from Varik’s crew, who were arrested earlier. It draws attention to another point — no other Human remains are in the ruins. Varik or another passing scavenger confirms their crew hasn’t found any.

Battered Dataslate

A damaged dataslate still flickers with life, crammed with information about the manufactorum. It’s hard to know what’s pertinent to the investigation.

The Dataslate contains a wealth of information about Manufactorum Vitus-II, including details on the last work shift at the time of the explosion, the Overseer on duty DeGuar, and the precise chemicals being made there. A successful Challenging (+0) Tech (Engineering) or Logic (Investigation) Test reveals that these chemicals are mostly inert — it would take a monumental mistake to produce an explosion of the scale that occurred here accidentally.

Twisting Paths

Depending on the party’s choices, they may have arrived at the site of the manufactorum before visiting @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Barsis Vand} in @UUID[.XeypfEF1bMJE0BmC#under-the-radar]{his shack}, and, indeed, may be unaware that anyone survived the explosion. If this is the case, Varik can send the party to Vand, having heard that one lone survivor has emerged in the nearby slums, though Varik has no idea how anyone could have survived that blast.

Interviewing Varik

As long as they haven’t committed any acts of violence against him or his crew, Varik is willing to speak with the party. If not, they must coerce him into talking.

If asked about his captured scavengers, Varik informs the characters that the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} swept through several hours ago, occupying the site before taking Selto and Henn in for questioning.

Should the characters ask him about the strange ration papers, he states none of his crew can afford them, but he’s met a man called Datan who sells the black market rations. He’s set up most nights at a nearby fighting pit called ‘The Dreg’. The characters can spot Datan by the dirty red scarf he always wears, matching the colour of the wrappers.

As they speak with Varik, a distant scream is heard in the manufactorum ruins, prompting the scavengers to depart with their gains. Varik says some of his crew reported seeing a pale, sickly-looking creature haunting the ruins, possibly a mutant. They threw debris at the creature, prompting it to flee, screeching as it went. The scavengers have no desire to get a closer look at the thing. 

If the party wishes to, they can track the high-pitched agonising screams emanating through the darkness from the far edge of the ruins. As they approach, the screaming stops, but they find large bare footprints with far too many toes. The trail is impossible to follow as it appears the creature climbed over the rubble.

If he is taken alive, @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak}} pleads for his life. He promises the characters wealth and power, claiming connections with noble houses and extensive forbidden knowledge — all this is nothing but bluster aimed to save his own skin. Any examination of his purported connections reveals them to be a lie. His fate is at the character’s discretion, though if they do not prevent her from doing so, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Lerna Harrog} makes quick work of the man to fulfil her vendetta.

If rescued, Tech-Priest @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Arx} offers a stilted, emotionless expression of gratitude for the rescue. The Tech-Priest is not of any notable rank, but directs his thanks to the party member with the most artificial limbs and implants, assuming they are in charge of the group. If the party escorts Arx back to the Skitarii, who are still occupying the ruins on the surface, the characters are approached by Landa-12 and thanked for their aid and told to leave — about the warmest thanks they could expect from the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.vsiOALilPnEe3dKg]{Skitarii Alpha}. The Skitarii immediately call off their crackdown of the area and retreat to their base at the ruined manufactorum.

If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Lerna Harrog} survived, the party has a difficult choice. She is a mutant, abhorrent in the God-Emperor’s eyes, but has also offered extensive aid to the characters. Do they believe she is a traditional mutant or merely the victim of chemical misfortune? Undisturbed, she gives thanks and turns her back on the characters, making for the maintenance tunnels she has hidden in thus far.

Some NPCs the characters encountered could become valuable Contacts or Hirelings in their future adventures, such as Tech-Priest @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx} (if they successfully rescued him). Datan, Kem, Yarneg or Varik all have significant connections in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} underbelly (depending on who among them the characters left a favourable impression upon). Even the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o]{Skitarii Vanguard}, including their Alpha, Landa-12, could become a valuable contact if they were treated as more of an ally than a foe during the adventure.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Exposed Calis DeGaur's identity as Barsis Vand]{10 XP} if they exposed Calis DeGaur's identity as @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.gw1UiYXapR7TRNHF]{Barsis Vand}.

  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Defeated Kathor Navrak]{20 XP} for defeating @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak}.
