  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Recovered the Tech-Priest Tybaris Arx]{20 XP} for recovering the Tech-Priest @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx}.

Influence

Award or reduce the character's Personal Influence according to their behaviour towards the factions they have encountered — primarily the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} if they interacted with the Skitarii favourably, or ultimately rescued Tech-Priest @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx}. Consider Influence gains or reductions based on the significant number of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} NPCs they encounter; rumours of their deeds are bound to spread across the Lower Hive.

These increases can bleed over to their Patron’s Influences if they represented their Patron honourably or made such a gross error in judgment as to affect their Patron’s standings. Aim to award (or detract) at least one point to each character and their Patron.

Failure

@UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak}’s gangers eventually capture Calis DeGuar, and he quickly becomes one of Navrak’s ‘volunteers’. More mutants, akin to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL]{Lerna Harrog}, begin to appear in and around the manufactorum ruins, as Kathor Navrak continues his experiments, producing more failures than results. Eventually, he requires more labourers and test subjects and begins abducting citizens from the surrounding hive sectors.

The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o]{Skitarii Vanguard} continue their cold and calculated crackdown on the area. It takes them some time to find @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak}, but not before they’ve turned the surrounding hab blocks upside down looking for the source of @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#tech-priest-tybaris-arx]{Tybaris Arx}’s signal, harming local citizens’ perspectives of the machine cult, and causing manufactorum strikes in neighbouring hive sectors.

In between all this, citizens begin to abandon their habs in the surrounding area, wedged between @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak}’s abductions and the ongoing Skitarii crackdown. This sector of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} is scarred for years to come, before the efforts to rebuild the manufactorum truly begin.

What’s Next?

The end of this adventure has a few loose ends that could be spun into further adventures for your party. Consider the following:

  • The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#the-vylathi-knives]{Vylathi Knives} have learned what the party did to @UUID[.0Ozt4mfDwFIqYyBJ#kathor-navrak]{Kathor Navrak} and his wayward plans. Even though Navrak was ultimately a fool, the gang cannot afford any blemish on their influence. The Knives hunt down and purge the rest of Navrak’s crew, but their kill teams also set their sights on the party. Learning this, their Patron suggests they look into the rumoured connection between the gangers and House Vylathi, and uncover something they can use as leverage over the gang. 

  • Yarneg has set out to rebuild The Dreg in another sector of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Lower Hive, and may seek to cut the characters in on the deal. Except there is a problem: the area he aims to move into is controlled by an unsavoury cult. Whispers speak of them worshipping a twisted version of the God-Emperor (if Yarneg died during the adventure, then his role could be fulfilled by Kem, using his clout as a fighter to raise in social standing).

  • The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o]{Skitarii Vanguard} may call upon the party to aid them in future investigations, perhaps acknowledging their ability to parlay with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} citizenry effectively. After the destruction of Manufactorum Vitus-II, Forge Fane Incalcos-6 has put the maniple’s attention towards the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#the-vylathi-knives]{Vylathi Knives} and, by extension, House Vlyathi. The machine cult seeks to dissuade the Knives from ever treading upon their manufactorums ever again.

The auto quill scratches fitfully on the bone-white page as Curator Varness reviews the reports for the thirteenth time in two hours, yet the details remain the same. Then there are the picts, but she can’t deny them, though she’s tried. Having ruled out distortion, grime on the lens and atmospheric interference, she’s left with a single regretful conclusion: they’re real. As she scrubs all but a select few from the archive, acid rain lashes the narrow armaglass windows of her cramped quarters aboard the Interminable Devotion, beyond which the rolling fortresses’ harsh lumens reveal an expanse of inhospitable wasteland, corrosive fog and acidic devastation.

Designed for a party of low to moderately advanced characters, Interminable Devotion combines mystery, horror and investigation elements to tell a story of murder, conspiracy and familial hatreds. The party is tasked by their Patron to investigate a secretive research mission and soon find themselves pulled into the thick of a mysterious string of murders aboard an ancient Capitol Imperialis traversing Voll’s acidic wasteland.

@UUID[.gqWQ8LhVWHKBodFY]{Part 1: The Brunt of Voll} — After reaching the Interminable Devotion, the party discovers Captain Alarad Veridian’s corpse. Initially suspected of murder, they are soon vindicated and meet with Curator Varness, now the highest-ranking officer aboard the Devotion. After telling them about strange happenings, she charges them with finding the killer.

@UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR]{Part 2: Scrutiny and Suspicion} — The party begins their investigation, exploring the Devotion and talking to NPCs to uncover clues. As they progress, they’ll find new clues to help them solve the mystery, uncovering a dangerous chemical agent before building towards the final confrontation with the adventure’s villain, Vesterick Nethecaré. 

@UUID[.8OWiZxbLaURKKVKb]{Part 3: A Mind in Ruins} — Armed now with a trove of information, the party returns to the Curator and makes their case, only for calamity to erupt as a concentrated form of Vesterick Nethecaré’s agent is released aboard the Devotion. Upon making their way through the maddened decks, the characters must pursue the noble into the wasteland for the last confrontation.

@UUID[.MbWSJCh5GLhtUKvE]{Aftermath} — With Vesterick Nethecaré defeated and his plan foiled, the party may recover or destroy the formula for the noxious chemical agent he had used upon the crew. Upon returning to the Devotion, the party calls for extraction. 

Vesterick Nethecaré

Vesterick Nethecaré was born into a decrepit, precarious branch of the vaulted House Nethecaré, the family name, while enough to raise him above the teeming filth and grant him a life amongst the smog-choked spires of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal}, it granted him little else. His young life was tense, ever wondering if the rest of the brood might tire of his family’s drain on the Nethecaré coffers and see fit instead to prune them. Yet this all changed with the death of his father. 

Hundar Nethecaré left to attend a meeting and never returned. Despite a body never surfacing, he was swiftly declared dead, and a cursory memorial followed. After the mandatory mourning period was observed, Vesterick Nethecaré’s mother was quickly married to Gruledis Nethecaré — his grand-uncle from his father’s side of the family. Technically, this was a vast leap in status for the lesser noble and his mother, but his grand-uncle’s heirs ensured Vesterick Nethecaré never forgot the stain he was on the Nethecaré name. This atmosphere of ridicule and derision pushed the young man to work tirelessly to prove his worth and master the House trade. No gene went unmapped or cell unturned from the meagre remnants he was permitted to work with. Years passed without success, yet everything changed the night of the test. 

Bitter and frustrated at the stark variables presented by his test thralls, the noble took rash action, injecting himself with an unknown concoction of potent hallucinogens and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }pheromones. The room spun, his perceptions reeled, he stumbled and fell as strange noises and hallucinations began to scurry and flutter in his periphery. Then he saw a vision.

Vesterick Nethecaré gasped as, amongst the melting walls, crawling things and disembodied laughter, a twisted figure emerged, Human flesh mingled with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi} biology, yet the face was unmistakable; it was his father. 

Vesterick Nethecaré fell back in horror, yet the monstrous revenant pushed forward, mandibles clacking so close to his face that he could smell the reeking spittle, then he began to speak. Several hours later, Vesterick Nethecaré awoke to his lab in ruins. He and his equipment lay broken, notes were scattered, and his hands were bloody, yet one thing caught his eye above all else. On the floor, written in blood, was a nearly complete chemical formula, one he believed allowed him to commune with the dead.

But he knew the formula needed more testing and resources than the house would allow. In his father’s notes, he learned about the Interminable Devotion and how it had fallen under the sway of the chem guild in their ongoing expeditions, and as a source of collecting the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }pheromone that his formula required. Vesterick Nethecaré saw an opportunity; he would go right to the source and continue his experiments far from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} in an enclosed environment. He would perfect his formula, commune with his father again, and show House Nethecaré his worth.

The Last Living Castle

The Interminable Devotion, a retrofitted Capitol Imperialis, grinds through Voll’s acid wastes on tracks large enough to crush buildings to dust. It currently shelters hundreds of souls deployed on a privately funded research mission. The veteran engine has a long history dating back to the Macharian Crusade — it was initially deployed as a mobile fortress for Imperial Knights and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} walker squads who hunted the planet’s once abundant strains of colossal @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}. It could withstand the brunt of their monstrous attacks, provide ample artillery support, and transport their prized carcasses for study.

Even with the decline in colossal @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, the Interminable Devotion still soldiers on across the wastes, surveying spawning grounds for signs of reemergence and catching strains for research. Some among the crew think it has been lost somewhere in the Departmento Munitorum’s records, or, while revered as an engine of war, deemed too burdensome to transport off Voll to a new battlefront. However, they still recognise how much of an honour it is to serve on such an ancient Imperialis.

Centuries exposed to Voll’s rigours have not been kind to its internal workings. Despite recent and arcane maintenance rites performed by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} personnel regarding its environmental systems, many lie marred beyond repair. Perhaps worst of all is the inert macrocannon that juts at its zenith, the once-impressive armament serving as a symbol of power now lost to the ages. Yet even so, the mobile fortress is far from defenceless. Stalling due to engine failure or track damage is a constant threat, but there is little short of concentrated heavy ordinance that can pose the Devotion serious peril from the outside. Inside, however, is another matter entirely.

Chemical Communion

‘Through snaking pipelines and rusted vents, Vesterick Nethecaré’s chemical communion slithers its gaseous form through the Devotions bones, infiltrating every passage, occupying every chamber as vast as the Hangar, as minute as the smallest runoff grate, a hidden spectre, invisible and everywhere’.

This potent nerve agent, rendered from toxic fungi, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }pheromones and refined neural secretions quietly builds in the subject’s system, inducing paranoia and conjuring disturbing hallucinations before culminating in explosions of apoplectic violence. The Interminable Devotion possesses a bespoke filtration and air supply system to combat Voll’s hazardous environment — the perfect place, so contained and off the grid, for the noble to experiment with his chemical communion.

Mixed with the standard oxygen supply, the chemical communion is impossible to detect on any craft systems, and there is no central source for any curious menial to blunder into. Vesterick Nethecaré himself has tampered with the equipment aboard to avoid any interference. For example, all rebreathers and protective gear aboard have been carefully and undetectably damaged to ensure the crew’s exposure. Despite preventative measures, tar-like build-ups have congealed in the Devotions’ air filters. Should a character possess the knowledge or tools to analyse this substance, they may attempt a Hard (+20) Logic (Investigation) Test. If they succeed, inform them of the following:

CLUE: The residue appears to have congealed from an airborne substance synthesised from acynadi pheromones. An extended analysis with lab equipment would be required to unravel its secrets fully. However, it’s likely to have hallucinogenic properties. It’s pretty likely this substance has been leaking outside the Devotion. This could account for much of the strange acynadi behaviour surrounding the craft.

Vesterick Nethecaré believes his deceased father has supplied the formula for his chemical communion and that he can commune with him while under its hallucinogenic effects. The noble has built up a tolerance to the communion, allowing him to withstand constant mild exposure while aboard the Devotion. Additionally, he has devised grenades that hold a concentrated form of the communion along with syringes loaded with a similar liquid solution. 

Contamination

During the adventure, the party is passively exposed to Vesterick Nethecaré’s chemical communion via the Devotions' air supply. Ask the characters to make Fortitude Tests at various points in the adventure (do not invoke the Poison specialisation as it might give the game away!). The following list covers some suggested points in the narrative to ask for these Tests, but it rather depends on how long your characters spend on the Interminable Devotion trying to figure out the mystery.

  • At the end of Part 1 (when the party is detained in the brig).

  • After they have investigated a few locations in Part 2.

  • After they have investigated a few more locations in Part 2 (see @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#time-for-communion]{Time for Communion}).

  • As they race through the Devotion in Part 3.

As their exposure to the chemical increases, the Difficulty of these Fortitude Tests also increases.

  • During Part 1: Routine (+20)

  • During Part 2: Challenging (+0) 

  • During Part 3: Hard (−20) 

Among the characters who fail these Tests, choose someone who rolled the least SL. They experience some form of auditory or visual hallucination. See the Auditory Hallucinations and Visual Hallucinations Tables for some ideas for what characters could experience under the effects of contamination — but any of these suggestions can be improved by adding aspects of NPCs who are important to the characters, especially anyone who has passed away; family, friends, lost comrades and the like (much like how Vesterick Nethecaré saw visions of his dead father when first exposed).

Furthermore, any character who fails two of these Tests in a row begins to suffer severely from the chemical communion. They effectively have the Fatigued Condition, rolling all Tests with Disadvantage, until they can breathe clean air once more (either by fixed breathing apparatus, spending time outside the Devotion, or fixing Vesterick Nethecaré’s sabotage of the air systems).

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.w6qJK8mdonMAPkSG noCenter=true description=bottom]{Hallucination}

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.Gl7QDuzJmGGFTiLg noCenter=true description=bottom]{Hallucination}

At this point, the party should have enough information to suspect that @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} is behind the murders and is currently posing as @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}. If not, use the following events to bring the investigation forward:

  • If they decide to search the Interminable Devotion for @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos}, who keeps dodging their presence, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} can slip up in his imitations of the sergeant over the vox by giving incorrect details or acting rashly. If you need to press the point, members of Drukos’ squad could approach the Party asking if they’ve seen him.

  • If @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} is still alive, they’ll have inspected the Medicae’s (Drukos’) body and concluded that the corpse is @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}, adding that the Medicae has been missing all day.

  • If none of the above works, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} calls the party to her cabin for a progress report, after which you can begin the following scenes.

The party must present their findings to @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness}. She thinks the idea of a hidden Nethecaré noble being responsible is initially preposterous. Unbeknownst to the party, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} is listening in through the small vox receiver he hid in her augmentic hand some time ago under the guise of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick}.

The party meeting with @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Varness} triggers the climax of the adventure. Once finished stating their case, but before the party leaves the Curator’s cabin, the chamber is swallowed in darkness before red emergency lights kick in. Then the craft-wide vox crackles, and the following can be heard.

‘My my, aren’t you the clever little lab rats? Unfortunately for you, you still find yourselves within my maze and I can’t have you scuttling off and spoiling things, there are grander things at work here.’ 

Then the groaning sound of aching metal splits the air as the Devotion rocks sharply. Each character must make a Challenging (+0) Athletics (Climbing) Test or be knocked Prone and suffer 3 Damage. The vox then crackles again, the voice now frantic, rapturous even. 

‘He’s come… he’s finally come for me… he’s come to save me… father, I’m here!... Let this be my parting gift to you. The formula works! Breathe in the blessing of chemical communion!’  

A hiss sounds as a pungent, sickly sweet odour fills the air. The characters must make a Hard (−20) Fortitude (Poison) Test as @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} releases his communion at full concentration aboard the Devotion (see @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#contamination]{Contamination}). 

‘Curator Varness races to her cogitator, typing frantically. ‘Something has crippled the Devotion’s left track. We’re paralysed,’ she coughs. ‘And that bastard might have sealed us in, but if we can get down to the Hangar, we should be able to release that door manually.’  

Vesterick's Plotting

As the characters cobble together their last clues and present their findings to @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness}, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} has put his final plans into motion. Hiding between the Devotion’s decks and crawlspaces, he has created the final form of his chemical communion and has set it up to distribute throughout the Capitol Imperialis’s air filtration system.

At the same time, the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }outside the Devotion have continued to swarm towards it. All this time, some of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s chemical communion has been leaking from the Capitol Imperialis, the pheromone component within the formula has been attracting the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}. A behemoth-sized, latently psychic, and unclassified acynadi is about to strike the Interminable Devotion. 

When @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} sees this colossal @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi} coming, he believes his father has come back for him, and seeks to escape the Imperialis and meet him in the nearby ruins.

Rush to Save the Crew

The party is challenged to descend through the Devotion’s decks as chemical-induced madness overtakes the crew. Their goal is to reach the Hangar and vent the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} from the Devotion’s decks (if they do not think of this solution, Varness can pose it to them). If they have a workable solution of their own design, use the following encounters to hamper their movement towards their goal.

In each challenge, failure causes the character to make another Hard (−20) Fortitude (Poison) Test to resist the@UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{ chemical communion}.

‘Beyond the Curators’ cabin, the sound of maddened screams and gunfire fills the Militarum Deck as manic mercenaries fire at one another and things only they seem to see.’ 

In this first challenge, the characters need to avoid or confront the mercenaries. They could make a Challenging (+0) Reflexes (Dodge) or Stealth (Move Silently) Test to avoid them, or find a different route with a Challenging (+0) Navigation (Tracking) or Tech (Engineering) to find an alternate route. Treat the corridors as a Minor Hazard if the characters fail their Tests.

‘Passing down a stairwell, another shudder rocks the Devotion as something batters it from outside threatening to send you all tumbling down the narrow metal stairs.’ 

In this second challenge, the characters need to pass a Hard (−20) Athletics (Climbing) or Fortitude (Endurance) Test to stay on their feet. If they fail they fall Prone and take Damage equal to their negative SL.

‘Entering the Habitation Deck you see huge gangs of menials running through the passages, jagged metal and tools in their blood slick hands. Howling like beasts they drag a screaming scribe out from under a bunk and bludgeon him to death.’ 

In this third challenge, the characters can choose to aid the captured scribe, or continue on to keep pace. If they choose to aid the scribe, they’ll fall behind and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} will get to the Hangar release before them (described at the end of these encounters), and they’ll be forced to make another Hard (−20) Fortitude (Poison) Test to resist the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} for lingering. Otherwise ask them to make a Test similar to the first challenge to avoid the mob, but the area is considered a Major Hazard if they fail.

‘Reaching the Enginarium Deck you see menials and haywire servitors thrashing about, under the effects of the chemical communion. Some are crowding near the hangar door’s control console, and they notice you.’ 

In this fourth challenge, the characters are confronted by two menials (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourer} stat-block to represent them) and two @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.px7pplClKR01chqM]{Servitor}. Under the effects of the chemical communion, they attack randomly, perhaps even each other, and all Tests against them are at Advantage. The characters are four Zones away from the door controls, located up a small gantry way next to the door aperture. They can avoid the assailants and reach the hangar’s door control console by making a Difficult (−10) Athletics (Climbing) or Reflexes (Dodge) Test instead, but failing causes them to fall into the fight.

No test is needed to activate the door’s release mechanism, so long as someone reaches it and hits the clearly marked button, then proceed to the next section.

Old Hinji’s Fate

If the characters do not make it there in time, or all succumb to the effects of the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} comes to the crew’s rescue in their stead. He senses his way to the Hangar and releases the hangar door, allowing the toxic gas to drain from the Devotion’s decks.

The party finds him next to the hangar door console on the brink of death, having been pushed to his limit. Only a Very Hard (−30) Medicae (Human) Test can stabilise him, otherwise he’ll promptly die after relaying the following information.

If the characters made it to the hangar door console in time, they’ll find Old Hinji nearby; exhausted. He’ll need medicae attention, but no Test is required to stabilise him.

@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji }tells the party he ran into @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick} (@UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}) on his way to the Hangar, and has some vital information for them: 

‘Ruins outside, he said he was going to meet his father in the ruins’. 

The chemical communion vents out of the Interminable Devotion, but at the same time, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }of various sizes begin to enter the Hangar from outside, investigating the source of the airborne pheramones (mostly tiny variants and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.7F9x6CZCJCp0IV6b]{Acynadi Beta-3}, among a few more ornery @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5}). The characters can aid in setting up barricades and warding the enemy tide off, or you can skip to the next section; some of the Devotion’s security and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49}’s servitors come to do the job regardless.

Stalled in the Wastes

Regrouping with @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varnes}s, she speculates how @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} could have known they were on to him. If the characters do not search her office or augmetic arm for the hidden vox caster, Varness discovers it alone. She curses herself as a fool and destroys the device. 

She relays the state of the Devotion to the characters. Whatever hit the Capitol Imperialis caused the ancient engine to stall, and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49} is working to get it moving again. They won’t be underway for some time. Regardless, the crew is in shambles. Their minds are broken, and many of them are dead. Anyone still alive is fending off the stray @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }who scuttled aboard or is patching up the engine.

To gain some form of victory from this ordeal, the Curator presses the party to finish their job and chase down @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} once and for all. She hands them a report formed from the Devotion’s augur scans, and only one patch of ruins is nearby, marked on an attached map. They have a moment to catch their breath but must make haste to find the madman.

The Ruins

Leaving the Devotion and emerging into the storm-wracked acidic wilderness, the party’s portable lumens soon reveal dozens of huge depressions scattered around the side of the Capitol Imperialis. These are immense footprints, each at least twenty feet wide, leading out into the dark. Armed with a data slate loaded with geographic reconnaissance data, the party knows the ruins aren’t far. 

The area is filled with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, though they are more interested in getting into the Devotion than getting in the character’s way. They reach the edge of the ruins unhampered, read or paraphrase the following:

‘Sharp lines of acidic rain cut through the bright beams of your portable lumens as you see them, rotten and fang-like. Ragged stone structures, broken and ruined, leer out of the storm forming angular walls, crumbled pillars and sharp-edged obelisks.’ 

They should easily notice that no @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }are in the ruins, as if they won’t step inside. The few they see seem to stand still at the edge. As they move deeper, the outcrops of stones grow closer together until something resembling a massive ruined structure looms out of the dark, its huge circular entryway yawning like a vast, hungry maw. Read or paraphrase the following:

‘The winding passages terminate in a huge circular chamber, its domed ceiling, cracked and broken, looms precariously as the storm winds whip through in a series of keening howls. Huge, crumbling pillars dominate the space in a forest of shattered stone while at the centre a raised dias supports an altar inlaid with strange spirals.’

Investigating the Ruins

The characters should be making haste to confront @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}, but if any of them halt to glance at the ruins, you can reveal some of the following information.

  • Apart from the crumbling parts of the structure, none of the ruins’s architecture present seams or breaks between the stonework, seeming impossible to construct by conventional imperial means.

  • The only markings on the ruins surfaces (walls and floors) are strange, spiral-like indentations; some are small, thumb-sized spirals, others take up entire spans of rock.

  • The stone appears incredibly acid-resistant. Unlike imperial construction, there are no acid-markings from centuries of being submerged in Voll’s acidic swampland.

Once inside the inner chamber, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} makes his presence known, stepping onto the raised dais at the chamber's centre. He insults the party, mocking them for their stupidity as he hid right under their noses. As his madness and paranoia come to the fore, read aloud or paraphrase the following:

‘They sent you to ruin this for me, didn't they? Didn't they?! Who was it? My Uncle? One of his heirs? They’ve always tried to keep me down, pushing my nose into the dirt so they can laugh like I wasn't a Nethecaré! But not anymore! I’ve solved the formula! The chemical communion! My formula will bring the house to new heights!’ Behind him, heavy, thunderous, plodding steps approach the ruins, shaking the earth and threatening everyone to their knees. Vesterick cackles madly, withdrawing an odd-looking grenade. ‘You see! Father is coming, father is coming to rescue me!’ He pulls the pin on the grenade, dropping it at his feet. It releases a thick plume of orange gas as he vanishes into the forest of pillars.’

Once among the pillars, characters can attempt to make a Challenging (+0) Perception (Sight) Test to search for @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}. Should they be successful, they hear the unmistakable click of a pin being pulled from a grenade before a sudden plume of bright orange gas erupts around them. Characters must make a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Poison) Test to resist the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}. Any character who was successful in their Perception Test may make the Fortitude Test with Advantage as they anticipate the coming hazard. 

@UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} aims to attack those he’s afflicted with his chemical communion, evading the party until he can get the drop on them. Three rounds after combat begins, as the heavy footsteps grow closer, the following occurs:

‘The colossal thumping footsteps now hammer the ground beyond the chamber’s walls, each thunderous boom louder than the storm as the ground trembles. Something huge beyond reckoning and dark as the night smashes a section of the domed ceiling, sending large chunks of stone plummeting to the floor.’

The party must make a Challenging (+0) Reflexes (Dodge) Test to avoid the falling stone. On a failure, they are knocked Prone and suffer 5 Damage. All Zones gain the Lightly Obscured Environmental Trait from all the silt and debris kicked up into the air. Meanwhile, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} continues to evade the party as best he can in the same manner as before. Debris continues to fall into different Zones for another two rounds, then the following occurs: 

‘A horrible scream cuts through the din, and you see Vesterick Nethecaré, his legs pinned beneath a heavy piece of rubble. ‘Father,’ he screams. ‘Father, please help me!’ As if beckoned by his call, a huge tentacular claw emerges from the shadowed canopy beyond the dome. Slimy, glistening and dotted with small bioluminescent pits so synonymous with deep water acynadi. It reaches towards him.’

The party can react in a number of ways, but make it clear to them that they only have six rounds to escape the ruins unscathed:

They may wish to free @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} from the rubble and take him back to the Interminable Devotion, to answer for his crimes and face the God-Emperor’s justice. Freeing him requires an extended Hard (+20) Athletics (Might) Group Test, requiring 8 total SL to succeed. The party has three rounds in which to succeed in freeing Vesterick Nethecaré before the giant creature seizes him and draws him out into the blackness beyond the ruins.

However, the party may wish to escape right away, as it should be clear that the ceiling has become critically unstable. Fleeing the ruins requires a Routine (−20) Reflexes (Dodge) or Athletics (Running) Test as they move around the falling debris. They need to succeed at this Test twice to escape individually. If they are dragging @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} along, the Difficulty of these Tests increases to Hard (+20). Failing this Test, a chunk of debris hits them for 3 Damage, or on a Critical Failure, they are also knocked Prone.

If the party takes any opportunity to go through @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s possessions, they find a dataslate detailing the formula for his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} along with three of his remaining gas grenades.

As the party emerges into the wilderness, the ruined structure behind them crumbles as they narrowly avoid its total collapse. As the dust cloud subsides, they notice all the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }that had gathered are now gone. Furthermore to their relief the storm seems to be moving off and the sky begins to brighten. Read aloud or paraphrase the following:

‘The raging storm seems to shift to the west away from the Interminable Devotion and deeper into the barren acidic wasteland. The darkness within the lashing tempest seems to swallow the oncoming landscape under the shrouding pressure of its heavy clouds. Yet every so often a flash of lightning illuminates that dark inner world and in its after image you see a shape, vast and monolithic, moving in its blackened depths.’

With the storm moving the characters see salvation nearby in the proud defiant shape of the Interminable Devotion, its armored battlements dominating the landscape, beckoning them to return to safety.

With @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} defeated or lost, his plan foiled, and the formula for his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} recovered or destroyed, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} and the reputation of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#nethecare]{House Nerthecaré} have been spared horrific damage. The party can return to the Interminable Devotion and contact their Patron for extraction. @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness}, if she is in good standing with the party, will back their version of events and thank the party for thwarting Vesterick Nethecaré’s plan.

The characters make arrangements to recover the Capitol Imperialis if their Patron tasked them to do so. However, if they do not, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49} contacts his superiors, and the craft is eventually recovered by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} before undergoing a significant retrofit for future deployment. Some NPCs the characters encountered could become Contacts or available as hirelings in their future adventures, such as @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji}.

Experience Points

All characters should earn @Reward[xp=30 reason=Interminable Devotion]{30 XP} for participating in the adventure. If any characters achieved personal goals or fulfilled a goal for their Patron, their reward should be increased accordingly. In addition, the following experience can be awarded:

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Reached the Interminable Devotion]{10 XP} for reaching the Interminable Devotion in Part 1.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason= Saved Scribe Hess]{10 XP} for saving @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} in Part 2.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Vented the chemical communion]{10 XP} for venting the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} in Part 3.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Figured out Medicae Roderick's true identity]{10 XP} for figuring out @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick}’s true identity.

  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Confronted Vesterick Nethecaré]{20 XP} for confronting @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} in the ruins.

  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Acquired or destroyed Vesterick Nethecaré formula]{20 XP} for acquiring or destroying @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s formula.

Influence

Award or reduce the character's Personal Influence according to their behaviour towards the factions they have encountered — primarily House Nethecaré as a result of sparing their reputation from their misbegotten sons' planned sabotage. Additionally, increase or reduce each character’s Personal Influence according to their behaviour and decisions surrounding the fate of NPCs who related to the wider factions at work throughout the Macharian Sector. These factions include the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists} (Trackless Chain). As a result these effects may in turn influence their Patron’s influences depending on their behavior. Aim to award (or detract) at least one point to each character and their Patron.

Failure

Should the party fail to capture or eliminate @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} before the massive creature he refers to as his ‘father’ can seize him, they must retreat from the crumbling ruins empty-handed. Leaving the rubble behind and despite seeing their adversary carried off by some gargantuan creature, the party won’t be able to shake the feeling that the noble is still out there.

@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji }reinforces this feeling, if he is still alive at this point in the adventure, who speaks it aloud to the party. Without Vesterick Nethecaré or the formula for his chemical communion, the party must trek back to the Devotion with a strange disquiet heavy in their guts.

Otherwise, there may be a chance that @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} is somewhat successful and escaped with his formula. The next time the party encounters the noble, it may be to thwart his plans to infect @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} with his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, turning the populace mad and drawing a massive population of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }to attack the hive.

What’s Next?

The end of this adventure has a few loose ends that could be spun into further adventures for your party. Consider the following:

  • The Interminable Devotion sits in ruins from the chaos that so recently wracked its decks. One of its vast tracks sprawls in broken disorder, while inside its mechanical guts, cables, relays and piping are laid bare. While the great engine has suffered extreme damage, it is not beyond repair. It would take a dedicated team and considerable resources to revive this iron leviathan — the race is on between the scavengers gangs, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#nethecare]{House Nethecaré} and the local @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}.

  • A whisper can be just as potent as any toxic chemical with a half-life powerful and persistent enough to cause a fallout. Upon returning to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, some of the Devotion’s survivors have been less than tight-lipped about what happened. Most were unaware of any noble involvement, but rumours of strange @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }behaviour were rampant. Word has spread of a chemical that draws the typically skittish and hard-to-hunt acynadi together in large numbers. As a result, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleets} and acynadi hunting teams are already searching for it. Such an agent would be worth a fortune to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#carnem]{Mercador Carnem}, but in the wrong hands could spell disaster.

Fear and suspicion mount amongst a skeleton crew of distrustful souls toiling together within a venerable Capitol Imperialis while an underhanded enemy sets sinister plans in motion. Interminable Devotion is an adventure that can be used as a stand-alone experience, spanning 2–4 sessions or as a part of a larger campaign. Be sure to familiarise yourself with the various @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg]{Dramatis Personae}, as their interactions and confrontations with the party are key to how this adventure evolves.

The danger of the storm is apparent; attempting to fly through it would tempt death. However, vast eyes in the storm are observable, forming sizable islands of calm in the otherwise raging atmosphere. One is not far from the coordinates their Patron provided. This is the safest chance at reaching the surface intact.

Braving the Weather

‘The lander settles down upon the uneven surface and promptly sinks several feet into the mud below. Around you, an expanse of fetid acidic marshland stretches out to meet the borders of the swiftly approaching storm.’

The party is then confronted with obstacles on their journey to the Interminable Devotion. As they progress, take note of the SL of each roll they make, adding the party’s positive SLs together and subtracting negative SLs from the total. Upon reaching their destination, if the total is 6 SL or more, the party avoids obtaining the Fatigued (Minor) Condition. 

‘Exiting the lander, the storm engulfs you, smothering all natural light and leaving you to traverse the acidic marshland in storm-choked darkness. The howling wind and torrential acid rain lash you terribly, forcing you between jagged rock formations that quickly become labyrinthine.’

In this first challenge, characters must succeed on a Routine (+20) Awareness (Sight) Test with Advantage if they are working together as a group. Characters who fail take [[/r 1d10]] Damage from jagged rocks as they wander in the storm. 

CLUE: The characters with the most SL on the Awareness Test notice that these rock formations more closely resemble ruins, with markings and signs of structure evident.

'The terrain around you narrows into a sharp gully flanked by sheer cliffs on either side. Though sheltered from the wind, a strange mist thickens, and you soon come to a significant circular depression at least twenty feet across in which a caustic green liquid bubbles.'

In this second challenge, the party must succeed on a Challenging (+0) Athletics (Running) Test to jump over the depression. If a character fails, they suffer [[/r 1d10]] Damage from landing in the exceptionally corrosive substance.

'As the gully opens out once more, the wind howls in a terrible keening roar and from a ridge to your left dozens of terrified and disoriented acynadi spill over in a chaotic stampede, their alien forms flailing with barbs, spines and claws.'

In this third challenge, the party must succeed on a Routine (+20) Stealth (Move Silently) Test to avoid the frantic creatures; should any of them fail, two large @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5} attack them. 

'In a flash of lightning, the characters notice a colossal shadow on the far side of the ridge. It seems like a hill, then it begins to move, sinking back into the darkness of the storm. As you recover from the acynadi stampede, you see it, standing out in the black gulf of storm-wracked wasteland. A bank of lights, yet even at this distance, its source is clear. The Interminable Devotion.'

The party makes their last push through the open to reach the Devotion. If any character suffered 7 or more Damage from the three challenges, they receives the Poisoned (Minor) Condition, and their extreme weather clothing has been damaged to the point it no longer protects them from the toxic conditions. Also count up their total SL from all three challenges and inflict them with the Fatigued (Minor) Condition as previously described.

Read or paraphrase the following:

’A mobile fortress, ancient and colossal towers before you. A retrofitted Capitol Imperialis, the Interminable Devotion boasts fifty-meter-high battlements, potent weaponry and tracks large enough to level small buildings. Its huge disembarkation ramp yawns open before you.’

Safe Harbour

Upon entering the Hangar, the party finds that the heavy lumens have been deactivated. The massive hangar door is open, and an @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter} is visible nearby. Should they investigate the Hangar further, they discover the corpse of Captain Alard Veridian. Read aloud or paraphrase the following:

‘Slumped against a storage locker, you see the body of an ageing man in a large pool of blood, a discarded laspistol at his side. His pale, bloodless features locked in silent terror above his utterly crushed throat.’

Immediately, the sound of an opening bulkhead accompanies heavy bootsteps. @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos} and ten of his mercenaries enter the Hangar (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Trooper} stat-block to represent them. Drukos first asks the party if they are the work detail. But upon noticing the body, he and his men become aggressive, demanding they hand over their weapons before placing them under arrest for the murder of Captain Alrad Veridian.

The party is escorted to an ex-storage cabin turned brig, where @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos} questions them about the murder. Initially suspicious of the characters, he soon begins to believe their story but keeps them in the brig under heavy guard until he can investigate. As they leave, the massive hangar ramp retracts, and the Interminable Devotion gets back underway.

What happened?

During a routine medicae check, Medicae Roderick (or rather @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}) took the opportunity to secretly inject the Captain with his latest batch of his concentrated @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}. Driven by visions and paranoia, the Captain called for the Interminable Devotion to a complete stop, and attempted to leave alone on the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-requisition.actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter} they keep for emergencies. 

Having bugged Captain Veridian to monitor the effects of his formula, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} was forewarned of his plan, and he intercepted the Captain in the Hangar, accompanied by one of his Medicae Servitors. He ordered the Servitor to kill the Captain to cover his tracks, then to hide the murder weapon, subsequently ordered the Servitor to disappear into the wastes while the Devotion was stationary. The noble managed to return to the Medicae Ward without being noticed.

Hours pass, allowing the party to rest before Drukos returns, where he informs the party that they are cleared of his suspicions. The Devotion’s augur scans detected their landing craft, and the adepts’ medicae report states time of death as just before they touched down. Drukos then tells them that @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} wants to speak with them and leads them to the Curator’s Quarters. Once inside, she asks the party for their account while dismissing @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}. With him gone, she promptly states the following. 

‘Peculiar occurrences have been reported and duly suppressed for several weeks now. Strange reports of seeing frightful things aboard, distorted acynadi that look partly Human. This is ludicrous; the reporters have been disciplined and told to keep quiet. But the reports keep coming in, and they are all so similar. Then there’s the picts.’ The @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator} turns her cogitator display to show a pict of hundreds of acynadi lying still, just beyond the edge of the Devotion’s heavy lumens. ‘They seem to be flocking or gathering and following the Devotion as if waiting for something…’

‘I have suppressed the reports and the picts as much as possible to avoid hysteria amongst the crew, yet now with the murder of the Captain, something needs to be done. You seem like capable individuals, and seeing as you arrived after the murder, you are the only ones beyond my suspicion. So, as acting commander of this expedition, I’m charging you with spearheading this investigation. Whatever you find, you are to come to me here and present your evidence before I will authorise the use of any force. The last thing we want is a bloodbath.’

The party receives a handheld vox, the authority to question the crew and any previously confiscated weapons. If any characters are unarmed, they are given two common weapons of their choice from the Devotion’s armoury (Imperium Maledictum). @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} suggests beginning with the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#a1.-hangar]{crime scene}, the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b1.-the-medicae-ward]{Medicae Ward} or asking around in @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b2.-the-mess]{the Mess}.

The adventure begins with their Patron’s briefing on the mission — they are provided with initial information on the expedition and their motivations for sending them to investigate. Their Patron also supplies them with the following equipment to aid them in their adventure. 

Extreme Weather Clothing

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.items.Item.zyIQkeHkEhcRn2Gu]{Extreme Weather Clothing} grants the wearer +1 SL on Fortitude (Endurance) Tests to resist the types of extreme weather the clothing is designed to protect against. In this instance, they are provided with coverings and cloaks that protect them from Voll's acidic rainfall and atmosphere.

The party has an opportunity to gather anything they require before departing, but their Patron insists they must leave before the end of the day. They have been provided with aerial transport to reach the last known coordinates of the expedition — if they are in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, their transport departs from the mid-levels of the Void Buttress.

A few hours after takeoff, nearing the landing site, their flight encounters a savage storm that has swallowed the area, complicating their landing.

Patrons

Understanding the players’ Patron’s involvement in seeking out the Interminable Devotion is key to kicking off the adventure. Below are suggested motivations for each Faction:

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}: Your Patron has received word that several archives have been redacted without proper authorisation. Further digging has uncovered fragmented information that, when pieced together, points to a private Nethecaré expedition into Voll’s wilderness. This breach of protocol must be investigated. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}: Your Patron has encountered strange fragments of disturbing beastial imagery clinging to the astropathic currents near Voll’s wastes. The source of this interference must be determined. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}: Your Patron has uncovered evidence of a Capitol Imperialis at work on Voll, upon cross-referencing its idents with Mechanicum records, the engine was designated killed in action over a century ago; the fate of such a relic must be confirmed. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}: Your Patron has received intel about a Nethecaré noble who claimed they can speak to the dead. This man, one Vesterick Nethecaré, has recently departed @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} on a secretive research mission. Whatever madness is at hand affronts the God-Emperor’s Holy Ministorum.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}: Your Patron has heard rumours that several deserters have formed a mercenary company on Voll. After applying the correct pressure, it was uncovered that the deserters' ringleader, a man named Drukos, is stationed aboard a secretive Nethecaré research craft. This coward must face the God-Emperor’s justice for his crimes.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}: Your Patron has intercepted a short-wave vox message cast out into the void. While heavily corrupted with vox distortion, a ‘Captain Alrad Veridian’ requests immediate extraction from an isolated region of Voll, providing specific coordinates.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}: Your Patron has received a tip on the whereabouts of a former associate who cleaned out three gambling dens and skipped planet with the winnings. The cheater has acquired false papers under the name ‘Hinji’, working for a shady Nethecaré research expedition in Voll’s wastes. Find him and settle the score; the house never loses. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}: The Inquisition’s eyes and ears have collated many rumours regarding rogue Nethecaré chemists and supposed prophets who can speak to the dead — this all reeks of heresy, and it all points to the wayward Capitol Imperialis.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasties}: Your Patron’s curiosity has been stoked upon discovering records of rare chemicals changing hands tied to a secretive Nethecaré research mission. Investigate this curio, and recover anything that might be of value. 

Depending on a Patron’s Motivation, the following may also be suitable:

  • Conflict: Discover whoever leads this secretive mission, put them down for their deceit, and set the Interminable Devotion back to its regular patrol.

  • Information: Such a well-occluded expedition must surely have valuable secrets. Retrieve all data on the expedition's elusive goal and its findings.

  • Materiel: Such a shady expedition is likely to have brought in any number of valuable resources off record, not to mention their objective. Secure any notable assets for future use. 

  • Reputation: Expose this secretive expedition so that others think twice before attempting such clandestine operations. 

  • Unity: If others expose this expedition’s underhanded nature, it will only create further distrust; investigate and resolve it quietly to avoid potential conflict.

The Interminable Devotion shelters some two hundred souls from the storm-wracked darkness beyond its walls. Some are major players who influence the ebb and flow of power upon the craft, while others fade into the faceless morass of downtrodden souls. Each major character holds information that can inform the party of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s presence and agenda. 

Apart from these characters, the Interminable Devotion is crewed by a mix of menials (@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers}), @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.px7pplClKR01chqM]{Servitors}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adepts}, and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Troopers}.

Curator Varness

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.Dhe0z7z8c9ZFDeM0 description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Curator Varness}

Roleplaying the Curator 

As this is her first senior post, the Curator is eager to do well and to put forward an air of authority and unflappable leadership. However, she fears that she is far out of her depth. Initially, she is curt and to the point, providing only the information the party needs and supplying what is requested in as few words as possible. As the adventure moves on and pressure builds, the cracks in her mask begin to show. She becomes prone to barking orders and stumbling over her words.

The Curator takes to plying herself with amasec, resulting in an acrid smell that follows her like a cloud. She harbours an incredible fear of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}, heightened due to the effects of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}. If the party’s Patron is an Inquisitor, and Varness becomes aware of this fact, she aims to avoid speaking to the party, making it evident that she is hiding something. If pressed, she swiftly cracks and provides the clue below.

CLUE: Fearful of the Inquisition’s intervention, Varness destroyed almost all reports of strange phenomena recorded by the Devotion’s expedition and reported by the crew. The Curator then divulges that she formally held a low-ranking position and was given this assignment and rank by a mysterious benefactor. All paperwork was marked with a wax seal bearing the initials ‘V.N.’ (unaware it was Vesterick Nethecaré).

Mathus-49

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Curator Varness}

Medicae Roderick

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Medicae Roderick}

Roleplaying Medicae Roderick

When roleplaying Medicae Roderick, you are roleplaying a disguise of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}. He has become a talented mimic and has had long years to perfect his guise as the kindly old Medicae, he can still occasionally slip into older, more typically highborn speech patterns. Medicae Roderick is helpful and understanding, eager to assist when troubles or ailments might be eased. As a result, he is a well-liked figure amongst the Devotion’s crew with a reputation for wisdom and warmth. Should he be questioned about advising @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Varness} to destroy reports, he states truthfully that he felt it was in the expedition’s best interests. 

As the story progresses, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} usurps @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}’s identity to cover his tracks. Think of this as another mask behind which the same character you have been portraying already hides. You may even drop subtle hints after this event occurs, such as Drukos’s renowned grim demeanour being broken by the odd jovial remark or helpful offer as Vesterick Nethecaré struggles to break the habits of his former guise.

CLUE: Should the players wish to cast a critical eye over Roderick, they may make a Routine (+20) Intuition (People) Test. Upon success, they realise that on occasion, how the Medicae orders his words is somewhat elaborate, extravagant even, almost as if he were of noble birth.

Menial Boris

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.XfuOWlQ5fvUgtElU description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Menial Boris}

Old Hinji

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Old Hinji}

Roleplaying Old Hinji

Despite his impairments, Old Hinji is a jovial and animated fellow fond of chatter and eager to find ears to listen to him. He happily wiles away the hours discussing almost anything with anyone, especially when a strong drink is offered. He is also an infamous gambler, the only crewman to have never lost a game of ‘Dagger Counts’ in @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b2.-the-mess]{the Mess}.

Most write off the old man’s attachment to @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b2.-the-mess]{the Mess} to his love of drinking and gambling; however, Old Hinji sticks close to the Mess because he fears being alone. Though unaware of his psychic potential, due to the effects of the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, he believes that a strange @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }presence is calling out to him. Immersing himself in the chatter of the Mess drones out the worst of it. Yet many of these delusions persist and spinning them into tales is the only way he can manage to cope.

Spending any significant time with Old Hinji, he tells the characters the following tale. 

CLUE: ‘There was a boy once… a boy that lived in high towers, sharp as knives and tall as the clouds. Yet the folk he lived with were sharper still, and they did away with this father and married his mother off to some lord or other… t’was his kin that did it… Wretched doings, and the boy never got over it. He spoke to the shadows that come about when you’re at that sort of business… but he never could feel any better, I think his mind ‘as gone a bit rotten now… poor lad… I just hope he doesn’t hurt anyone.’

Scribe Hess

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Scribe Hess}

Sergeant Drukos

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Sergeant Drukos}

Roleplaying Sergeant Drukos

Having secured such a lucrative contract for him and his men in an out-of-the-way place with so little risk feels almost too good to be true. As a result, Drukos takes his position as sergeant quite seriously, eager to get this mission done, enjoy his earnings and secure potential future employment. 

Yet all of this fine luck is not enough to lift his spirits. The threat of his past lingers like a ghost in the back of his mind. He’s paranoid that one day he will be discovered by the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} for desertion. then it will be his skull getting the last las-round. Drukos will not easily give up the information about his shady past unless persuaded with a Hard (−20) Rapport (Charm) Test or confronted with hard evidence. The characters can find this evidence if they notice the inconsistencies found in the personnel files in the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#a2.-central-cogitarum]{Cogitarum}, granting the following clue.

CLUE: Drukos and his mercenaries are deserters of the Astra Militarum. Having only secured this contract by the aid of a mysterious benefactor who provided falsified papers and identity tags. These documents were marked with a wax seal bearing the initials V.N. (once more standing for Vesterick Nethecaré).

The characters can now explore the decks and interact with the Devotion’s various NPCs, piecing together initial clues and suspicions. There is no set path for the order of the investigation. As clues are discovered, the scenarios provided trigger, each providing the party with an additional clue to help solve the mystery.

Remember that @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} has rigged the Devotion’s air supply with his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, and has bugged many of the key locations and NPCs across the Capitol Imperialis to keep an ear on the key members of the crew and observe the effects of his chemical communion from afar, which means he can often stay one step ahead of the characters once they are aboard.

The Interminable Devotion

The Capitol Imperialis is arranged into three primary decks from bottom to top.

A. Enginarium Deck — (bottom) the Hangar and primary engines.

B. Habitation Deck — (middle) the Barracks and other crew services.

C. Militarum Deck — (top) the Bridge and other administrative cabins.

Throughout the decks are plentiful gun emplacements and battlements. Not listed but still worth considering is the topmost deck located above the Militarum Deck. This deck consists of the upper battlements, where the macrocannon sits (currently needing extensive repair), a small observation nest, and a landing pad for flyers.

Throughout the Capitol Imperialis, the interior is constantly tight, like the innards of a voidship, with plenty of turns and overhangs that characters can hit their heads on. The Hangar is the largest open space aboard, multi-levelled and accessed externally from the front or the rear of the Imperialis. It can hold multiple tanks, walkers, and even flyers simultaneously.

A. Enginarium Deck

Flickering red lumens dully illuminate a snaking labyrinth of steaming pipes, ribbed cables and coolant tubes, as footsteps of servitors and menials alike echo metallically from the walkways and gantries beyond.

Sections of the Interminable Devotion’s engines are spread across this deck, bisected by the massive multi-tiered central hangar. Tightly packed engines and constructs constantly whirr and strain, spitting out steam and crackles of electricity — the servitors at work are programmed to ignore the obvious hazard, but the party should be well advised to keep their hands at their sides while passing through.

A1. Hangar

Towering crates and stacks of steel barrels form a series of high walls around lines of metal storage lockers where data slates stand racked in steel housing.

The Hangar is a huge bulk storage area buried in the dimly lit guts of the Devotion’s Enginarium Deck. Where once the grind of battle tanks and the lockstep of guardsmen echoed in the space, the Hangar is now an area that few frequent and those that must, do so swiftly. The sound of footfalls resounds loudly on the metal decking, and the towering walls of supplies cast thick shadows. The party can find a reliquary of data slates. If they inspect the data, they uncover the following clue. 

CLUE: The records state that a locker was accessed just before the Captain’s estimated time of death. Inside is a small bloodstained data coil. Upon loading it into a cogitator, they find a report requesting the termination of the expedition, stating initial reconnaissance data was falsified, implicating the initials ‘V.N.’ along with copies of official documents tallying losses from a battle forty years ago. These include a record of the destruction of a Capitol Imperialis designated the ‘Interminable Devotion’.

If the party examines other data slate entries for anything unusual, they can make a Routine (+20) Tech (Security) Test. Upon success, supply them with the following clue.

CLUE: A particular report details a recent withdrawal. It is notated and logged on the supply manifest as a withdrawal of ink and parchment. However, only the stores of pain meds and bandages have been reduced. Someone has been stealing medical supplies.

If the party inspects or takes items stored within the Hangar, they find it well stocked with stacks of tools and clothing of Common availability (Imperium Maledictum). Should any characters look for weapons or armour, they find none stored within the Hangar, as all such items are firmly locked within the armoury on the Militarum Deck. 

A2. Central Cogitarum 

Pale-faced scribes and grotesque servitors hunch over banks of cogitators and auspex scanners underlit by the harsh blue light of their instruments. Curator Varness’s imposing command throne looms over a large holographic display, projecting the wasteland beyond the Devotion’s walls.

Embedded near the Devotion’s core, the Central Cogitarum never sleeps. As a facility wholly dedicated to information storage and exchange, this feretory is where most of the expedition’s data is enshrined. Should a character inspect one of the cogitators, they can open and examine several different archives, as follows.

Personnel Files

The party quickly finds that many of these are incomplete, with whole areas missing, and many are marked with a seal bearing the initials ‘V.N.’ Characters can make a Routine (+20) Logic (Investigation) Test to reveal the following clue. 

CLUE: You soon uncover inconsistencies that strongly suggest the files surrounding Drukos and his men are forgeries, along with patchy service records that imply a former militarum affiliation. 

Initial Survey Data

The expedition’s initial survey data is an archive of the original data supplied to justify the mission. It details vast @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }population numbers, tolerable climate pH levels and theories of surviving infrastructure. Glancing over this data reveals the following clue.

CLUE: It quickly becomes clear to the party that this information is so blatantly incorrect that it is likely to have been intentionally falsified. 

Pict Records

Inside the Devotion’s pict store, the party finds a horde of grainy images depicting misty acidic marshland and strange desolate ruins. However, something becomes apparent as they flip through them and gain the following clue.

CLUE: Flipping through the picts you notice images of the same locations captured at different time stamps. However, the landscape seems to change dramatically in some of the picts with a large dark hill appearing out of the mist time and time again, almost as if it were following the Devotion. 

If characters question any of the scribes about the strange information contained within the records, many admit that they had noticed the same irregularities. However, it is not within their remit to question superiors, but they have inquired about the strange pictures. Despite the honesty of this statement, the party gets a sense that they are holding something back. They can make a Routine (+20) Rapport (Inquiry) Test to gain the following clue.

CLUE: The scribes unwittingly or maliciously reveal that they believe Curator Varness is underqualified for her post and, as a result, has been unable to perform her duties to a routine standard.

A3. The Artificery

Large steel tables support several workstations where incomplete servitor arms and other more unrecognisable devices lie strewn. Racked banks of cogitators display complex graphs and binaric readouts while loose chains and thick steel hoists hang from the chamber ceiling in a foliage of rusted metal.

In the guts of the Enginarium Deck lies the personal quarters of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49}, the Devotions’ sole Tech-Priest. Effectively a shrine to the Omnissiah, the crew generally regards it as something more akin to a repair station, much to Mathus-49’s chagrin. Characters can use this area and the tools available to repair or maintain their equipment, but the Tech-Priest will surely approach them if they linger too long.

B. Habitation Deck

Cold lumens punctuate the gloomy corridors with harsh white beams as the drunken clamour echoes from off-duty crew. Behind closed doors, the cramped crew cabins are packed with stacked bunks bearing the rust and acidic stains of decades of service.

The Habitation Deck consists of staff and barrack cabins, mostly cramped cabins stuck between blocks of machinery and battlements, where most of the crew spend most of their time off duty.

B1. The Medicae Ward

The smell of antiseptic gels and coagulants saturates your nostrils with a stinging tang. Against the left wall, a dozen beds are laid out upon a grimy tile floor set with rusting drains. A brown plastic curtain partially covers a narrow passage through which a surgical table and medical supplies are visible.

If this is the party’s first time entering the ward, they find @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick} and his attendants finishing a bloody amputation. If this is their first time meeting him, the medicae will introduce himself. Ushering them into his surgical theatre, Captain Veridian’s corpse is laid out under a sheet. If the party asks about the autopsy, Medicare Roderick truthfully corroborates his adept’s findings — it appears the Captain died from his crushed throat, inflicted by some mechanical tool. However, he has only given the body a cursory once-over himself, with a complete autopsy to be performed in time. He also informs the party that the Captain’s effects are in a box on the shelf. Roderick then excuses himself to attend to his other patients.

Should the party wish to examine the Captain’s corpse, they may attempt a Routine (+20) Medicae (Human) Test. If they succeed, they are supplied with the following additional clues. 

CLUE: Upon examining the body, the party discovers shredded pieces of flesh beneath the Captain’s fingernails, whether his own or someone else’s, it cannot be deduced. 

CLUE: Furthermore, you discover what appears to be a small bruise on the Captain's arm, indicative of an injection site. 

If Roderick is informed of these details, he scolds his adepts and servitors for their foolishness and compliments the characters for their diligence. 

Should the party wish to examine the Captain’s effects, they find a heavily stained yet unremarkable @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} uniform, a pair of boots and a silver ring.

If the characters want to search the rest of the Medicae Ward for clues, they may attempt a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test. Upon success, supply them with the following clue. 

CLUE: Looking through the various files and cabinets, you find a book that doesn’t fit. This tome is bound in the finest polished leather, its pages gilded with glittering gold edges. Inside, you find flowing embellished script forming a strange dialect of High Gothic. If a character has the Linguistics (High Gothic) Specialisation, they discover it is a historical text detailing the family tree of House Nethecaré. If questioned, Medicae Roderick states that he has a great interest in the histories of Volls' noble families, particularly house Nethecaré, as he does have a distant familial connection to the house.

Should the party scrutinise @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick} further, a character can attempt a Challenging (+0) Intuition (People) Test. On a success, they suspect that he is withholding something. 

B2. The Mess

‘The bitter odour of stale grog hangs heavy in the air, and though the mugs are rusted and the lumens flicker, it’s the only place on the Devotion with any sense of levity. A scattering of stools surrounds oblong tables leading up to a corroded counter that stretches the length of the far wall.’
