The adventure begins with the characters receiving a message and accompanying papers from their Patron. The characters are assumed to already be in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, but their Patron’s message could reach them elsewhere if necessary and direct them to Voll’s capital. Depending on the Patron, this might come via a written message slipped under a door, delivered by a Servo-Skull, or some other means.

Considering the Patron’s origins and motivations, you may wish to adapt the following text before reading aloud:

‘I have arranged for you to meet Lord Felputh and provided you with the necessary papers. This minor noble has had trouble overseeing his manufactorum. It has ceased operations, risking Rokarth’s fulfilment of the tithe. Your task is to establish the nature of the problem for Lord Felputh and offer him guidance so that he can rectify the situation. Additionally, you should determine the extent of the noble’s failings and report back to me. The affairs of Rokarth’s elite are rarely simple, and knowledge of his affairs might prove valuable.’

Patrons

There might be many reasons why the characters’ Patron sends them to meet @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}. The noble may have contacted the Patron for aid, or the Patron has their own motivation for interfering, and the noble remains ignorant of their interest until the players arrive. The following are suggestions for each Patron Faction:

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}: If the Patron is Tithe Prefectus, then @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} likely begged them for mercy, afraid he would be unable to meet his quota. In this case, he had no choice but to agree to the players’ visit, but received them reluctantly.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}: Aware of the true purpose of Maltus Refinery VI and its mysterious product, the Patron knows it’s paramount that the refinery resumes production. This information is highly classified, something the party will never know.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}: Magos Vark alerted the Patron to the situation, and no member of the Adeptus Mechanicus is comfortable with the thought that Maltus Refinery VI remain unused. Imperial machinery must be maintained to serve its purpose, and this manufactorum is in dire need of attention.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}: @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} was once known for his generosity to the Ministorum, but as his fortunes have fallen, his faith too seems to have waned. Recognising his ancestral house, the Patron intends to give the lord a chance to redeem himself and set the situation right.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}: What seems a minor inconvenience today, a few snatched citizens or a minor rebellion among manufactorum workers, might become a significant threat to the Imperium tomorrow.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}: Any situation that affects the regular flow of goods to and from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}is likely to catch the attention of the party’s Patron. Significant disruption along the supply chain could eventually impact the imperial fleet’s departure schedules.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}: The Patron has identified @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} as a potential ally, customer, or target of extortion. Even a minor noble has wealth and connections that could prove useful, and this one is clearly desperate.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}: No one is above the Inquisition, and whatever the Patron’s Ordo they’ve been watching @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} from afar for some time. When a noble becomes desperate they’re most likely to succumb to the many vices and temptations of the Imperium’s enemies. If there is evidence of corruption in the refinery, its owner must be held responsible.

  • @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasty:} While it’s not for the players to know, their Patron’s Dynasty or connections played a part in arranging the mysterious shipment that brought @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} his new workforce. By sending the players to investigate, their Patron hopes to demonstrate their own innocence.

Depending on a Patron’s Motivation, the following may also be suitable:

  • Conflict: If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} cannot keep the refinery operational, then he has already failed in his duty to the God-Emperor. The situation should be swiftly rectified, the noble’s infirmities exposed, and normal operations restored.

  • Information: Knowledge is power, and power over a noble, even one as minor as @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, is desirable. This Patron may rather prevent the lord’s fall for the moment. He may have assets, contacts, and inside knowledge of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} noble houses worth extracting first.

  • Materiel: The Patron may take a personal interest in the produce of the refinery, and the wealth it brings its owner. Holding leverage over @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} is appealing, or — if the Patron has the power to do so — confiscating the refinery might be preferable.

  • Reputation: The greater the degradation of the refinery, the more appealing its restoration to Imperial greatness. If Chaos, xenos, or some other foul enemy of the Imperium has taken root, purging that enemy should bolster the Patron’s reputation, especially if the situation is dire.

  • Unity: Everything about this case makes the Patron uncomfortable. Tithes should not go unfulfilled, refineries should not lie unused, and nobles of any sort should not sink below their station. The Patron won’t be satisfied until the status quo is restored.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s compound is among the Hive Spires, in the exclusive, well-defended upper-class echelons of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. If the characters haven’t been to the Hive Spires before, they travel by maglift from the upper hive, and their entry should be challenged by a pair of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT]{Macharian Vigilites}. The papers they carry are genuine, but unless the characters appear to belong in the Hive Spires, the Vigilites may require some persuasion (or a bribe) to let them through unhindered.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s address, in the Steeple district, is on the papers. Two of his household guards are stationed at the entrance. They are ex-militarum and can be represented by the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Trooper}, though they carry no grenades, and their armour is a bright magenta. The characters must convince the guards they have an appointment; they’re viewed with suspicion despite their proper papers. In any case, before being admitted to the atrium, they are instructed to remove their weapons as well as their acid-stained outer garments and footwear.

Beyond the atrium, a vast echoing hall awaits. A shrine to the God-Emperor looms over the characters from the far end, and doors on either side lead into the rest of the building. Unless the characters try the doors, they won’t realise they are false. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felput}h had to sell much of his ancestral compound to pay debts and maintain his staff, so he’s gone to great pains to ensure his home still appears far larger than it is.

Here they are met by a black-clad woman, decked with knives and twin autopistols hanging unobstructed from her belt. This is @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik}. She ignores any questions and leads them through one of the many doors, into a small chamber. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} is waiting here, sitting on a throne-like chair behind an armaglass screen (the screen provides him with an additional 5 Armour).

Interviewing Lord Felputh

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} takes the characters’ papers and presents them to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, slipping them through a box in the protective screen. The noble scrutinises them before welcoming the characters and thanking them for coming to his aid. He plays the part of a concerned ruler deeply troubled by what might have happened at the plant. He claims his problems are caused by a worker uprising, though if pressed, he admits that the speed at which it happened and the lack of any demands make this seem somewhat unlikely. He mentions that @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Brandt Kesker} was stirring up so much trouble among the former workers that Felputh was forced to replace them all.

If the players ask more about @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker}, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} tells them the labourer is likely living in the habsprawl near the refinery, since he graciously allowed the workers to continue living there despite being unable to employ them any longer. If the players ask why the workers caused trouble or why he could no longer use them, Felputh admits there was some trouble with conditions at the plant, but the Magos who inspected it assured him that no urgent repairs were necessary. If questioned further, Felputh supplies the name of the Magos, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.fdJv9lqD4Nr2SAQz]{Elipses Vark}, who now works in Forge-Fane Incalcos-6 (located among @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Hive Spires).

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} is grateful to the characters for looking into his problem and insists they take @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} with them as a guide and protector (if they manage to refuse, Sandik follows them from a stealthy distance). He asks that they don’t linger in his home, however, as the presence of such ‘visitors’ might invite suspicion.

While Felputh is keen for the characters to leave, they might wish to question his household guards on the way out. They initially seem reluctant to talk, but if the characters speak to one out of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik}’s hearing, the guard reveals what they know: @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} has been docking their pay for the most minor of infringements recently, and the guards are concerned that his wealth, and therefore their livelihood, are at risk. Always a paranoid employer, the noble has been especially fearful of late, and his moods have become more erratic. The trouble with the refinery has made him desperate, and possibly dangerous.

Interviewing Magos Elipses Vark

The characters may wish to seek out @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.fdJv9lqD4Nr2SAQz]{Magos Elipses Vark} at Forge-Fane Incalcos-6. If they ask for Vark directly, they are told to wait outside, as the Tech-Priests have no intention of admitting outsiders to the Forge-Fane. After an hour of waiting, the Magos, along with a pair of armed servitors, meets with the party just beyond the gates, that seal shut abruptly behind him. He only has time to answer a few questions before excusing himself to return to his work.

Forge-Fane Incalcos-6 is detailed in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf]{Rokarth: A Guide to the Hive}. It is the sanctum mechanicum of the Cult of Mars in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, where the highest-ranking Tech-Priests in Rokarth pursue their essential and esoteric works. It is a veritable fort of knowledge; even Tech-Priests and Tech-adepts within the Adeptus Mechanicus have trouble accessing the building.

From Vark, the characters can learn about his inspection of the refinery. No urgent repairs were required, but plenty of minor ones could have been hurried along if @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} had been willing to make an appropriate donation to the Tech-Priesthood of Mars. Vark expresses concern that Felputh was more concerned with fulfilling the tithe than appeasing the machine-spirits. He believes the conditions of the refinery must be so poor by now that no Humans could possibly work there safely. Vark would be grateful if the party could ensure the refinery is restored and put back to work — the machine spirits should not be left to degrade in such a way. If the characters agree to help, Vark mentions that the ventilation shafts might provide a good vantage to survey the refinery itself, should they need to.

Interviewing Brandt Kesker

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Brandt Kesker} is the last thread they can chase before heading to the Refinery. Travelling to the Lower Hive from the Hive Spires takes the characters the better part of a day, so they may wish to prepare or rest before taking on the next part of the adventure. 

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} can be found in the crumbling habsprawls surrounding the Refinery, but it takes the characters some effort to locate him directly. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik} has some idea of where he is — remember that she is accompanying the party or following them from the shadows. Otherwise, they’ll need to interview other citizens to find their way. They can make Challenging (+0) Logic (Investigation), Navigation (Surface), or Rapport (Inquiry) Tests to gather information. Failure means lost time, adding several hours to their search and may cause them to become Fatigued.

They should notice that many of the local citizens here are suffering from a disease, revealed to be known as Bloodlung. These inhabitants can be represented by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers}, but they have an ongoing Poisoned (Minor) Condition. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} is in the final stages of the disease, lying on a bed of rags in the corner of a crowded hab. The other residents keep their distance, fearful of sharing his fate.

If asked about his supposed rebellion, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} says he got in trouble for daring to complain about the refinery conditions. He then escaped through one of the run-off pipes. His whole shift was dismissed as punishment. He doesn’t know who worked there afterwards, but is afraid they may have all perished there as the refinery is dangerously toxic. If the party can persuade him to speculate, he’ll tell them about the rumours that the whole place is staffed by mutants, but he finds this ridiculous, since surely even mutants can die.

Helping Kesker

If the characters can restore or shore up @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker}’s health, he is willing to accompany them to the manufactorum, usher them to the run-off pipe entrance and lead the characters around. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik} is opposed to this, saying he’s in such bad shape he’ll die before even getting there. In truth, she wishes to stay in better control of the situation and views Kesker as a wild card. If the characters do accept Kesker’s help, he’ll die soon after the adventure concludes, but may sacrifice himself using his I’ll Die Trying Trait.

Rumours that players might hear from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} or other locals are as follows:

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.No9sZ8JS0BvcygHQ noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumour}

Bloodlung

The lowliest inhabitants of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}are plagued with various conditions, infections, and diseases. Not all are named, but Bloodlung is well-known as a common affliction among refinery workers, likely as a result of their daily inhalation of poisonous vapours. The symptoms begin with a scratchy throat and dry cough, progress to painful, rattling lungs, and finally develop into a hacking, retching cough that brings up first blood, then partially dissolved lung tissue. Few live long after reaching this stage, and the Officio Medicae has no officially sanctioned cure.

If the characters spend too long in the refinery, they may begin to experience early symptoms themselves. If unprotected, after each encounter, characters should make a Difficult (−10) Fortitude (Endurance) Test. Any who fail become inflicted with the Poisoned (Minor) Condition for the remainder of the adventure, or until they receive treatment. Several quack cures are sold in the black markets of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}— some of these are useless but harmless, while others might make a character’s situation worse. It is at your discretion whether a character who tries one is cured or gains Corruption as a result.

Onto the Refinery

Maltus Refinery VI is within an hour’s walking distance of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Brandt Kesker}’s hab unit. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} can lead them there, or they can gain directions from local citizens. When they reach the refinery, read the following:

‘After pushing your way through the unwashed crowds of the Lower Hive, the sudden emptiness of the habways in front of Lord Felputh’s refinery is an ominous relief. Despite the distant rumble of the hive’s Generatorium, the manufactorum is unsettlingly quiet, embodied by a grave-like hush. Even with the refinery dormant, the heat remains intense, and the thick brownish air stings exposed skin. The ground is water-logged, and when flashes of the flickering lumens cast enough light, they reveal an oily scum floating on the surface. The towering iron gates rise before you, the welding that sealed them shut obvious from the lumpy scar of molten metal oozing and hardened through the gate’s central seal.’

The liquid at the characters’ feet is a corrosive but diluted acid. It’s essentially harmless, but it means there’s little evidence to find, other than some organic matter slowly melting that might once have been part of a limb. Examining the gates, they can make a Challenging (+0) Lore (Forbidden) Test to identify what has been scrawled upon them. What initially looks like rusted patches are in fact symbols painted in blood, in effigy of the eight-pointed mark of Chaos.

The gates are a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.zQYkbNcsJmGintdL#barrier]{Barrier} that can be surmounted by a Hard (−20) Athletics (Climbing) Test or by dealing 20 Damage targeted at the welded area in the middle. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} discourages using this entry, as making any noise or climbing over might alert whatever is inside. This method causes a party of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} to attack soon after they enter the refinery.

If the characters heard about the ventilation shafts from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.fdJv9lqD4Nr2SAQz]{Vark} or the run-off pipes from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker}, they can locate these entrances without the need for a Test. Otherwise, searching for one of these entrances requires making a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) or Navigation (Surface) Test. Failure means the party could take some Damage from traversing the area or alert the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} within if they make too much noise. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} is reluctant to help here, wary of dredging through the runoff, but follows the players if they find a way to enter.

Maltus Refinery VI is an enormous, ancient refinery in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} Lower Hive. The sprawling mass of furnaces, storage tanks, refining mechanisms and pumping stations is fully enclosed within its walls. There was no relief from the blistering heat, poisonous smoke, and thunderous noise while the manufactorum was in operation. Pipes and funnels carried away waste products, and the mysterious produce of its workings rolled out in barrels stamped with the Cog Mechanicum. The refinery operated monotonously for generations, regardless of the labourers who were mangled in its workings or died slowly of Bloodlung as they worked.

Though the refinery now lies quiet, the evidence of its centuries of industry shows everywhere. Every surface is thick with toxic filth, every pipe drips noxious fluids, or bears the strange whorls left by swirling gases. Some parts of the refinery are multi-levelled, standing on unsteady metal mesh floors, while other sections are more open, dominated by towering storage tanks or processing units. In some areas, lights are dim due to staining and corrosion, creating only a sickly orange glow. In others, there’s no light at all. Energy still being drawn from the Generatorum fizzes and pops among the refinery’s oily cogs and blood-stained wheels, vainly waiting for the machinery to move again.

If the party forced or surmounted the front gate to enter, they are immediately attacked by a horde of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} double the number of characters in the party. If broken open, a pair of Beastmen work to hastily re-seal or barricade the gates behind them.

If the characters entered via the , read the following:

‘After climbing up through the shafts, you reach an opening in the ceiling of the refinery and find yourself looking down at a gargantuan drum of black liquid. There appears to be no other way down other than by the rungs of a rusted ladder. Your hands have become coated in oily residue from the shaft, making it hard to grip; slipping here could be fatal.’

The characters must lower themselves 100 feet to land on a gangway; the ladder down is usable but slippery, requiring a Challenging (+0) Athletics (Climbing) Test. Any character who fails falls into one of the vats below, each full of an unpleasantly slimy, foul-smelling but harmless liquid. This fall shouldn’t inflict any Damage or Conditions, but feel free to improvise a drawback for failure. From there, climbing down to the refinery floor puts the players at the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1a.-wrecked-machinery-floor]{Wrecked Machinery Floor (1A)}.

If the players entered via the Run-off Pipes, read the following:

‘After trudging through the pipes, small enough that the tallest among you were forced to walk bent forward, you find yourselves in a large square container with a thick layer of neon purple sludge coating the metallic walls, and pooling at your feet.’

This container is 7 feet high, and the metallic walls have been reinforced with iron strips and thick bolts that make exiting an Easy (+40) Athletics (Climbing) Test. However, the purple slime is a poisonous residue. Unless the characters protect their flesh, each must make a Difficult (−10) Fortitude Test or receive the Poisoned (Minor) Condition for the next two hours. Exiting the container brings the characters next to the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1d.-desecrated-shrine]{Desecrated Shrine (1D)}.

Once in the refinery, distant explosions echo through the cavernous space. These are the result of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s agents cutting off their exits. The characters won’t discover this unless @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} becomes an ally and warns them, or they try to leave the refinery via the ventilation shafts or run-off pipes. They then find these destroyed, their exits irrevocably blocked.

Use the diagram to inform the characters of the nearest structures to their location so they can choose which areas to explore. Each labelled location is described in the following section. In addition, random encounter tables are also provided to increase the difficulty or extend the length of this part of the adventure. You may include as many or as few of these as necessary. The only information the players need to gain here is that the refinery is full of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} who worship Chaos, which should quickly become apparent.

If the players need reminding of their objective, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} can prompt them that they are there to establish what has taken over the refinery and halted its operation, so they can aid @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} in fixing the problem. Once they’ve seen @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen}, however, Sandik’s objective is to trap or eliminate the characters and prevent them from exposing Lord Felputh’s shame. To conclude this part of the adventure, the characters must leave via the tunnel entrance at the north end of the refinery and enter the tunnels.

Sandik’s Mission

Once it’s clear that the characters are aware of the Chaos-worshipping Beastmen, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} is on the lookout for a way to sabotage the party’s efforts in order to cover @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s tracks. She may alert a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} patrol to their presence and flee herself, activate some machinery while they’re inside, or attempt to meet with a character alone and attack them. How dangerous and effective her efforts are is up to you.

However, once the party knows of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik}’s betrayal, she tries to save herself. In a pinch, she proposes a deal: If the party or their Patron can protect her from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh}, she’ll work with them, for at least as long as it takes to get out of the refinery.

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.10m912eLDoBpYITR noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumour}

Refinery Locations

During their traversal of the Maltus Refinery VI, be sure to convey to the party the sense of enormity within the facility and how multifaceted and confusing the surrounding machinery appears. The whole facility is littered with vats and broken machinery, and an eerie disquiet hangs in the air throughout, felt especially by any members of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus }present.

The party doesn’t need to visit all locations presented; be sure to lead them towards the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1e.-northern-tunnel-entrance]{Northern Tunnels Entrance (1E)} to enter the next section of the manufactorum. Use the encounters in the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.10m912eLDoBpYITR]{Maltus Refinery VI Encounters} Table to add complications to their travel between locations or punish them for failed Tests.

1A. Wrecked Machinery Floor

In this section of the manufactorum, most of the machinery has been damaged or destroyed. Investigating, it looks to have been battered and torn apart, and many pieces are missing. Characters can make a Hard (−20) Logic (Investigation) Test, depending on their successes, reveal to them the following clues:

  • 1–3 SL: A trail of wreckage leads north towards the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1e.-northern-tunnel-entrance]{Northern Tunnel Entrance (1E)}, via the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1d.-desecrated-shrine]{Descecrated Shrine (1D)}. Whatever was taken from here was dragged there (material the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} have used to create their cages and effigies in the tunnels).

    4–5 SL: Despite the wreckage, some tools and workbenches have been used recently. In particular, they find some long lengths of discarded metal that have been sharpened along one edge (some @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} have been constructing their @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.items.Item.tqGb4ULjvQP5x7AK]{Herdcrafted Cleavers} in this area).

    6+ SL: If the characters are yet to discover the Beastmen, they find a chunk of organic material stuck between an array of wrecked cogs. Inspected further, this is revealed to be a tip of some animal’s horn, a strange thing to find on Voll altogether (part of a Beastman’s horn that broke off in the assault on the machinery).

1B. The Pens

A large cage made of bent girders and lengths of sharp wire has been built against the wall of an enormous vertical drainage pipe. Several figures are visible through the twisted metal, but only one is upright. This is Bek, who has only recently been captured (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourer} stat-block to represent him). He begs the party to save him, and if they refuse to help, he intentionally screams to alert a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} patrol. The other four Human captives are either close to death or mortally wounded.

If the characters have decided to look for missing citizens from the surrounding area (mentioned in a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.No9sZ8JS0BvcygHQ]{rumour}), they’ve been stored here. Bek has no idea what the Beastmen need them for; only that a captive is retrieved from the pen every day or so and taken further into the facility.

1C. The Furnaces

Three starved-looking @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} huddle by a small fire they’ve started, surrounded by the cavernous furnaces. If the characters watch and listen, these Beastmen bemoan that their brethren have turned to Chaos, and consider their options now. If a character succeeds on a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Charm) Test, these Beastmen can be talked to and give information to the players, but they are too afraid to enter the tunnels. Otherwise, these Beastmen flee rather than put up a fight and disappear into the manufactorum’s maze of machinery. 

Critical Information

Talking to any of the Beastmen at The Furnaces, or any the party encounters in the Tunnels (such as @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.J8fomG1IJs18g3F5]{Gelka}, or even some exposition from @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore}) reveals to the party pieces of how the Beastmen got to the refinery — their capture from a Feral World, their travel across the Void in a Rogue Trader’s voidship, and their subsequent arrival at Maltus Refinery VI. This is vital information to pass on to the characters, as it implicates @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s complicity. If they fail to retrieve this information from the NPCs, the characters should be able to recover shipping logs from cogitators and paper records kept in the refinery that line up with rumours and speculation they might have acquired earlier. Hard evidence may be required or at least reinforce how they wish to deal with Lord Felputh at the end of the adventure.

1D. Desecrated Shrine

At the centre of the refinery, a labourer’s shrine to the Glorious God-Emperor has been reduced to rubble. The party can spend an hour to restore the shrine, and all involved recover one spent Fate (or gain one temporary Fate they can spend but not burn, which they can use until the end of the adventure). They can also automatically pass the next Test they make to resist Corruption. 

They also notice hoofed footprints in the dust and rubble that seem to be heading north towards the tunnel entrance.

1E. Northern Tunnel Entrance

A tunnel entrance at the northern end of the refinery is guarded by a pair of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen}, ones loyal to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore}. A smeared trail of blood, left by bodies being dragged below, mars the entrance. Skulls, spikes and chaotic effigies surround the entrance, marking the tunnel entrance as the entrance to their territory.

Once the characters find a way past the Beastmen guards here, whether by defeating or distracting them and sneaking past, they enter the tunnels and the next part of the adventure.

This part of the adventure is intended to be eerie and occasionally horrifying. Most of the tunnel areas are unlit, and the characters must find their own source of light or navigate in darkness. The tunnels should feel maze-like and unfathomable.

Characters would be advised to hide from or flee some of the encounters here. There are many hiding places in the tunnels, crevices to squeeze into, debris to hide under or behind. In some places, pipelines or wires run across the ceilings as a reminder of the refinery above, and offer a handhold if characters need to hide in a hurry.

Various threats roam freely, you can introduce locations and random encounters as required (see the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.jBVqRmfuErptNaGv]{Maltus Refinery VI Tunnel Encounter}s Table). The characters should be able to avoid some of these encounters if they’re careful; the only encounter they cannot avoid is with the Beastmen Shaman @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore} in The Shaman’s Lair (2E), lying between them and the last remaining exit.

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.tables.RollTable.jBVqRmfuErptNaGv noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumour}

Tunnel Locations

The tunnels under Maltus Refinery VI are many and winding, a criss-crossing tangle of metallic walkways, rocky burrows and crumbling foundations, often interspersed with reaches of acidic runoff from the manufactorum above. It’s a maddening warren, home to the Chaos-worshipping Beastmen, and perhaps older, stranger foes.

2A. Northern Tunnel Exit

As the party enters the tunnels, read the following:

‘The tunnels slope down, far below the refinery. It’s dark and humid, the rough walls dripping moisture. Every sound echoes, so each single drip or footstep sounds like many. It would be easy to lose your way in these tunnels, and wander forever through the blackness.’

Each character can make a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) or (Hearing) or Intuition (Surroundings) Test to detect two potential ways forward. A blood trail leads to @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2b.-mesks-cage]{Mesk’s Cage (2B)}, and the sound of far-off chanting and flickers of light point towards the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2c.-beastmens-ritual]{Beastemen’s Ritual (2C)}. If everyone fails their Test, the party might stumble into either encounter, and any enemies could gain the drop on them. 

2B. Mesk’s Cage

The former leader of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} is trapped in a cage, suspended from the ceiling of an unlit cavern. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} lies weakly at the bottom of the cage, clothed in thin rags, his limbs dangling in the air. He’s battered and starving, and he’s given up any hope of rescue. He believes all the Beastmen have embraced Chaos, and he’s just waiting to die.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} willingly answers any questions he can, but doesn’t plead for help. He has given up, and unless a loyal member of the herd is with the characters, the only way to help him is to appeal towards his deeper desire for revenge. The thought of sticking a knife into @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgor}e’s back would be a moment worth living for. If the characters rescue @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} and outfit him with a weapon, they gain +1 Superiority for the upcoming encounter in the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2e.-the-shamans-lair]{Shaman’s Lair (2E)}. 

The cage is made from old pipes and strips of metal scavenged from the refinery and is suspended via a heavy chain passed over a rusty girder. Lowering the cage safely requires making a Hard (−20) Athletics (Might) Test, wherein each character involved lowers the Difficulty of the Test by 1 step. If the chain is broken or the cage dropped, it splits open when it hits the ground, dealing 5 Damage to @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk}.

Herdcrafted Cleaver

Many of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} carry weapons they’ve made themselves in the refinery, using shards of metal broken from the dormant machinery and whatever other materials they can find. With fires and forges at their disposal, these cleavers are well-made in a style familiar to the Beastmen. They function as large knives and are used to fight, butcher meat, or make sacrifices to Chaos.

These cleavers would be considered an unusual item in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} black markets, so they are Scarce. Arming @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} with a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.items.Item.tqGb4ULjvQP5x7AK]{Herdcrafted Cleaver}, if the characters have recovered one, would remind him of his former pride in his Herd and make him a willing ally when fighting @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Talgore}.

2C. Beastmen’s Ritual

Strange guttural chanting echoes from the tunnel’s walls, and a flickering red glow casts deep, squirming shadows up ahead. If the players continue, they find a chamber ablaze with thick brown candles that fill the air with a meaty stench. A pair of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.TRcwwntLPqt7KaJy]{Mutated Beastmen} wearing hoods over their horned heads are circling a similarly hooded figure on its knees in the centre of the chamber. Its hands, bound behind it, look distinctly Human, as do its bare and bloodied feet. The chanting Mutated Beastmen are preparing their blades, whetting them and wiping them down as best they can. This unfortunate victim is an unwilling part of some tainted ritual, awaiting the attention of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Shaman}.

If the players rescue the victim, the hood comes off, and the figure is revealed to have the horns and bovine features of the Beastmen, although there’s still something Human about them. They can’t speak but only bray mournfully, and if left alive, run off into the tunnels (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dreg} stat-block to represent this pitiful creature).

2D. Acynadi Den

The tunnels open up into a shallow cavern waterlogged by acidic runoff. Strangely, signs of life among the pools — clusters of sizable dormant @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }— are visible. Rusted pipes run through the cavern, boiling the runoff into steam that fills the chamber. The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} have been harvesting them as an additional source of meat.

If the characters succeed at a Difficult (−10) Stealth (Move Silently) Test, they pass unharmed through the chamber. For each character who fails, the party is attacked by one @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5}. If all characters fail, they are attacked by an @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.8dS1s1UvVXyt6dyv]{Acynadi Gamma-7} instead.

The entire chamber is Difficult Terrain. If any of the pipes is damaged, the related Zone becomes a Minor Hazard. Passing through the acynadi den allows the characters to enter the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2e.-the-shamans-lair]{Shaman’s Lair (2E)} from a point of vantage, also granting them +1 Superiority in the upcoming encounter. However, they do not gain this Superiority if they use any Loud weaponry or equipment in the chamber.

2E. The Shaman’s Lair

The Beastmen Shaman @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore} conducts unholy rites in his gruesome lair. Here, the air smells of sulphur and blood, and any Psykers in the party can feel the painful, maddening presence of Chaos nipping at them from the Warp. The lair is cluttered with empty crates that serve as furniture, barrels with dismembered limbs protruding from the top, and odd items taken from the refinery or stolen from the nearest habsprawls: bits of old machinery, a broken cart, piles of rags, all items the party might use as cover if they seek to enter the lair unseen. These are scattered all over the Lair, with four surrounding Zones and a central Zone as follows.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Talgore} has also had his followers erect a false herdstone in the centre of the cavern, a great lump of rock into which they’ve carved Chaos symbols, before pouring the blood of sacrifices into the grooves. A Human corpse lies drained and dead at its base. This stone is a source of Corruption — characters who end their turn within this central Zone make a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Psychic) Test to resist 1 Corruption Point. Making physical contact with the stone is Moderate Exposure, requiring a Challenging (+0) Fortitude Test to resist 2 Corruption Points. Every SL reduces the number of Corruption Points gained by 1. Damaging the false herdstone at the beginning of the encounter, or during, grants the party +1 Superiority.

If the party enters without @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Talgore}’s knowledge, they see him sprinkling clouds of corrosive chemical dust, taken from the refinery, over herdstone and followers alike. This hisses on contact, singeing the fur and skin of those it lands on, but they don’t react. Talgore mutters as he works, invoking the gods of Chaos, and preaching to his followers. Some of what he says sound like grunts or wordless bellows to the characters, but some they can understand:

‘Rise up! Show them your strength! Death to humans and glory for the Herd!’

There is a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastman} here for every character (including allied NPCs), plus the Shaman @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore} himself. While the party may enter unseen, passing to the exit at the far end of the chamber, beyond the Shaman’s makeshift throne, is difficult. It is possible to escape without fighting the Shaman, and there are a number of Hazards that might be used to the character’s advantage:

  • The barrel of chemical dust near the Shaman could be upturned over a character to cause 10 Damage, or knocked over to cause 5 Damage to all opposing characters within Close Range.

  • Any @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} allies are sickened by the perversion they see here and cannot resist attacking the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Shaman} outright. This should keep him occupied for a few turns.

  •  A crazed @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultist} has been chained, unarmed, to one of the walls. It strains at its bonds, reaching its grasping tentacles towards whoever comes nearest, herd or Human doesn’t matter to this maddened creature. If released, it attacks indiscriminately, and may seek to escape backwards in the tunnels.

If the characters left the two @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.TRcwwntLPqt7KaJy]{Mutated Beastmen} undisturbed at the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2c.-beastmens-ritual]{Beastmen’s Ritual (2C)}, they’ll join the fight four rounds in, after hearing any commotion.

After the encounter, a tunnel at the back of the Shaman’s Lair can take them back to the Lower Hive, a hidden exit just outside the area surrounding the manufactorum, bypassing the closed-off entrances behind them in the upper floors. If they go back and aim to exit from the refinery’s gates, they’re still sealed, and a band of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers} wait to ambush them — paid off by @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} to ensure no one escapes.

Dealing with Lord Felputh

The adventure’s conclusion lies with how the party seeks to deal with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}. If @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik} becomes an ally, she offers to arrange a meeting with Lord Felputh, or they may seek to return to the Hive Spires of their own accord. The party has some time to prepare, since everyone has been convinced they’ve become blockaded within the manufactorum.

Exposing Felputh: If the characters reveal that not only did @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} bring @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} into work in his factory, but that those Beastmen corrupted Human labourers and spread Chaos, then he’s likely to lose everything, including his life.

If he can convince the party to lie about what they’ve seen, and let him spread the word that his problems are caused by rampant mutancy in the surrounding habsprawls, nothing to do with him at all, he can call for the whole area to be purged and no one would ever know he was to blame.

The characters may accept a bribe of 1000 solars each to keep @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh}’s secret. Whether the party’s Patron would approve of their choice depends on their faction and motivations, so the players may have to consider keeping this secret from their Patron. 

Punishing Felputh: Alternatively, the party may be determined to bring @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} to justice, either of their own making or by informing the Macharian Vigilites or an agent of the Inquisition of the Chaos worship going on under his watch. In this case, the refinery is purged, the tunnels sealed off, and a new noble takes over his holdings, taking on the burden of repairs so the refinery is soon operational again.

The news of the Harbinger’s fall swiftly moves through @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, strongly reinforced by the fact that for the first time in close to half a year, the nightly killings cease.

However, the characters might notice that the Harbinger’s body does not conform to all the information the characters may have gathered on his activities. His only weapon was a single-bladed powered scythe, and no toxins were found on him. Indeed, the open ambush was completely atypical of how he has operated thus far. Any captured Vertexis are in mourning, for they swear that he was the Harbinger, and they all believe it, declaring it so even under the duress the Vigilites put them to.

Within two days of the ambush, Captain Vern calls the characters to his office, where he awaits them alongside Master Morlay. Depending on the nature of their relationship with the Master and the circumstances of the Harbinger’s fall, the characters may be sincerely congratulated and perhaps even rewarded, or sneeringly dismissed. Morlay expects them to move on and pointedly ignores any notion that the Harbinger hasn’t been permanently dealt with. With that, he leaves to attend to festival business, which is now less than a week away.

If the characters insist the true Harbinger hasn’t been dealt with, Captain Vern believes them, but his hands are tied. With the deaths seemingly stopped, he suggests the characters must quickly act if they intend to investigate further, as Morlay will soon cut off their access.

The Shanty Man’s Connection

As the characters plot their next moves, presuming they dealt with him during @UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV#rokarth-voidport-records]{Rokarth Voidport Records}, a courier arrives with a missive from Port Ensign Novus of Void Buttress Station SW9. 

‘I met someone you all really need to talk to.’

Once the characters reach his office, Ensign Novus tells them that a Tech-Priest approached him with an unusual story they should hear. Presuming the characters agree, he’ll swiftly arrange for her to join them. If the characters never contacted Ensign Novus, they could be approached by a different Contact who knows the Tech-Priest, or Captain Vern might direct Loga Binary-46 their way.

Loga Binary-46 proves to be a woman with gleaming, golden-hued augmetic eyes. The lower portion of her face is a permanent augmetic respirator. Her voice is surprisingly pleasant, and she speaks softly, albeit with a distinct metallic reverberation. She wears the distinct red robes of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. Several mechadendrites smoothly stir about her. (Use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Tech-Priest} stat-block to represent her).

Roleplaying Loga Binary-46

Though it is considered somewhat gauche to admit to strong emotions within the Adeptus Mechanicus, Loga Binary-46 is very concerned with the implications of the pattern of events she has observed thus far. Her mechadendrites move in time with her voice, stopping suddenly and unnervingly when she is surprised or intent.

‘Genial greetings. I am Loga Binary-46, servant of the Omnissiah. Several anomalous events have transpired, which Ensign Novus suggests require social interaction between us. Ongoing analysis indicates a series of misappropriations from various Adeptus Mechanicus holdings within Hive Rokarth. Several were highly volatile explosives capable of causing substantial damage, along with devices used for remote detonation. Common data point — each theft used a high-level override code over six centuries old, and one not usually seen on Voll.’

Ensign Novus grins and produces a dataslate. ‘The exact same code used to gain access to Hive Rokarth through an exterior hatch, just shy of 6 months ago, not long after a small impact was detected in the vicinity of the hatch.’

‘Ensign Novus tells me these events have congruence and will be relevant to you. Query – is his analysis correct?’

Loga Binary-46 is willing to answer several clarifying questions, but will otherwise raise an eyebrow and ask ‘Relevance?’ to any other unrelated queries. If asked what she does for the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, she notes that she is one of the Machine God’s Curators, offering no further explanation. If asked what ‘substantial damage’ translates to, her mechadendrites stop still, and after a pause, she responds, ‘Extensive damage to ancient and revered apparatus would occur, including a significant reduction in the locally available workforce. Importing and retraining replacements would take weeks.’

Loga asks only a few direct questions — if she is satisfied that the characters can aid her in averting disaster, that is sufficient. She knows where the hatch is located. It will take considerable time to travel to it as it corresponds to an exterior portion of the lower-Upper Hive, nearly as far from the Maglev Nexus as is possible within @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. The Tech-Priest lifts a hand, and a servitor enters, bearing a gleaming cog axe, which she accepts. ‘Query: shall we undertake an excursion?’

The Damaged Pod

It takes a full five hours to reach the hatch Ensign Novus identified. Any characters who intend to go out onto @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} exterior to see what they can find may want to acquire protective gear beyond what they usually carry. The access point is a maintenance hatch that opens onto Voll's caustic environment, which the characters can easily open as they have the codes. Journeying into the mild caustic haze requires a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Endurance) Test. Characters that fail are subject to the effects of exposure to a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.UaRHLqZ99zmg7AeE#exposure]{noxious environment}. Any character without protective eyewear (or augmetic eyes) has Disadvantage on all Awareness (Sight) Tests in this environment. 

It takes some time to locate the source of Ensign Novus’ impact site, as it has been hidden under a large swatch of chemically treated covering removed from elsewhere on the hive. A successful Difficult (−10) Awareness (Sight) Test soon notes faint scorch marks and scraped metal, eventually leading to the partially camouflaged orbital drop pod. Failure on the Test eventually reveals the pod, but it takes time, necessitating a Difficult (−10) Fortitude (Endurance) Test and potentially more substantial exposure damage.

The drop pod is clearly damaged, with a partially scorched and ravaged exterior. Its size indicates that it likely held only a single occupant. Loga Binary-46 immediately moves to study the pod. Though she readily accepts the assistance of any @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} characters, she pointedly stops anyone else from assisting her. One of her mechadendrites begins asserting various devices into the pod, and her fingers tap across different points.

‘Analysis: This is one of the most advanced of these blessed devices I have ever encountered. It is a cryo-crypt as well as a drop pod. The communication module of this vessel is heavily damaged — its occupant received orders to activate, but a second message is stuck within its data circuits. That second message’s transmittal code originates from Voll, directly from the Crystalline Reflectory, sent at the highest priority. This incept date… the message was broadcast approximately five hundred and sixty years ago.’

A Challenging (+0) Lore (Macharian Sector) Test reveals that the message originates squarely within the time of the Macharian Heresy, several decades after the founding of Voll. Loga Binary-46 notes that the data circuits have sadly degraded, leaving the message garbled. But she has successfully recorded the complete transmittal code, meaning that, in theory, the message can be retrieved from the Crystalline Reflectory. 

Other duties call her, but the Tech-Priest passes the message’s code information to the characters on a dataslate and asks the party to inform her of what they discover.

Interception

If the characters are not careful to keep their ongoing investigation quiet, Master Morlay eventually sends a group of Meat Guild Enforcers to speak with them (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcer} stat-block to represent them). If they’ve had a decent working relationship with Morlay, it is a pointed warning and a strong suggestion to wrap their affairs up and move on. If not, the enforcers attack, intending to beat the characters to a pulp, but not kill them. If the characters still don’t take the hint, two days before Halion’s Triumph, a whole squad of Meat GuildEnforcers attack them on the street with the intent of capturing them and imprisoning them until the festival is over, so they can’t interfere further.

The View from Above

Travelling to the Crystalline Reflectory is likely an unusual experience for the characters, as it is located within @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Spires. Once they’ve left the Maglev Nexus, the characters immediately become aware of how open and comparatively quiet the spaces are. There is little thrum of machinery in the spires, no loud vox hailers, no distant screaming. The people here are engaged in business while dressed in casual finery that lower hivers can barely conceive of. All the buildings seem opulent, though careful study notes time-worn cracks in many.

Characters of a less affluent appearance are stopped and questioned by the most immaculately dressed Vigilites they’ve ever met. Though they may have a right to be there with the correct identification, the Vigilite makes clear they should be about their business and then swiftly leave.

The Crystalline Reflectory is a gleaming spike that stands out even amidst the opulence of the Spires, but something about the building's alignment causes a headache if it is gazed at directly for too long. It is an open secret that all the interior walls are said to be lined with psychically active crystalline lattices, enabling the Astropaths within to receive and send Astropathic transmissions more efficiently.

Access to the Crystalline Reflectory is relatively easy, as they routinely accept commissions for messages from the kind of individuals that would have access to the Spires; however, once the characters request access to records supposedly sent centuries ago, they are ushered into a consultation with Adept Callidon Miers (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adept} stat-block to represent him).

Adept Miers’ age is difficult to tell, for his features have a timeless quality. His eyes are hidden behind a deep red scarf, covered with brightly coloured whorls of turquoise and magenta that slowly flow over the surface of the cloth as the characters meet with him. He occasionally tilts his head and cocks it at an angle, apparently listening to something the characters cannot hear. He chooses his words thoughtfully, and though he speaks softly, his voice echoes uncannily.

If the characters have an Influence of 2 or more with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}, or one among them is a psyker, the discussion goes smoothly, and Adept Miers accompanies them to the Crystalline Reflectory’s Transept Vault to help retrieve what they seek. If they do not, he still ultimately helps them, but he requires their assistance with a future matter. In short, the party would owe the Adeptus Astra Telepathica a favour. 

The Transept Vault

After passing the vox transmittal code, the characters recovered from the downed pod through a cogitator and a consultation with a data crypt, Adept Miers leads the characters through various well-appointed hallways while pointedly ignoring the screams and shrieks that occasionally emerge from behind closed doors. Eventually, they pass down into a large hall formed of large grey blocks of stone covered with various sigils that visibly flicker out of the corner of the eye.

‘Astropathic messages are not as simple as vox transmissions. Interpreting them is more art than fact. When an Astropath receives a message, it often comes in symbols akin to a waking dream. Many will translate it into a physical medium as they strive to understand it. We seek a mural, created by Astropath Nalgi Osh well over five centuries ago — thus, it rests amidst some of the oldest records of the Crystalline Reflectory.’

In the vault, Miers pulls forth a sheet of marble-lined crystal, which slowly rolls out of the wall. Fixed upon the crystal is a painting, protected by the slight shimmer of an energy shield of some kind. Miers passes a hand over part of the marble, and the shield disappears. He solemnly takes the painting and places it upon a broad table, upon which increasingly brighter lights shine. Among the details, it features a menacing skull with glowing eyes, a man hanging from a tree, and the piece is covered in distorted text and symbols in between, except for the names ‘Interitas’ and ‘Caelius’ spelt out clearly. Show or hand your players a copy of the mural for them to analyse.

A Hard (−20) Lore (Macharian Sector) Test recalls that Marshal Surlan Caelius was a traitor who served under General Lysander. He was supposedly killed during the Macharian Heresy. Characters can make a Hard (−20) Linguistics (Cypher or High Gothic) Test to decode the symbols. Otherwise, Adept Miers can transcribe the symbols for them.

After a moment, Miers whispers ‘Throne.’ He pauses for a long moment, looking visibly upset. ‘This seems to be an official missive from the Officio Assassinorum. These red symbols are code, rescinding a kill order against a man named Caelius and his entire household. It instructs the assassin Interitas to… unclear… suspend its operations, I think… and await further orders.’

He allows the characters to take picts of the mural, but won’t let the physical artefact leave the Crystalline Reflectory. He specifically requests not to know anything more about this matter and escorts them out with haste. He also provides them with the translated decoded shutdown command: ‘Unit Shutdown: Primus Sanctus Red’ adding the vital fact that it must be spoken aloud to Interitas.

The adventure begins with the characters already situated in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, perhaps wrapping up the loose ends of one of the other missions within Voll Adventures. When the party is gathered in a relatively secluded location, an ornate and heavily scrimshawed servo-skull approaches them and begins relaying an urgent message from their Patron. 

Read or paraphrase the following text:

‘A suddenly pressing matter needs your immediate attention. What were once thought to be random acts of murder and sabotage occurring throughout the eastern portion of Rokarth have been linked to a growing heretical cult known as the Vertexis. They supposedly worship a figure known as the Harbinger whom they dare claim is an angel of the Emperor and say is responsible for the violence. Many workers have apparently grown so fearful of this Harbinger that production has greatly slowed and the Tithe is endangered.

Find this Harbinger, discover its nature, and eliminate it. There is a contact who has earned my trust, Captain Matis Vern, a Vigilite who can give you more information to direct your efforts. Seek him in the East Wing, Block 3, of the Precinct Fortress Majoris. There are conduct passes within this servo-skull to grant you access to the fortress.

Blasphemy cannot be tolerated. Neither can failure. May His will light your way.’

The characters have some time to prepare, gather equipment, or anything else they think they might need for the mission ahead, before heading to Precinct Fortress Majoris.

Identity and Authorisations

The players may wish to work out what their character’s cover for this investigation will be, though this may well be influenced by whatever past relationship they’ve developed with @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Macharian Vigilites}. Worth noting is that the passes which their Patron has bequeathed to the characters bear the symbol of Voll’s Ruling House Castyx and give access to not only the fortress but authorization to ride a private Maglift within the hive’s central Maglev Nexus to it — consider how their Patron came upon these passes. An Inquisitor Patron could have simply demanded them, whereas an Infractionsit Patron may have spent a considerable sum of solars to create forgeries.

They are introduced to their Macharian Vigilite liaison, Captain Vern. They are given the few clues that have been gathered so far and given the choice to either meet or ignore Master Nixious Morlay, who is eager to assist in their efforts. 

@UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV]{Part 2: Strange Patterns} — The characters have the opportunity to follow up on promising leads, including potentially studying the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}’s records, questioning the survivor of a Harbinger attack, and inspecting the gruesome recent aftermath of a Harbinger-style massacre.
