Caelius's Legacy

The High Lords of Terra are not known for their mercy. In the wake of the Macharian Heresy to demonstrate the price of turning against the Imperium, they took particular note of Marshal Surlan Caelius. A charismatic and rebellious figure, Caelius had fought on against the Imperium even after the death of his commander, General Lysander. It was not Marshal Caelius’ military skills that truly condemned him, though — it was the soaring rhetoric with which he made a continual and articulate case for rebellion against an Imperium he declared unjust.

Even though his insurgency had been crushed, and the Marshal reportedly wounded, the High Lords turned to one of their most reliable tools and dispatched an Imperial Assassin to eliminate not only Caelius but his entire household. The Marshal’s flight was traced to the then recently founded hive world of Voll, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} in particular, as he sought to hide amongst the teeming pilgrim masses. Considering what had been sent after him, Caelius’s cowardly ploy would have served the heretic poorly, but the Warp is fickle, and the assassin’s transport vessel was lost on its journey to Voll.

Marshal Caelius never faced the justice he deserved, and lived out the rest of his long life in unearned safety, amidst a large family that knew barely anything of his previous crimes against the Imperium.

Over five centuries later, in the wake of the opening of the Cicatrix Maledictum, a heavily damaged Imperial vessel with no discernible markings emerged from the Warp, bearing a lone surviving passenger in cryo-stasis, locked within a single-occupant drop pod. The ship arrived within the Voll System and initiated crash procedures even as it hurtled toward the planet. The small crew of servitors aboard the vessel launched the drop pod only moments before uncontrolled entry into Voll’s atmosphere tore the voidship to pieces.

It did not take long for the newly activated assassin to tap into @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} datacrypts in search of his assigned targets. Over half a millennium later, Marshal Caelius’ descendants numbered close to a million, giving or taking several thousand lost to the Adeptus Administratum’s arcane bureaucracy.

An Imperial Assassin now hunts the habways and spires of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, his Sentinel Array noting faint traces of Caelius’ genetic signature in endless crowds of people throughout the hive’s eastern quarter. If he had originated from a different Assassinorum Temple, perhaps he would’ve sought clarification on his mission, but he is an Eversor. Gene-altered to inhuman combat prowess and psycho-conditioned to be utterly without remorse or pity, Eversor Assassins do not exist merely to kill. Their purpose is to annihilate, to terrify, to show heretics that the Wrath of the God-Emperor is entirely without limits or mercy.  

The Eversor has never received counter-orders, so the mission stands: eradicate Caelius and his entire household… no matter how large it may be.

Hands of Death

Within the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, buried beneath layers of bureaucratic meandering and deliberate obfuscation, there lies a body dedicated to swift, inevitable, and efficient disposal of any target. The Officio Assassinorum has a range of assets for whom the art of death is not merely a martial virtue, but an irresistible spiritual calling. Within the halls of its assorted temples are crafted killers beyond compare. They are masters of stealth, equipped with ruinous weaponry and hideous toxins, each capable of unparalleled bloodshed inflicted in countless ways. Each is pushed past the boundaries of average Human capability by augmetics, medicae drugs and combat stimms to hone their brutal efficiency. They are a horror most citizens of the Imperium have no idea exist, and would count themselves lucky never to share a planet with.

Nevertheless, countless billions owe their lives to the secret acts of these brutal assassins. Though few official records exist, these unheralded agents of the God-Emperor’s will have slain corrupt planetary governors, executed xenos generals, and laid waste to nascent cults that would have offered up whole worlds to their dark gods. 

Of all the tools crafted by the Officio Assassinorum, the Eversor is perhaps the least subtle. The Eversor Temple believes that the best way to eliminate a target is in a blaze of psychotic fury, disregarding factors such as collateral damage, practicality or the potential innocence of bystanders. Eversor Assassins are locked in cryo-stasis and, when active, only kept in check by mission parameters delivered via cranial augmetics. Once roused, potent combat stimms drive them to superhuman levels of speed, strength and aggression. Chosen targets have little chance of survival against such a ruthless foe, and any who come between them will meet the same brutal end.

Failing Quotas

Murder is all too common in any hive city — a certain incidence count is expected and accounted for by the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}. Indeed, a (rare) subsidence in the rate of homicide generally leads to a momentary increase in the number of soldiers tithed to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}, and a good deal of paperwork to accompany it. The majority of deaths within @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} are commonly attributed to gang violence, summary justice from various enforcers, industrial accidents, Infractionist activity, or a bored nobility in search of bloody diversion. Thus, a long series of grisly murders occurring throughout Rokarth’s eastern quarter went unremarked by the Macharian Vigilites, given the gargantuan population density and scale of the districts involved. All until the data points related to the murders began to match up. 

Over several months, the murders grew increasingly grisly and became increasingly associated with nearby industrial accidents, which further investigation showed were clearly sabotage. A newly reconsecrated cathedrum wall collapsed, killing hundreds. An entire manufactorum shift was slain by an explosively rerouted acid wash. Even the ordinary citizenry of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, rarely informed of goings-on far beyond their hab, began to take notice. They slowly discerned that they were being targeted and grew increasingly fearful. This has led to a notable decrease in productivity throughout the eastern hive, though some imaginative overseers fear it may lead to far worse than that. This, at last, drew the attention of both the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum }and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#castyx]{House Castyx} — for there is nothing of greater importance on Voll than the sanctity of the Tithe, especially after the dark and unproductive years of the Noctis Aeterna.

With increased scrutiny came a name for this supposed perpetrator.

The Harbinger 

Hivers throughout @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}claim to have caught glimpses of a dark, deathly figure flitting through the habs and manufactorums where sabotage occurred, as have the few rare survivors of its attacks. A small, but growing, cult — the Vertexis — claims that the figure is an angel of the God-Emperor, bringing His righteous judgement against the many sinners of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} (ironically, not an entirely incorrect sentiment). They refer to the dark angel as the Harbinger, and they have begun to graffiti murals depicting his pale face with various exhortations — the most common being simply ‘Judgment is Coming’. Many are unhinged fanatics and may potentially attack anyone they perceive as being out to stop the Harbinger from purging @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} sins. 

Witnesses’ descriptions of the Harbinger have a few consistencies — all note a sinister, swift-moving figure clad in black with a terrible, gaunt, pale face and burning eyes. Some claim the eyes glowed a deep crimson, others a pale blue. A few stated that the figure wielded a scythe that could shear through an armoured bulkhead like it was paper. A widely circulating rumour says a group of Macharian Vigilites nearly caught the Harbinger in a trap, and it killed most of them in return. The Harbinger is, in part, the Eversor Assassin codenamed Interitas. But very few witnesses remain of his true work. Most witnesses related to the investigation have observed a copycat killer instead, a death cultist masquerading as something far more, whom the characters will invariably meet during their investigation.

Interitas has experienced rare frustration in his present mission. Cracking into @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} datavaults, he recognised that the sheer volume of targets would take him a thousand years to eliminate by traditional linear means. He is frenzied by the fluctuating number of targets: knowing the longer he takes to complete his task, the more he has to eradicate, and so many have already lived full lives escaping the God-Emperor’s wrath. One detail of note is that most of his targets dwell in the eastern Lower Hive sectors of Rokarth, though scattered across its many levels. With a relatively compact zone for such a large number of targets, the necessary slaughter can be perpetrated with utmost efficiency.

Not long after the characters begin their investigation, news of an upcoming event in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} leads the assassin to modify his tactics once more, as he suspects a massive amount of his targets will assemble into a single hive buttress, affording him a unique opportunity to eliminate a considerable portion of them at once during the festival known as Halion’s Triumph. There is sure to be significant collateral damage.

Halion’s Triumph

One of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} most critical civic commemorations, Halion’s Triumph, celebrates the official founding of Voll and is marked by a vast series of feasts. Each decade, on the day of Halion’s Triumph, workers are rewarded with their share of a grand feast at the end of their shifts, provided they meet the day’s quota. @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{Acynadi} meat is served on behalf of the commemoration’s patrons, a joint venture between @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#castyx]{House Castyx} and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#carnem]{Mercator Carnem} — the Meat Guild of Voll. 

The Halion’s Triumph feasts are one of the few times many of Voll’s hivers will ever get to taste meat in their entire lives, and all inhabitants of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} highly anticipate the day. The population of Rokarth is such that many thousands of feasts of varying sizes occur across the hive over an entire day, with a few notable locations hosting feasts for many thousands of clamouring, hungry citizens.

The Frantic Official

Master Nixious Morlay is a high-level agent of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, though firmly allied with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#carnem]{Mercator Carnem}. Master Morlay’s entire existence revolves around Halion’s Triumph. It takes nearly ten whole years since the last festival to plan for the next, and this is the third Triumph that Morlay has been responsible for overseeing. The predations of the Harbinger have now caused what is all but unthinkable to Morlay: various Factions within @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} quietly suggest that the festival should be postponed, or even entirely cancelled, until the threat to production is dealt with. He is, however, determined that the massive festival goes forward as is tradition. The characters are tasked to stop the Harbinger's plans by Morlay and his hysterical requests for immediate support in handling the increasingly dire situation.

Should the characters choose to help him, they find Morlay an overanxious but ostensibly well-meaning ally, eager to assist their investigations in any way he can, while constantly requesting updates on their activities. The Master is assisted by a cadre of iridescently jacketed enforcers from the Mercator Carnem who do his bidding, assisting the characters as requested. Drawing on Morlay’s Influence can open certain doors, though not without a cost; however, at the midpoint of Implacable, once the characters have apparently dealt with the Harbinger — though in fact have merely stopped a copy-cat killer — and the brutal murders have suddenly stopped, Morlay is all-too-eager to profusely thank the characters for their efforts and send them away. He is stubbornly unwilling to look at evidence suggesting the Harbinger hasn’t truly been dealt with, and his enforcers turn their aggression onto the characters if they persist in their investigations against the Master’s orders, hampering their efforts.

Festivals in the Imperium

Repeated @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} analysis points to consistent productivity spikes surrounding extended periods of annual worship and observances. Therefore, worldwide and hive-wide commemorations are curated in each world’s calendar to give workers moments of collective pride and subservience — all practical efforts in raising @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} regiments to defend the Imperium and provide the populace a sense of purpose in their backbreaking toil. Even if such festivals are barely concealed propaganda, designed to stir religious zeal, martial pride or appeal to the legions of workers, acknowledging the contributions of their toil.

Masters of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} are assigned to work with Planetary Governors, or their representatives, to coordinate these massive festivals and occasional entertainments. These are often accompanied by processions, parades, and carefully negotiated breaks from labour, often followed by extraneous overtime to make up for and exceed the brief dip in production. Some feature occasional feasts, among the only times in their lives that most hive citizens get to taste anything other than remanufactured nutrient pastes that are a staple of hive life.

With Interitas rebound to his cryo pod, the party’s Patron wearily contacts the Officio Assassinorum, alerting the Assassin Temple to Interitas’ survival and presence on Voll. Their Patron orders them to scour any thought or notion of Interitas from their minds — the Officio Assassinorum is never to be spoken of again — and threatens to wipe their minds if they cannot stay their tongues. That said, Interitas is an interesting character to keep in your back pocket for future adventures — perhaps the Officio Assassinorum took the opportunity to keep Interitas on Voll, to improve their operations in the Macharian Sector. But the characters would never know this for sure.

Some NPCs the characters encountered could become valuable Contacts or Hirelings in their future adventures, such as Loga Binary-46 (if they manage to defeat Interitas with her help), Captain Matis Vern or Port Ensign Novus (who could aid the characters in gaining access to protected parts of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}), and Curator Adjen Sablik or Adept Callidon Miers (who could help the characters with appropriate research during their future investigations).

Experience Points

All characters should earn @Reward[xp=30 reason=Implacable]{30 XP} for participating in the adventure, but if any characters achieved personal goals or fulfilled a goal for a Patron, their reward should be increased accordingly. In addition, the following experience can be awarded:

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Gathered a clue]{10 XP} for each clue gathered during Part 1. 

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Gathared a clue]{10 XP} for each clue gathered during Part 2.

  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Survived the Vertexis ambush]{20 XP} for surviving the Vertexis ambush and defeating the copycat Harbinger.

  • @Reward[xp=40 reason=Confronted and shut down the Eversor Inheritas]{40 XP} for confronting and shutting down Eversor Interitas.

Influence

Award or reduce the character’s Personal Influence according to their behaviour towards the factions they have encountered — primarily the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, if they successfully worked with Loga Binary-46 during Parts 4 and 5, or the Macharian Vigilites (@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}) for aiding Captain Matis Vern, or the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet} for dealing favourably with Port Ensign Novus. Consider altering their Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} (by extension of the Officio Assassinorum) for dealing with Interitas. However, they might not recognise this effect until they next directly deal with the Adeptus Administratum or the Officio Assassinorum.  

These increases can bleed over to their Patron’s Influences if they represented their Patron honourably or made such a gross error in judgment as to affect their Patron’s standings. Aim to award (or detract) at least one point to each character and their Patron.

Failure

If the characters fail to complete the main objectives of the adventure, Interitas is left to continue on his rampage, as noted in the @UUID[.UHtSqeiaUMvo4YMP#the-cowards-way]{Coward’s Way}. However, there are also some other points of failure to note from earlier in the adventure.

Failure to stop the Harbinger during Part 3 allows the Vertexis Cult to continue growing. They use Halion’s Triumph to wipe out more targeted citizens (with or without Interitas’s attacks to back them up), and Master Morlay won’t halt the commemorations for anything. If Interitas is dealt with, the Harbinger garners a greater cult of personality and continues their killings without proper direction. They swallow up lesser cults in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} to add to their ranks and continue spreading throughout the Hive, turning the lower reaches of the hive into battle zones, pitching fights between them and the Vigilites.

Failure to stop the attacks during Halion’s Triumph and the resulting loss of life cause @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} productivity to plummet, and with it, the average citizen’s quality of life. The eastern sectors of the hive become ripe for @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} elements to thrive, and by extension, Rokarth’s Genestealer Cult cells. As the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#castyx]{Castyx} Dynasty scrambles to source replacement workers from Voll’s other hives or nearby systems, the Dynasty’s control over Voll wavers, allowing other families and guilds to rise in power against them.

What’s Next?

The end of this adventure has a few loose ends that could be spun into further adventures for your party. Consider the following:

  • Captain Matis Vern approaches the characters, asking for aid to track down the remaining pockets of Vertexis Cult members strewn across the eastern sectors of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. They are still eliminating citizens, a long list of names given to them by the Harbinger before their demise. But without a leader, the Vertexis remnants are ripe to be manipulated by one of Hive Rokarth’s hidden chaos cults, or perhaps tied to the following thread. 

  • During the adventure, characters may have noticed the Harbinger’s strange Power Scythe, and its obviously tech-heresy construction. This can only mean one thing: a rogue heretek is operating on @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. They offer their services to the widespread heretical cults hidden in the hive city, seeking to bolster their power and dissent against the hive’s status quo. Did they know about Interitas’s mission, the presence of the Eversor Assassin, and think the Vertexis a cult worth manipulating? The characters could once more gain the aid of Loga Binary-46 to track down this foe — the magos within Forge-fane Incalos-6 would greatly appreciate the character’s support if this heretek is dealt with swiftly and without public notice.

To call the Precinct Fortress Majoris a ‘fortress’ is a misnomer, or a staggering understatement. It is in fact the entire bottom level of the Upper Hive of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} — a maze of dark rockcrete, the headquarters of the Macharian Vigilites on Voll, and the main checkpoint through which everything and everyone travelling from Upper to Lower Hive, or vice-versa, must pass.

A flash of their passes easily gets the characters into the very heart of the Maglev Nexus and they may well marvel at how notably smooth and swift their ride is. Heavily armed @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.KTlRprKRb8XzlnAD]{Gun Servitors} and steely-eyed @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Vigilites} immediately track them as they exit the Maglift with immediate demands to see their identification. A Routine (+20) Intuition (People) Test notes that the Vigilites on guard immediately stiffen and become very polite indeed once they’ve authenticated the party’s passes. The sentries readily direct the characters on the best way to get to Block 3 if asked.

Captain Vern’s Office

The characters are stopped several times along the way to Captain Vern’s office, but a flash of their passes always sees quick salutes, and the characters are immediately waved on. Block 3 proves to effectively be a large marshalling yard where squads of Vigilites run through hand-to-hand drills and crowd control tactics.

Vern’s office is a relatively simple affair attached to the yard. It’s filled with shelves packed with dataslates. Any organisation, if it exists, must clearly be particularly arcane. Various pieces of mismatched furniture lie about the room and a massive weapons locker dominates one entire wall. Captain Vern is a veritable grox of a man, eschewing the typical Vigilite carapace armour for a sturdy-looking great coat. His dark hair is flecked with grey. He regards the characters as they enter his office with one sharp green eye and one silver-pale augmetic lens which audibly whirrs and clicks as he studies them.

Roleplaying Captain Matis Vern

Captain Vern possesses a surprisingly genial manner and welcomes the characters with no small sense of relief. He is clearly frustrated, not to mention concerned, though he does his best to keep the last emotion to himself. Use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Vigilite} stat-block to represent Captain Vern if needed. If asked about his connection to the party’s Patron, he smiles and taps his augmetic eye. ‘Our mutual friend saved me from getting gutted by the Throne-cursed cur who did this.’ He picks up a dataslate, checking details as he speaks.

On The Vertexis: ‘Cults come and go in Rokarth at a fast pace. A few citizens got themselves a glimpse of our perpetrator at some point. Dressed in a black, gaunt pale face, carrying a scythe of all things. They call ‘im The Harbinger. Claim they’re loyal to the Imperium, that he’s an angel of the Emperor, come to punish the guilty. You’ll see their murals about. We erase them and eliminate anyone we catch putting them up. But they always return. Just addled scum.’

On the Killings: ‘Near as we can tell, about half a year ago is when the relevant murders began. Pretty much every night cycle since, regularly as clockwork, though the scale varies. I have a slate here for you with autopsy reports. Don’t eat afore you read. Our killer doesn’t discriminate much. No motivations that we can identify. Whole habs butchered. Few survivors. Likes blades, but not exclusively. Leaves a big mess. We thought he was a pattern killer, higher-ups didn’t much care — nobody in the Spire was getting hit. But then the sabotages began.’ 

On the Case: ‘At this point, all I’ve hit are deadwalls. We’ve had scores of savants scouring over the datapoints, but no useful connections among the victims have been discerned. However, we’re not allowed access to the Administratum’s or Imperial Navy's full records. That’s why I’m hoping you lot can shake something free. Go where I can’t. I think you should know why you’re here. It’s not just ‘cause of the Tithe. I had a squad, some of my best. Set up a trap for the Harbinger. That thing slaughtered them all, took them apart like they were nothing. Killed a squad of ten Vigilites in mere moments. I don’t know what this thing is, but like I told your boss, I don’t think it’s Human. Find this thing before more of my officers get butchered, but don’t engage it at close quarters if you can help it.’

Vern answers what questions he can, but mostly notes, ‘All in the file.’ If the characters wish to speak with one of the more coherent survivors, he arranges it for the next day. He offers them a private vox channel to contact him for support as needed, and asks to be apprised if possible. Finally, he ruefully shakes his head, saying there’s one last situation the characters have to deal with.

‘There’s a man, Administratum. Master Morlay. He’ll be waiting for you, outside the fortress, Upper Hive Gate 6. He might be useful. Maybe not. But you should probably see him, he’s got some pull.’

Grim Reading

The sheer scale of the killings listed on Captain Vern’s dataslate is daunting — well over three thousand autopsy files, including some listed as ‘corpus inconclusive’ — noting the number of victims in several incidents was undiscernible as extensive tissue breakdown due to ‘exposure to caustic elements’ had rendered differentiating victims effectively impossible with the resources available to the Vigilites’ verispex. There are clearly countless more victims than even the investigating Vigilites can account for.

It takes a successful Routine (+20) Discipline (Composure) Test for a character to force themselves to continue to read the extensive litanies of gruesome deaths listed in the reports long enough to pick up anything useful. For each level of success, they manage to understand the key details of one of the four following paragraphs:

Weaponry: Of those still intact, the bulk of the autopsies for those killed in habs indicate cause of death as deep lacerations, typically with a bladed weapon that was likely powered in some way, but not a chain weapon, as the cuts were too clean. Some died from blunt force trauma, typically from a precise blow that crushed a windpipe or a broken neck. 

Unusual Munitions: A few were shot with unusual munitions that exploded after impact. The summary report notes, with clear reluctance, that while such rounds certainly resembled those of sacred bolt weaponry, their likely calibre was not at all standard.

Toxins: The Vigilite autopsies are listed in a separate file. Several have appended toxicology reports that indicate they were exposed to a particularly virulent toxin, likely introduced via laceration with a multi-bladed weapon that readily cut through carapace armour. Several showed extreme nerve degeneration, which happened pre-mortem within mere moments of exposure. Likely exceedingly painful. One’s breastplate had been partially melted by what appeared to be a random spray of a particularly powerful corrosive compound, traces of which matched none of the many acids and corrosives found on Voll, a stunning conclusion the verispex confirmed with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#dilaquo]{Mercator Dilaquo}.

Sabotage: A file marked as sabotage contains ten detailed industrial incidents. The common thread throughout the incidents is that, while they appeared to be accidents at first, they were all perfectly executed to cause maximum carnage. Several indicate the use of a @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.99dVOsy85KLNtGTj]{Melta Bomb}, which is not at all a common or inexpensive munition.

The Master Awaits

The characters can choose whether they meet with the Master or not. A Challenging (+0) Lore (Adeptus Terra or Voll) Test notes that Master Morlay is an Adeptus Administratum Master whose main job is coordinating hive-wide festivals, chief among them Halion’s Triumph. Failure to meet up with Morlay, he considers it an insult and results in greater difficulties during @UUID[.5GjYiCc0FBtc8dhc]{Part 4: Old Records}.

If the characters head to Upper Hive Gate 6, they find a slight man in once-sumptuous dark robes covered in flowing silvery script, which have seen a lot of use and appear worn. He occasionally pulls heavily on a massive, long-stemmed wooden pipe with engraved bone and metal plates. A group of rough-looking sorts, all wearing brightly scintillant jackets, surround him, acting as bodyguards.

A Routine (+20) Lore (Voll) Test recognises the distinct jackets, marking them as members of the Mercator Carnem — the Meat Guild of Voll. Sporadically, he snaps his fingers and points, causing one of these minions to lean over and relight his pipe. Use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adept} to represent Morlay, and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Trooper} to represent his guards, if required.

‘Ah, here at last. Exquisite. I am Master Nixious Morlay. I’m told you’ve come to set my festival to rights. Exacting business. I am briefly at your disposal.’ 

Morlay tends to speak in measured bursts, with unusual liberal adjective use as punctuation. A Difficult (−10) Intuition (People) Test reveals that he is very worried, though he conceals it well. Morlay asks the characters if they are aware of the supreme importance of @UUID[.GjnFA1lCGKEla9yA#halions-triumph]{Halion’s Triumph} and relays various details about it, including that he must return to work on at once. This serves as his preamble to offering his services in assisting with this ‘vexatious affair.’ 

What Morlay offers is effectively 2 @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#temporary-influence]{Temporary Influence} with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, particularly useful if the characters have no such Influence with that Faction among their members. But the cost of invoking Morlay’s Influence is that the Master knows exactly what sorts of questions the characters are asking, what they learned, and he expects regular updates on their progress with the case. He can also offer the services of his Mercator Carnem allies if the characters feel they need some muscle; however, the Meat Guild’s members ultimately answer to Morlay — which may be a problem for the party once the Master decides it is time for the characters to move on.

Characters who take Morlay up on the offer are given a copy of his personal sigil and a vox channel by which he can be reached. He requests regular reports of their progress. He looks visibly put out if they decline his offer, noting, ‘Superlative, to be so gifted at your work.’ He reacts by withdrawing in a huff but sets his Mercator Carnem agents to monitor the characters’ movements and cause them further trouble during @UUID[.5GjYiCc0FBtc8dhc]{Part 4: Old Records}.

When the characters descend from the Spires, it is approximately three days till Halion’s Triumph begins. Once the characters have had a chance to talk about their next moves, a messenger servo-skull appears with a message from their Patron.

‘Your mission’s parameters have changed. You must do what you can to retrieve the Harbinger alive. I have assembled a strike team to aid you. They are en route to you but will arrive in approximately seven days. The Emperor protects.’

Bringing in the Tech-Priest

If the characters take what they’ve learned to Loga Binary-46, she registers as pleased. She explains to the characters that she and some colleagues have determined that the stolen remote detonators have signals that can be interfered with, in part because the density of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} architecture dilutes their signal. 

‘The information you have gathered suggests the assassin will strike at Halion’s Triumph. We must disrupt his signal. In this matchless opportunity, he will be forced to activate his explosives manually, even as you are compelled to directly confront him to input the cancellation order and terminate his mission. A pleasing symmetry; the Omnissiah approves.’

She assists the characters in determining the most likely spots where explosives would need to be placed to cause the most harm at the Halion’s Triumph commemoration in eastern @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. She employs numerous Adeptus Mechanicus’ devices, many of which she does not discuss openly, to search for the Harbinger in those areas. 

The night before the commemoration, she sends a vox message to the characters, informing them she has spotted the assassin moving stealthily at great speed and knows with only a 3% chance of error where he will be located on the morrow to set off his explosives manually.

‘May probability skew in our favour. Ave Omnissiah.’

Confronting the Eversor

The site Loga Binary-46 has determined as the most likely location where the characters can confront the assassin, is a maintenance corridor within the upper sections of the Lower Hive. The corridor is under three meters wide, its sides lined with piping and various inscrutable machinery. A Challenging (+0) Tech (Engineering) Test reveals that the bulk of the machinery is for air regulation and power dispersal, but also that the corridor underlies one of the main retention walls, which supports the eastern Windswept Buttress.

The information the characters have gathered about Interitas during the course of Implacable means they likely gain 1 Superiority against him for Know Thy Foe. You should also determine if the party has garnered more @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.3j1kargHBeCTssE7#gaining-superiority-before-combat]{Superiority} for the fight ahead.

No level of stealth affords the characters the opportunity to catch the assassin unaware due to a device he carries called a Sentinel Array — but they won’t know that. Characters working with the Tech-Priest have a good idea when the assassin is about to arrive due to ongoing vox warnings. That still doesn’t lessen the impact as he looms out of the shadows of the hive.

Confronting the terrifying presence of an Eversor Assassin requires a Hard (−20) Discipline (Fear) Test. It also takes a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Composure) Test to speak Interitas’ mission retraction orders clearly and calmly. If the speaker doesn’t know High Gothic, they make this Test with Disadvantage. Failure means they must try again in the following round, presuming they are still alive, as Interitas immediately shifts to attack anyone trying to give him a shutdown order.

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.Tb2PzBCvBZiVSKPD]{Eversor Interitas} is more than capable of slaughtering all the characters — fighting defensively is almost certainly their best option. Echoing gunfire in an enclosed corridor prevents the assassin from being able to hear what is being said to him clearly. This does not necessarily prevent him from shooting — the best way to stop that is to engage him in melee combat.

If the shutdown command is successfully delivered, ‘Unit Shutdown: Primus Sanctus Red’, Interitas immediately stops in his tracks — even mid-attack. He sheaths his weapons and moves for the drop pod, where he falls into a deep state of psycho-restraint.

The Coward’s Way

If the characters choose not to act and await their Patron’s strike team, on the day of Halion’s Triumph, a series of massive explosions collapse the greater part of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} eastern Windswept Buttress. The number of deaths is staggering, and the final number is ultimately impossible to determine. The Harbinger’s predations begin again the following evening.

Let the characters say what they choose to do, if anything, to assist the folk of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. Once the strike team arrives, they take all the information the characters have gathered, then dismiss them. It takes weeks for them to track and confront the Harbinger, and during that time, hundreds more civilians die. Their Patron is exceedingly displeased with them all, holding their failure to intervene as reprehensible cowardice.

If the Tech-Priest Loga Binary-46 ever learns the characters suspected what was coming, but did not act, they immediately lose 2 Influence with her and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. 

Other Solutions

The characters may have gathered enough information to confront the assassin without the Tech-Priest's assistance. The characters may have deduced some way of locating him or correctly surmised that he must be close enough for the detonation signal to carry through @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} thick architecture. In such a case, bow to the law of dramatic necessity and let them find him before he has set off the signal. If they cannot stop him one way or another within four combat rounds, he sets off the explosives, then withdraws to continue his mission the following evening.

As the characters leave the devastated hab, they see Vertexis-style graffiti marked on an opposing hab wall, the sinister figure of the pale-faced Harbinger looming over crumbling statuary with an inerudite inscription that reads, ‘Judgement is coming!’ 

Harbinger Ambush

As the weary characters make their way back towards the Maglev Nexus through the crowded habs and walkways of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Lower Hive, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.47e5e8pz6cKrei1w]{the Harbinger} and a particularly fanatic group of his @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BNzIELnXHo5A5LGP]{Vertexis} followers attempt to end the characters’ sinful existences and stop their blasphemous investigation into their righteous activities via an ambush.

Describe the habway the characters are navigating along, noting the flowing crowds that all appear functionally identical, all dressed in almost the same grey and brown utilitarian garb. The drainage canal flows beside them, and the sharp calls of commissary vendors holding aloft metal sticks spiked with questionable meats from the risen areas above. There is a continual murmur of the horde and the scraping, gritty shuffle of countless muddy feet. The lumens flicker, and the shadows are long. 

Ask the characters to make a Difficult (−10) Awareness (Sight) or Intuition (Surroundings) Test to see if they notice the upcoming ambush and whether they are @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.YEIzXenjBxa3GlTQ#surprise]{Surprised}:

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 or more SL): The character notices the slight thinning of the crowd around them as menacing figures appear on the walkways and the covered bridge above them. They are not Surprised and have the time to take an Action before combat begins.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): The character perceives the crowd thinning about them. They are not Surprised when combat begins.

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): The character does not notice the Vertexis gathering to attack and is Surprised when combat begins.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The character does not notice the Vertexis gathering to attack and is Surprised when combat begins. When the Harbinger leaps down to attack, the character must make a Difficult (−10) Discipline (Fear) Test or become Frightened of the grim figure.

There are a number of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.BNzIELnXHo5A5LGP]{Vertexis Cultists}, equal to the number of characters plus 2, in addition to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.47e5e8pz6cKrei1w]{Harbinger}. If the characters failed badly in trying to learn more about the Vertexis, add two more Vertexis Cultists to the pack.

The Vertexis are nearly identical to the crowd surrounding the characters, except they have makeshift skull masks covering their faces, all made from pieces of flat bone, skulls, or servo-skulls. They wield simple fire bombs, makeshift weapons, and poorly manufactured and maintained autoguns. The Harbinger appears exactly as the characters have been led to believe — a menacing figure swathed in black with a stark white face, gleaming red augmetic eyes, and a crude but effective-looking powered scythe.

Zone 1: Drainage Canal

The characters start in this Zone. For the first two rounds of combat, Zone 1 counts as Difficult Terrain due to the surrounding crowds, but the crowd also provides Light Cover. By the third round, these Environmental Traits cease as much of the crowd has fled. Characters can fall into the open drainage canal — they can make a Difficult (−10) Athletics (Swimming) Test to escape before the current pulls them away. Characters can also make a Difficult (−10) Athletics (Might) Test to jump across to the other side safely.

Zone 2: Northern Overhang

This Zone is strewn with market stalls offering trinkets, simple goods, and quick bites to eat. The area is Difficult Terrain due to the clutter but it also provides ample Medium Cover to characters within. Stray gunshots can ignite gas tanks and make holes in the surrounding pipeworks, causing Minor Hazards to those nearby. Half the Vertexis Cultists retreat towards this area if they become overpowered.

Zone 3: Southern Overhang

This Zone mirrors Zone 2 (Northern Overhang), with the same Features and Traits, except it also features a hidden escape hatch into the hive waterways. It can be found by making a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test or witnessing one of the Vertexis Cultists escaping. The other half of the Vertexis Cultists retreat towards this area if they become overpowered.

Zone 4: Walkways

Two wide walkways join Zones 2 and 3 together. The Vertexis Cultists begin their attacks from these walkways, hurling their firebombs onto the habway below. Characters have Light Cover in these Zones if characters in Zone 1 below attack them. Characters who fall from these walkways land in the Drainage Canal below.

Tricks and Tactics

@UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} characters gain Advantage if they forcefully confront the Vertexis Cultists with a Presence (Intimidation) Test. If they succeed at the Test with an Impressive result or better (+3 or more SL), the characters immediately gain a point of Superiority.

The Vertexis Cultists begin their ambush by hurling fire bombs down on the characters from above. As the burning fuel of the bombs causes the screaming crowds to flee, the Harbinger leaps down to finish off the characters. The Vertexis aim to pick off stray characters from above while their angel fights the wicked.

The Harbinger is a fanatic and will never retreat. He fights to the death. If the Harbinger falls, any remaining Vertexis immediately break and flee from the scene.

Inspecting his weaponry, the Harbinger’s scratch-built powered scythe reveals to be a blasphemous device to any Tech-Priest. Its origins are unclear, and any interrogation of the self-proclaimed Harbinger results only in claims that it was a gift from the God-Emperor.

Never a Vigilite when you need one…

This ambush could rapidly turn deadly if the characters are not particularly combat-oriented. If they took up Master Morlay’s offer, they may already have Meat Guild Enforcers near to hand who surpass the odds (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcer} stat-block to represent them). If not, after one or more characters have gone down, the Mercator Carnem shows its hand, and their enforcers suddenly arrive to deal with the Harbinger. Morlay thanks the characters for their efforts in ‘routing out this mendacious scourge’ and then dismisses them — permanently, in his view.

After what they’ve learned during the first part of the adventure, the characters can attempt to follow up on these leads:

  • Connections between the various victims of the Harbinger may be found if the characters can study the voluminous records held within the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} Censorium.

  • They may wish to investigate @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Voidport Records surrounding the time roughly corresponding with the Harbinger’s first kills looking for anomalies.

  • They may have taken Captain Vern up on his offer to interrogate a survivor of one of the Harbinger’s attacks the following day.

  • They may wish to seek out a less Vigilite-slanted view of the Vertexis.

Various pieces of information that can help identify what the Harbinger might be trying to achieve may emerge during these investigations, though learning any given piece of information won’t tell the characters the full story. After a day or two spent investigating, Captain Vern invites the characters to inspect the gruesome aftermath of a fresh Harbinger massacre at the @UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV#the-shattered-hab]{Shattered Hab}.

To the Censorium

The @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} Censorium is a heavily reinforced rockcrete tomb high in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Upper Hive, filled with a staggering array of data towers and cogitator arrays. All information, important or otherwise, concerning Voll’s citizenry is held here. The air is thick and charged, filled with wafts of incense, sacred oils, and redolent of ozone. Minor scribes with cloths continually wipe away condensation from scrolls, dataslates, and the sweat of their superior’s brows as servitors bearing censers of blessed waters slowly walk in preassigned patterns leaving pockets of brief respite from the humidity in their wake.   

Access to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} Censorium is heavily restricted and the characters need a measure of Influence with the Adeptus Administratum of 1 or better to access the facility. If the party lacks Influence with the Adeptus Administratum, they can still choose to take Master Morlay up on his offer.

Presuming the characters gain access to the Censorium, they are assigned a Curator to assist them in their research. All data within the Censorium is encrypted with cyphers and impossible to access or understand without assistance (unless a character has the Linguistics (Cypher) Specialisation). The characters’ liaison is Curator Adjen Sablik, a young woman with symbols from different ancient languages tattooed about her eyes in a light shade of blue ink. Her arms hold augmetic auto quills which can snap forward and incase her hands. She constantly taps her fingers, whether in or out of the quills, the sound changing depending on whether her fingers are encased or not. She is delighted by trivial information and fascinated by weapons of all sorts. Use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adept} stat-block to represent her if required.

The character’s success in their search for information is ultimately dictated by how well they interact with Curator Sablik. Have them chat with her for a while and take note of exactly what questions they ask. All characters present should make a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Inquiry or Charm) Test. Remember to add the characters’ highest Administratum Influence as an SL bonus. It takes several hours of cogitating till Curator Sablik comes back with the following, depending on the highest SL achieved:

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 or more SL): Looking past the high-scale massacres, in cases where only single or handfuls of victims were recorded, Curator Sablik has found a tenuous familial connection. One that stretches back for centuries, but it is there almost every time. What’s more, she spotted that many of the records had recently been accessed, within the last year, but whoever had done so had somehow managed to erase their identity from the data towers, a supposedly impossible feat.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): A considerable number of the victims are distantly related, though sometimes those connections are several generations old and not apparent. A fair third or more don’t appear to have any relation to the others.

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): Some of the victims appear to be related, but there are so many, and contained within an old sector of the hive, that it is hard to say if this is merely a minor statistical anomaly or something more meaningful.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The Curator flatly states that she does not have the time to deal with their query, but logs it for non-priority processing. Unless the characters force her hand by invoking a higher authority, she estimates the query would take over 14 standard Terran years to process.

With a Marginal Success or better, if any of the characters ask Curator Sablik if she knows why most victims would come from one portion of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, she thinks for a moment. Then she says, ‘Oh, that’s standard hive population sedentism, isn’t it?’ She goes on to explain that, unless recruited into the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} or @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Navis Imperialis}, most born within Voll’s hives tend to spend their entire lives in the vicinity of their birth. This behaviour is actively encouraged by the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, making many aspects of population measurement far easier. If the characters don’t make the connection themselves, she explains that, if all the victims are related to a specific set of families, it makes some sense that they would all come from one region of the hive.

If the characters ask Curator Sablik if she can locate others with the same genetic connections she’s already found, she chuckles and says, ‘Yes, but there are literally millions of them. The greater majority of which do seem to reside within the eastern Windswept Buttress. Nobody calls it that but us Curators, though.’

Rokarth Voidport Records

A hive as massive as @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} holds many secrets, few of which are easily discovered; however, there is a specific collection point where all comings and goings to the hive, along with logged records of unusual activity, are stored: the Void Buttress. The Void Buttress is Voll’s primary planetside voidport. It is utterly massive, almost a secondary spire unto itself. Its profile was built to put one in the mind of the Imperial Aquila. All legal, and quite a few illegal, imports and exports of the planet Voll pass through the Void Buttress. Portions of the Void Buttress connect to every level of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, chiefly to enable the movement of goods and passengers. The characters have likely all passed through some level of the Void Buttress at some point in their lives.

It is a matter of tradition and practical history that the Navis Imperialis controls the Void Buttress, as it does the corresponding voidport in high orbit above Voll. All citizens who wish to access the records of the Void Buttress can technically put in a request at one of its many service offices that exist on nearly every level; however, without some degree of Imperial Fleet Influence, their query is likely an exhausting endeavour just to file correctly and could take a great deal of time to get even a succinct answer, possibly years in some cases.

If the characters have sufficient Influence to expedite their query, proceed to @UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV#data-discourse]{Data Discourse}. If not, they can acquire @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#temporary-influence]{Temporary Influence}. The easiest way comes from the eminently bribable Port Ensign Novus of Void Buttress Station SW9 (use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.pXsZLEawZr8Tf8Ym]{Armsman}n stat-block to represent him). If the characters find themselves rebuffed at another service office, they are directed here with a wink by a helpful citizen who overhears their queries. 

Located in the lowest levels of the Upper Hive, Station SW9 is far from busy, and its only attendant, Ensign Novus, has little to occupy his time. The Port Ensign is a lanky, affable data clerk fond of whistling void shanties and imbibing illicitly distilled beverages. A Routine (+20) Rapport (Charm or Inquiry) Test lets a character determine that a 100 solar bribe is more than enough to secure his assistance, and an effective +2 @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#temporary-influence]{Temporary Influence} with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Navy}. A failure increases the cost of the bribe to 300 solars, though Novus is quite willing to take any useful equipment or other goods in place of hard currency.

Data Discourse

The characters doubtlessly want any information on anomalous data reported at the Void Buttress circa 5 to 6 months ago (anything unusual, odd comings and goings, weird reports, etc.) To this, the clerk notes that they want an ‘Archivium Petition Rh-49ex, with an expedited stamp, I should think’. The clerk notes that they expect the inquiry to fail, as the characters don’t have enough specific data for the cogitators.

At present, they are unfortunately correct. There are hundreds of thousands of data entries that match the open parameters of the characters query. The clerk states that if the characters can find any unusual signals, codes, or specific incidents that would’ve been logged, that would help the cogitators narrow in on the details of more useful events. 

The clerk is willing to help the characters once again after they have more information to go on. Their aid will become far more useful during @UUID[.5GjYiCc0FBtc8dhc]{Part 4: Old Records}.

The Survivor

If the characters take Captain Vern up on his offer to meet with a survivor of one of the Harbinger’s attacks, he gives them the coordinates of a Vigilite Bastion located in the upper portion of the Lower Hive and a time for the following day that roughly corresponds to an hour or so past the Second Shift. 

This particular Vigilite Bastion was once an unsanctioned bar. It eventually drew the attention of the Vigilites and was shut down, then repurposed and reinforced due to its advantageous position. Vigilites and their combative @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} charges come and go, with few sparing the characters more than a passing glance until they present themselves within the public processing chamber. A sullen Vigilite Sergeant directs traffic from behind a very long table reminiscent of the bar it once was. If the characters mention Captain Vern or they’re here to see the survivor, recognition flits across the Sergeant’s scowl. He jerks a nod towards a corridor and directs the group back to a series of interrogation chambers deep in the interior of the building. 

A Vigilite named Kairn greets the characters outside the interrogation chambers and tells them that Citizen Sorvic is officially no longer under suspicion. She also notes that she passed her confessional assessment by the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} and is to be released, despite Kairn's protests, having been found among the bodies of a half dozen dead gangers.

Marta Sorvic

Marta Sorvic sits beneath a harsh light at a heavily pocked and scarred metal table. She wears the simple yellow-white fatigues of a detainee, and her skin is reddened, almost raw. An Easy (+40) Lore (Voll) Test reveals this is a sign of having undergone recent decontamination protocols, standard practice for those detained for questioning by the Vigilites. Use the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial Citizen} stat-block to represent her.

If Sorvic ever possessed any spark of defiance towards Imperial authority, it has all but been snuffed out. The characters may approach Marta Sorvic in several ways. She is reticent to talk, but a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Charm or Inquiry) Test can convince her to open up. Alternatively, the characters may attempt to intimidate her into speaking by making a Difficult (−10) Presence (Intimidation) Test or displaying some effigy of high authority. Sorvic answers their questions if the latter path is chosen, but is left a sobbing wreck by this approach.

If either Test fails, it takes several hours to extract the information from Sorvic, if the characters have the patience for it. In either case, Sorvic eventually recalls to them what she saw. 

Sorvic admits that she is a recent arrival to the area, having come up from the southern sectors of the hive in search of better opportunities. So far, this has not worked out well for her. Sorvic explains that she was a tag-along to a gang meeting, one called to discuss matters of tribute and territory. Everything was going well until ‘that thing’ attacked the assembled gangers. Sovic states that the Harbinger didn’t have a pale face, as some have claimed. Instead, it wore a pale mask, the details of which she could barely see, as the habway where the meeting took place was intentionally drowned in darkness. However, she clearly remembers its eyes, which glowed ‘red, like a terrible fire, but they turned an acid blue when they fell on me’.

If asked about gathered @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}, Sorvic is reticent to give too much detail. She explains that the gang was small, mostly made up of locals from a single family, the Zovols, and far from influential. If pressed for details, she admits to various small-time illegal activities in which she was tangentially involved — this is useless to the investigation, but does lead to Vigilite Kairn sweeping into the interrogation room once the characters have finished. The additional ‘confessions’ extracted from Sovic are sufficient to rescind the results of her previous confessional assessment, and the unfortunate woman is dragged away in manacles.

Attempting to investigate the Zovols leads to a literal dead end, as the minor gang has been totally wiped out. Beyond the information above, Sorvic has nothing else left to give.

The Vertexis

The characters may wish to investigate the Vertexis more, especially since the Vigilites all but dismiss them as an irrelevant cult. Allow each character involved to make a Test, and ensure each receives a different snippet of information. Asking after the group in drinking establishments, hive markets, and worship gatherings requires a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Inquiry) Test with these results:

  • Astounding Success (+5 SL or more): The characters have a chance meeting with a Sister Hospitaller of the Order of Searing Purity. She notes that she knows little of the Vertexis. Still, on the several occasions that she has had dealings with them, each time, they acted utterly awestruck by members of the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}, prostrating themselves and refusing to even look directly at priests.

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 to +4 SL): The characters meet a ganger who claims to have witnessed the Vertexis attack and kill a guild-bonded bounty hunter. He states that they tried to keep to the shadows before the attack, then hurled firebombs while opportunistically shooting. The group gains 1 Superiority in combat against the Vertexis, during the upcoming ambush in @UUID[.d03FcrEvHxHGZlE9]{Part 3: Ragged Faith}.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): The characters find a few citizens willing to discuss the Vertexis. Some think they’re harmless, just broken. A few think they are far more dangerous than they appear, but fortunately, not very well organised. The characters are directed to a newly painted mural, which frequently appears not long after a Harbinger attack. It depicts a shadowy figure with alabaster white skin, glaring red eyes, and wielding a harvest-thresher style blade above a caption which reads ‘His jugement is neer.’ 

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): The characters hear nothing as the citizens they meet are too fearful of the Harbinger and his disciples. Many tell them it is better not to talk about them, and so draw their attention.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The characters hear nothing as the citizens of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} have grown too fearful of the Harbinger and his disciples. Worse, the Vertexis learn that the characters have connections to the Vigilites and are asking after them. During the ambush in the following @UUID[.d03FcrEvHxHGZlE9]{Part 3: Ragged Faith}, a number of extra Vertexis equal to the number of characters attack them on the street alongside the Harbinger instead of waiting in the shadows to watch their angel finish the characters off.

The Shattered Hab

After the characters have explored several leads, when they are tired at the end of a working cycle and what approximates late evening in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, Captain Vern sends them a short message — whether via vox or a courier, depending on the circumstances and where they are staying — requesting that they join him to inspect the aftermath of a Harbinger massacre.

As they still have priority access to the Maglev Nexus, it only takes about twenty minutes for the group to descend into the Lower Hive. Still, it is over an hour’s travel through long halls filled with teeming crowds of workers before they reach their destination. The cramped tunnels are lit by heavily flickering lumens, throwing harsh shadows. A hive rain slowly drifts down, smelling of rotten mud, and it burns the nostrils of those unprotected by respirators or filtration plugs.

New Massacre

The hab level they seek is one amid reclamation from damage incurred during a hive-quake several years ago, known locally as the Heap. Due to the collapse of a macro-support column, a portion of the levels above collapsed almost entirely into this one, and the merged debris of the two has become a twisted warren of tunnels, chambers, ruined machinery and partially crushed equipment.

Reclamation has been slow, but this hasn’t stopped former inhabitants and less scrupulous looters from trying to recover some of the valuables left inside. Within the crushed ceramite and plasteel of the Heap, a quiet, forgotten war is fought in cramped tunnels and half-excavated chambers over the paltry valuables left behind in the collapse. Locals are used to the occasional muffled gunshot or distant explosion that can be heard within, and know to watch for further collapses should the violence get out of hand. 

Today, however, is unusually quiet. Captain Vern waits by a collection of construction and mining equipment, a squat burning Lho-stick in his hand. Two @UUID[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Vigilites} flank one of the larger entrances to the Heap. A successful Routine (+20) Intuition (People) Test indicates that all three are deeply rattled. Vern nods to the characters, then shakes his head and wipes a hand over his face.

‘Reclaimators will be here in another hour. I ordered it left undisturbed for you to see.’

If the characters have questions about the Heap, Vern explains in detail, glad for the distraction from the more immediate topic at hand. He finds any excuse not to accompany the characters immediately inside, as do the other Vigilites. 

Several large chambers have been the site of recent reclamation work and an even more recent slaughter. Every surface is covered in blood, pieces of mutilated bodies scattered across the interior. The primary chamber is brightly lit by lumens and tripod-mounted Stablights that the Vigilites have set up. They make the gore coating the walls and lining the ceiling in long sprayed arcs all too visible. Several nearby chambers are in a similar state, and those who venture deeper into the Heap finds lone victims scattered here and there in similar states.

Anyone who enters the Heap must make a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Composure) Test. Failure means that the Difficulty of any other Tests they take while inside is increased by one step. It is up to the Players to decide whether their characters that failed begin weeping, void the contents of their stomach, or are stricken by uncontrollable shaking.

New Clues

Captain Vern eventually enters and explains what the Vigilites have learned so far:

  • From the makeshift uniforms, scattered weapons, and some tattoos, it appears that the victims were looters, who Vern considers little better than @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} gangers.

  • There are more dead than can easily be counted, but it would appear that any looters not killed are lying low, as the Heap has been all but abandoned.

  • The locals claim to have heard and seen nothing, despite what must have been a substantial battle.

Have any character who passed the previous Discipline (Composure) Test to make a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test. Whoever achieves the most SL spots the remains of a broken @UUID[Compendium.impmal-core.items.Item.V2OgwHeEr3qpTbBy]{stummer} in an alcove. It appears Imperial in origin, but not standard. A Tech-priest can glean from its design that it originates from the Segmentum Solar. It also seems to have been crushed during a struggle.

Characters can make a Challenging (+0) Logic (Investigation) Test to search the hab (remember to increase the difficulty if they failed the Discipline (Composure) Test earlier), revealing the following:

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 or more SL): Judging by the clotting of the gore, this massacre happened approximately two days ago. Viscera and various limbs were scattered on purpose, post-mortem. There is no discernible pattern, but there is an underlying sense of controlled rage in the butchery.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): A powered sword was the primary weapon used in the killings. A few were done with a multi-bladed weapon as well, some variant of a power claw, perhaps. The victims were mainly caught unaware. Several were killed at the same time. The assailant was incredibly skilled — every blow was precise.

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): A powered blade was used, most likely a sword. The killings seem random.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The assailant used a bladed weapon and was incredibly strong — other details are lost amidst the slaughter.

Vern notes that no witnesses have come forward. The bodies were discovered during a routine search of the hab complex by Vigilite compliance teams. If shown the broken stummer, Vern smiles grimly. ‘Ah, that’s how the deviant stays so quiet.’

The party may encounter the following characters during the course of their adventure. Any other stat-blocks required to play can be found in the Imperium Maledictum Core Book, with the appropriate page number referenced in the adventure’s text.

Eversor Interitas

@Embed[Compendium.impmal-voll.actors.Actor.Tb2PzBCvBZiVSKPD description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

Wait, are they meant to fight that?

The short answer is — no. An Eversor Assassin is far beyond the capabilities of the average character. Their only hope is to take it by surprise (almost impossible), lure it into a trap (possible, likely suicidal), or deliver the shutdown code verbally (merely very risky) — ‘Unit Shutdown: Primus Sanctus Red’. Ideally, the players choose this final option, but at this point in the mission, they have seen several examples of how dangerous the Assassin truly is. If, knowing that, they still wish to confront this monstrous foe, you should allow them to do so. That is what Fate Points are for, after all.

The Harbinger
